# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 0.350.1
- **The credential gate's memory follows the size of what it reads, not the number of escapes in it** (swarm friction T32, issue 3611). With the server's accelerator, each `%XX` or `\uXXXX` escape cost ~300 bytes in the scan (a regex match and its slice of the decoded view, kept for the whole text) and as much again in the key-name tier (a match and a span per escape, regex backtracking state per escape of a `%XX` run, a new string per decoded character): a gzip of 4 MiB of `%41` held 451 MiB. The key-name tier now walks escape neighbourhoods one at a time and decodes runs in bounded pieces (`redaction._neighbourhoods`, `_unquote`, `_decode_escapes`: 39 -> 0.9 MiB on 900 KB of `%41`); a view with more than one escape per 64 characters is scanned without the accelerator, in the scanner's own 64K windows (`redaction.scan_accelerator`; per 4 MiB, CJK JSON at one escape per 6 characters: 266 MiB and 1.3 s accelerated, 5 MiB and 1.5 s windowed; sparser text keeps the accelerator); a JSON document too big to parse into objects (a `MemoryError`) is read by the key-name tier's text passes instead of failing the inspection; bytes no decode reads as text are read through their ASCII-preserving view in overlapping 4 MiB windows (`secret_gate._opaque_windows`; a credential across a seam is still read whole); a container's decoded views are released before its members are expanded; and views nobody reads (a second copy of valid UTF-8, an unusable cp1252 decode) are no longer built. Same answers on the Hyperscan parity corpus (server) and the reference-accelerator corpus (agent); what changes is at window seams, as in the scanner's own windows: a few characters less context at a seam, and a JSON file over 4 MiB that is not valid UTF-8 gets the key-name tier's text passes instead of its document walk. On a researcher's machine the full inspection runs only under `PROBE_ARTIFACT_OPAQUE_POLICY=block` and for output capture. The scanner itself (`tap_core/secrets.py`, vendored into the tap plugin) is untouched.
- **The page contract says a page comparing 4 or more runs on one key must draw them** (the server's `no_chart`).

## 0.350.0

- **The Probe daemon's commonest reads start no process** (swarm friction T22, R38): `run get`, `run check`, `notes find`, `outbox status`, `run reproduce` (without `--export`/`--materialize`), `project get` and `experiment get` -- 86% of the reads daemons spawned on one box -- are answered inside the daemon host by the CLI command's own body (`probe.cli.reads`), with the session's key, URL and session passed as arguments: the command's own stdout, stderr and exit code, byte for byte, in about 2 ms instead of about 1 s and 1 s of CPU and an 88 MB process each. They keep the command's timeout, the lease watch and the retries. `run check --verify` (it runs git), an outbox of more than 2,000 queued ops, a run with 8 reads in flight and an unexpected error still go to the CLI, as does every other read; each read is counted by where it ran (`probe_reads` in the session's store, and a log line naming a spawned one). Writes are unchanged. `snapshot.commit_on_remote` no longer passes a recorded remote that reads as an option to git.
- **A run's `finish()` gets the outbox in seconds, whatever the worker is sending** (swarm friction T23, issue 3618). One drain pass held the outbox's drain lock from its scan to its status write, so a close waited behind every upload and write of that pass: ~400 s per run behind the swarm's 10k queued ops, against `finish()`'s 600 s cap. A pass now lets go of the lock while one of its uploads is on the network, holding only that run's own lock (`<outbox>/.run-locks/`) so no other drain sends that run meanwhile; between two ops it gives the lock to a close that says it is waiting (`<outbox>/.drain.want`), and once it has held the lock 3 s it lets go for 0.1 s, so an older release's `finish()`, which only polls, gets in too. After letting go a pass reads each op on disk before acting on it, so nothing goes twice, and each run's ops keep their order. Measured with fake servers: three closes behind a 30 MiB upload that never ends returned in 0.02-0.05 s each (15 s, their whole deadline, before); a close behind a 20 s pass of 10,000 writes returned in 0.75 s (it waited out the pass before). A close lets go only for its own uploads and for other closes, and takes the lock back within its deadline or ends its pass there (its upload stays queued), so `finish()` keeps its 600 s guarantee; no metric points are batched in memory. An older release's own drain does not know the run locks: while a pass of this release is away for an upload, an older `finish()` of that same run, or an older `probe outbox drain`, may send that upload a second time (the server keeps one row per name and content); a write `probe outbox discard` sets aside meanwhile stays set aside.
- **A write a newer attempt of its run superseded is set aside, not dead-lettered** (swarm friction T24, issue 3629). The server refuses it every time (its `write_epoch` is past, and a run's epoch only grows), so the drain moves it to the outbox's `discarded/` (kept for the record, never sent) instead of `failed/`, where it nagged every session start and `probe outbox retry` could never land it. Told by the server's `code: stale_write_epoch`, or on a server without it by the epochs its message names. `probe doctor --fix` also sets aside the dead letters already there that can never land: a superseded attempt's, and a write whose run the server says does not exist, asked again with the write's own credential (only the server's own "run not found"; anything it cannot tell, a run in the trash included, stays for `probe outbox retry`).
- **`probe session delete <id>` and `probe session undelete <id>`** (swarm friction T25, research-os 0411). Delete one of your own captured sessions: it is hidden from search at once and deleted for good after 7 days (its transcript, and what Probe derived from it), and `undelete` brings it back until then. `delete` shows the session and asks for the id's first 8 characters typed back; run on a session already asked for, it prints where that deletion stands. Both are refused (exit 2, no request) inside a coding agent's shell or when the Probe daemon runs them, and the assistant never runs them. SDK: `Client.delete_session(id, dry_run=)`, `undelete_session`, `session_deletion`.

## 0.349.0

- **Late writes say when their work happened**, so Probe's agent-hours count it then (swarm friction T11): the outbox drain sends each queued op's queue time and the Probe daemon the oldest event of the work it files (`X-Probe-Event-At`, only beside an agent session; a spawned outbox worker never inherits a daemon command's `PROBE_EVENT_AT`). A queued write now also records the agent session that queued it and is sent as that session: one outbox worker drains every session's backlog on a machine, and sent its own session for all of them; a write an older SDK queued is sent as before. The branches view shows `agent_wall_h` (parallel agents once) beside `agent_h`, a compact row's two busiest sessions (`sessions_top`, e.g. `"codex 2.9h · pi 2.1h"`), and in a branch's detail each experiment's split by session.
- **The MCP lineage view of a project or experiment fits its budget, names both ends and pages every link** (swarm friction P6). Its links were up to 20 full server edges plus 20 run edges in front of the children, so on the swarm's sweep (`entity experiment:decay-fraction-surface view=lineage token_budget=8000`) the answer went out as a 23,593-byte `json_fragment`, and links past 20 were unreachable. Links are now split into `built_on` (what it builds on, replaces or drew on) and `used_by` (what builds on or replaced it), plus an experiment's `run_edges`; each link names its far end (`ref: "experiment:<slug>"`, `name`; a paper as `paper_id`, since `entity` reads no paper) and keeps its `relation`, `provenance`, `derived` (with `runs`, `files`), `reason` (200 characters on the first page, whole when paged), `at` and a stored link's `edge_id` (run edges too, for `probe edge remove`). The first page shows at most 10 of each, fewer when they would take more than half the budget, with each list's `total` and a `read_more` (`links_beyond_page`); `view_options.links: built_on | used_by | run_edges` pages that whole list as rows (`read_more` spells the whole call, without the page's cursor). Rows are fitted exactly, leaving room for a multi-ref batch's wrapper, so a page is whole JSON rather than a text fragment. New `entity project:<P> view=picks`: the best pick's history, newest first (each event's `id`, what was picked or cleared, why, who, when; `gone` when the pick left the tree; at most 50, `picks_beyond_server_limit` at the cap; issue 3624), paged after the last event id so a pick made mid-walk repeats no row; the daemon reader does not see picks of its own session's experiments. `browse mode=branches` carries the workspace pick's history as `pick_history` on its first page (at most a third of the budget, and only the room the branch rows leave when they all fit one page; when cut, `pick_history_total` and `pick_history_beyond_page`; never at the cost of the page's one branch row). Needs the server's lineage `ends` for names; an older server reads as typed ids.
- **A file change is one line for both daemons, and the folder check stops walking package trees and folders the agent only read in** (swarm friction T17-T21). The reader and the writer (its index lane and an opened turn included) now see a file change as what happened, the path and the sizes, `· looks like results` when its text looks like results (a JSON `"val_acc": 0.93` now counts), and how many lines `session op=open event_id=<id>` shows; only that open shows the content. The folder check skips a folder holding `CACHEDIR.TAG` or a `*.dist-info` child (a `pip install --target`, a uv cache), and a folder the agent only `cd`'d into to read (`cd ~/repo && git log | head`) is no longer a working folder. A file that changes at check after check (a log, a status file) is one `growing` line, then one `changed` line whose open shows the whole change, once it has been quiet for two checks or the session ends. New-file bursts are listed in the index lane too, whose calls now take about 8K tokens each, at most 2 at once. A run start or end wakes the writer within 60 s (past its 300 s least gap, at most one extra run a minute) and leads that run's message; another agent's message wakes the reader as a prompt does, at most once a minute. Writer conversations compact one bite (40K tokens) before their size, counting tokens as the model route does (o200k_base; 4 characters a token read a bite 12-28K tokens low, and the route refused 3 writer requests on 10-28), and track-work's `reference.md` is in the writer's instructions, so saved writer conversations start fresh once after the update. Replayed on the swarm orchestrator's daemon store (16,209 events): file-change text 10.1M -> 0.66M characters (-93%), all event text 11.5M -> 2.0M (-83%).

## 0.348.0

- **A plugin change no longer leaves Codex unrecorded until the next update.** Codex rebuilds its copies of Probe's plugins from the marketplace, and every rewrite (a new version or the same one written again) left all of Probe's hooks in them unapproved, so new Codex sessions recorded nothing until an update approved them again, which a live run defers for up to a day (issue 3617: 15 farm jobs on one box). The Probe service now looks at those copies every minute (the bytecode Probe's own hooks write there aside) and, when they change, approves Probe's own hooks in Codex as an update does (a `probe.core.run codex_trust` child, given the login shell's PATH and CODEX_HOME so an nvm or Homebrew `codex` is found; never beside an update, an action, a desktop change or a `probe wizard` run from a terminal), asking again with backoff (1 minute, growing to every 15) until Codex trusts them, at most 8 times an hour; `service.status` shows it as `codex_trust`. With automatic updates turned off it approves nothing, as no update does. It works while the service runs (a live Probe session or the desktop app keeps it up), and sessions that start before the heal (the one whose start rewrote the copies, and any in the minute after) stay unrecorded, since Codex reads approvals when a session starts. `probe doctor --fix` approves them on demand (the daemon's own worker may not run it), a deferred update approves them too, and `probe status` and `probe doctor` name `probe doctor --fix` when Probe's hooks wait in Codex.
- **`probe ask --writer` keeps a request's line breaks and indentation**, so a handover reaches the writer as the lists, paragraphs and code it was written in (each line's trailing space, the blank lines at either end and the indentation every line shares dropped, a run of blank lines kept as one: one rule, `mailbox.request_text`, in the CLI and the worker). A plain `probe ask` is still one line. A worker from before this release still flattens a request to one line.
- **`probe experiment set E --dead-end "<why>"` marks an experiment a dead end; `--clear-dead-end` clears it** (`Client.update_experiment(dead_end=..., clear_dead_end=True)`). Its branch reads `dead_end` until a run of it is live, and it still ranks; an agent's mark never replaces a person's. The MCP branches view names each branch's `line` of work (lines split only at a tree's root, or between trees) and the runner-up's; `no_other_line: true` says why there is no runner-up, and `line_dead_end: true` flags a line whose work has ended in dead ends everywhere. The MCP experiment card says `dead_end: "<why>"`. The daemon writer is told when to mark one, and its logbook says `dead end marked` / `dead end cleared`.
- **A training run no longer deletes the Probe daemon's mailbox** (issue 3616). Dead-run recovery in `probe.init()` took every folder under `~/.local/state/probe/reads` for a dead run's and deleted it once unchanged for 10 minutes: the daemon's `asks`, `requests`, `messages` and `hints` folders, open `probe ask --writer` requests and the worker's marker with them, after which `probe ask --writer` was refused. Recovery now touches only folders holding a run's own files (`owner.json`, a late-hash file, a `<host>.<pid>` spool, live marker, sidecar or close marker). For SDKs that are never updated (a pinned training venv), each mailbox folder now holds an empty `probe-mailbox.jsonl`, which every SDK's recovery has always left alone, so they pass the folders by whether or not a daemon is running; the daemon worker and `probe ask` write it, and the worker writes its marker again whenever it is gone. A machine where no daemon or `probe ask` from this release has run yet has no such file.
- **`probe ask` says what is actually wrong** (issue 3621). A session whose Probe hooks never ran (Codex hooks waiting for approval) was told the daemon does not run on the machine and to use the Probe MCP; it now hears that the hooks have not run and that `probe doctor` names the cause. `--writer` refused for a live worker with no marker now says to try again in a minute, instead of claiming the daemon is older than the CLI.
- **`Client.run(project=<project id>)` opens the run in that project** (issue 3623). It was refused as "no project with slug", and with `question=` could create a new project slugged by the id. A bare uuid (the 36-character form) now names the project it is the slug or the id of; one that is both, of two projects, is refused with the spelling for each: `id:<uuid>` is only ever the id, `slug:<uuid>` only ever the slug. An id is never created as a project, an experiment's id is refused with its slug, and an offline run's `probe sync` follows the same rule.
- **The SDK's outbox worker stays 30 s with its queue empty before it exits** (issue 3625), looking for new ops every 0.5 s. A training loop queueing an op every second or two restarted a worker after each one (38 starts, 37.5 CPU-s in 155 s); the same worker now sends them. Its `outbox.drained` report comes once per stay, about 30 s later than before.
- **pi's footer stops saying "not capturing" once the Probe service claims the session** (issue 3619). The footer read capture once, right after the start, while the recorder had not claimed the session yet (it does about 2 s later); it now reads again 3 s, 15 s and 60 s after the start while the claim is still pending. A footer read that comes back after pi switched sessions is no longer applied to the new session.

## 0.347.1

- **The lifeboat no longer "rescues" a machine whose last update check was minutes before a release.** When a release came out less than 15 minutes after the service's last check, the lifeboat's ask for a check was answered "checked recently", no update ran, the idle service exited, and 5 minutes later the lifeboat read that silence as a service that cannot start: it installed the release itself and posted a "Lifeboat rescued" alert for a routine update. The lifeboat's ask (`update.check_now` trigger `keeper`) now always starts an update cycle; other asks keep the 15-minute cooldown.
- **`probe summary push` marks its push as the whole page (`whole_page`), the one the server judges `no_chart`; the page contract says a page over logged curves must draw one.** `overview-contract` names the server's new `no_chart` refusal: no declared series and no `<canvas>` or `<svg>` while the entity's runs logged curves.

## 0.347.0

- **`probe ask --writer` takes requests up to 16,000 characters** (was 4,000), enough for a phase handover or a branch's conclusion. The worker's marker now names the longest request it takes whole (`request_chars`); a request longer than a running older worker would keep is refused with that worker's limit instead of being cut.

## 0.346.1

- **A project's Summary page weighs its parts by the work in them, not by which came last.** The page skills told a writer to rewrite the top around the newest result, so a project that is mostly supervised fine-tuning read as all RL once an RL experiment ran (Willow: 8 of 90 experiment runs are RL, the page led with RL). `write-summary` and `overview-page` now say a project's top is what the project has produced and where each main line of work stands, each part given room by its runs and weeks.

## 0.346.0

- **`probe summary push` refuses a page Probe's credential scrubber would rewrite, instead of storing it broken.** A figure's code naming a variable like `passSig = [false, ...]` was rewritten to `passSig=<redacted>, ...` on the way, the chart threw, and push still said pushed; push now writes nothing and names the text near the change, as `summary edit` already did. The page skills now say how to load a font (`<link>`, `@import` is refused), that counts stay exact, the chart caps and `PROBE.lineChart` options, where a project's experiments and a whole conclusion are read, and that a table never stands in for a chart. `evals/companion/render.py` no longer counts an icon-sized svg (a legend swatch) as a blank visual. pi's guard allows `probe session owed` under the daemon profile, as the other harnesses' guard has since 0.345.0 (its end-of-turn check was refused there).

## 0.345.1

- **A Hub dataset read from a `refs/convert/parquet` or `refs/pr/N` revision records that revision, not `refs`.** The SDK's dataset capture (`integrations/_hub.py`) now reads those revisions whole and url-decoded, as the server keys the same uri, so one dataset is not registered as two sources.

- **A setting changed while Probe updates itself is saved, not refused.** The desktop app's launch starts an update cycle, and while its CLI and plugin step ran the service refused every `action.run` as `busy`, so a change made right after opening the app (the new-session default, who records, automatic updates, the workspace limit) failed with "wasn't saved. Try again." for a minute or more. Now an action asked for while an update holds the one mutating slot (a cycle's CLI step, or a person's Update) is journaled and answered `{action_id, queued: true}` (`action.status` says `queued`), and the queue runs in the order it was asked for once the update lets go, one at a time. A restart onto a newly installed CLI waits for the queue, and so do the idle exit and `service.stop`; `service.status.actions` lists the queued ids. A `probe wizard --yes` routed there says it waits for the update. Still `busy`: an Update asked for while an update holds the slot, an action behind another action when none is waiting, and an action past 16 waiting. A queued action whose service was stopped by a signal reads as stopped with it, never as run.

## 0.345.0
- **Inline and the daemon use notes the same way.** An inline agent (`/probe inline`) gets track-work, write-summary and edit-notes whole, the text the daemon's writer reads, in parts that fit a hook (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi) or whole (pi). The first write a session makes to a project, experiment or run prints the opening of its note and its Open / Don't repeat lines (nothing when it has none), in both modes. The CLI keeps one owed ledger per session (`probe.cli.owed`): a summary for a project or experiment it created or concluded, and, new, a note on a run it tagged `invalid`. The daemon's writer is sent back from it as before (and once for the note); an inline agent is sent back at the end of a turn that completed by a new Stop route (`owed_hook.py`, never inside a subagent) and pi's `agent_before_settle` (never after Esc or a provider error), through the hidden `probe session owed --send-back`, at most twice per item; a turn that owes nothing, or only what was already asked twice, starts no CLI. Taking the `invalid` tag off settles the note. The CLI's own pre-send note refusal says how far over the cap the text is, in the unit it is over.

## 0.344.0
- **The daemon writes Summary pages as custom Claude artifacts.** `write-summary` now asks for an ELI10 TL;DR on top (one sentence, up to 3 bullets), a diagram wherever it makes a comparison or a pipeline clearer and a chart wherever a run logged a curve or runs can be compared, a rewrite of the top on each update instead of another paragraph, and a project page that sums up its parts. `overview-page` names the treatment (a research memo) and the order the page skills win in; `overview-contract` and `overview-charts` teach the page's own code inside its `<figure>`, pinned libraries, `PROBE.series('<id>')` for logged curves and charts drawn from run results; `artifact-design` is checked against today's Claude Code skill and fitted to the light, untitled Summary pane. The daemon puts the five page skills whole into the writer's conversation once, so even a new experiment's first page is written with them (it read `artifact-design` in 2 of 53 sessions that pushed a page when they were a read away). Libraries are Chart.js, d3 and echarts, which draw under the frame's CSP without `eval`. `evals/companion/render.py` renders pages in the dashboard's real frame and counts what drew.

## 0.343.1

- A run's queued uploads upload faster (prod, 60 x 5 KB on one run: 1.34 files/s on 0.343.0, 3.67 now). Every upload at the head of a run's queue enters the parallel window, including those queued behind the run's first writes, which 0.343.0 sent one by one; the window's many-file presigns go 8 files a request, 4 requests in flight. Run uploads ask for links straight to object storage (`X-Probe-Direct-Upload: 1`) where the server grants them; a machine that cannot reach the storage host (DNS, TLS, connect, or a refusal there) sends those files through the API's relay and stops asking for the rest of the process. `PROBE_UPLOAD_MANY=0` sends each file on its own worker instead of through the many-file routes.

## 0.343.0

- Queued uploads of a run go up together: the outbox sends the uploads at the head of each run's queue (up to 32 at a time, 8 bodies in flight, `PROBE_UPLOAD_WORKERS` to change it) with one presign and one confirm request per 16 files instead of one of each per file (presigned links are short-lived, so a request presigns only what is sent right after it). A presigned PUT the store refuses (an expired link) is presigned once more before it fails. The window asks for links straight to object storage (`X-Probe-Direct-Upload: 1`) where the server grants them; a machine that cannot reach the storage host (or is refused there) sends those files through the API's relay instead, and stops asking for the rest of the process. Order is kept where it means something: an upload never goes ahead of an earlier write of its run other than a metric point, two versions of a file land in the order they were queued, and the run's close still waits. A server without the many-file routes gets the same files one request each, in parallel.

## 0.342.8

- Refresh the bundled command index after the desktop workspace-save fix, so the daemon can use it immediately without rebuilding it on first use. The release gate now checks its source fingerprint.

## 0.342.7

- Wait up to one minute for an ongoing setup or update before saving or creating the desktop app's default workspace. Recheck the account after waiting and save once; a setup that stays busy still leaves the choice unchanged.

- **Reverted the compute router's client changes** (#3579, #3596, #3598, #3600, #3605, #3606): the shared upload classifier released in 0.342.4 is withdrawn, the per-file upload caps (`AUTO_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, the 64 MB pointer rule, `artifact_auto_multipart`) are back as before, and the hidden `probe job` commands are gone. The feature is shelved (2026-10-29).

## 0.342.6

- Fix saving daemon reasoning summaries with empty Claude Code settings and single-quoted Codex setting keys. Verify the requested value for every configured agent and name any agent whose save failed.

## 0.342.5

- **Making a project part of a bigger one updates the bigger one's page too.** write-summary (and its plugin and pi copies) adds: "Creating or linking a project `--part-of` another changes that one too: update its page so it names the new part." Before, the writer wrote the new part's page and left the umbrella's as it was (bench, a phase-2 session under an existing umbrella: 2 of 2 runs).
- **The bench's fake Probe serves a browse project's `part_of`** (evals only; nothing ships). Its browse nodes carried the old tree's `parent_project_id` and `subproject_count` but no `part_of`, so a benched writer saw `part_of: null` where the server serves the projects it is part of, oldest link first. A part listed under a `project:` scope now reads that project as its `parent_project_id`, as the server's `?parent_id=` does.


## 0.342.4

- **One upload classifier for every path, by what a folder IS, not only its name** (`probe.sdk.junk`). The code snapshot (with and without git), run-output capture, the folder import, the daemon's precheck and the new `probe artifact add <folder>` share it, replacing two hand-synced name lists (the daemon had none). A folder a tool rebuilds is skipped by its marker: a venv under any name (`pyvenv.cfg`), a conda env (`conda-meta/`), a tagged cache (`CACHEDIR.TAG`: cargo's `target/`), a tool cache whose `.gitignore` is `*` under pytest's, ruff's, mypy's or virtualenv's own comment, a linked git worktree whose main checkout is inside the same upload (`.claude/worktrees/x`; one whose main checkout is elsewhere, a submodule and a bare repo's are kept), `*.dist-info` / `*.egg-info` and `site-packages`, a Hugging Face hub repo folder (`models--*` with `snapshots/`; its parent only when it holds nothing else), W&B's `wandb/` folder and synced run folders (an offline run, the only copy until `wandb sync`, is kept). A wheel uploads only when a lockfile or requirements file at the root names it or its `--find-links` folder. An untagged `target/` and a folder named `env` are data again (`env` left the name list; a real venv there has its `pyvenv.cfg`). Inside a repo a marker judges tracked files too; a generated name only untracked ones. Every skip is a `skipped` record with its `marker`, and every upload says what it skipped and which folders sent the most bytes (`probe snapshot`, the folder import's plan, `artifact add <folder>` on stderr, a warning from the SDK when a marker gave a folder away). No size-based stop anywhere.
  - `probe artifact add [RUN] <folder>` uploads each file the classifier keeps, as `<folder name>/<path>` (`--name` sets the prefix; `--kind`, `--step`, `--span`, `--meta` go on every file), queued like `--from-manifest`. It honours `.probe.config` silently and never takes a credential store (`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.kube`, `.config`, ...) or Probe's own config and state. A single named file still uploads as before. The daemon cannot send a folder: that precheck block now has no override.
  - `probe snapshot RUN` adds the files the run READ (the read recorder) that git ignores inside the folder, like an `include=`, within the snapshot's upload budget; a read past it (or big enough to be recorded by reference) is left out as `read_over_budget`, never a failure. Reads outside the folder are listed, not captured. `Run.snapshot(used=...)` and `capture_manifest(used=...)` take the list; `junk.used_inputs` sorts `probe run inputs` rows into inside, outside and junk.
  - The folder import's walk rules move to 2: its census lists `skipped_generated` (path, marker), coverage calls a file an older import saw there `skipped`, not vanished, and a queued import from an older CLI re-walks by its own rules.
  - The daemon's precheck refuses a file inside such a folder (check `junk`, overridable) after its credential scan, judged only below the folder the file shares with the session's; it never judges worktrees, so a session in a worktree still sends its files.
  - Output capture looks a folder's markers up before listing it, so judging a flat folder of millions of files never reads it whole.
  - For the compute job's start-up step: `junk.cache_env()` names the cache variables to point outside the working folder (`HF_HOME`, `TORCH_HOME`, `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `PIP_CACHE_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `WANDB_DIR`), and `junk.write_restored()` records the files it restored (path + sha256) under `PROBE_RESTORED_FILES`, so output capture never re-uploads one whose bytes come back unchanged.
- **A good update is no longer undone because `runtime.json` lagged the switch.** After a side-by-side update, the service read the installed version through `runtime.json`'s interpreter; when that file still named the env the switch replaced, the restart started the old version and its guard, watching for the old version from the new env, switched a good update back and marked the version still running as rejected (10-28, probe demo: 0.339.0 → 0.342.0 undone, the machine held on 0.339.0 for 24 h). Before it restarts, the service now points `runtime.json` at the env the tool path names and expects that env's version (`updater.runtime_follows_switch`); when it cannot (that version unreadable, Probe being uninstalled) it does not restart this time.
- **`capture_stalled` no longer fires when a session idle for hours is used again.** Waiting lines were aged from the last receipt, so a session idle 11 h read as stalled 11 h minutes after its next prompt (10-28, New Workspace); so did one resumed after hours closed. They are now aged from when the service first saw them waiting, and a receipt read that failed forgets nothing. A stall already running when a service starts is reported an hour after it first sees it. The report's facts add `waiting_h`.

## 0.342.3

- **`probe project delete --recursive` says what it does: nothing.** Projects are flat, so the flag is accepted and changes nothing; its help and confirmation prompt say the projects linked to the project stay, instead of warning that filed projects go with it.
- **Project cards (MCP) name parts as parts**: no `parent_project_id` (one projected link of the many the card's `part_of` names) and the count of its parts as `part_count`, not `subproject_count`. `probe project contributors` and the SDK's contributor help no longer describe credit through another project (every credit is the project's own).

## 0.342.2

- **A `probe` word after a `$(...)` argument is no longer read as the Probe CLI.** The plugin's shell guard (and pi's port of it) ended a command at the `)` of every substitution, so in `harness --out $(mktemp -d) probe PATH` the words `probe PATH` looked like their own command and the Bash call could be refused. A `$(...)`, `<(...)` or `>(...)` among a command's arguments now resumes that command at its `)`; one in the program's place (`$(which probe) run start`, `X=$(...) probe ...`), one where a wrapper's command goes or among the arguments of a program that runs them as a command (`nohup $(...) probe ...`, `eval`, `sudo`, `xargs`, `uv run`, a shell), a line with a `case` statement or a backtick, and a `probe` command inside a substitution are read as before. The guard also now finds `probe` behind a shell keyword or a leading `2>&1` or a `{fd}` descriptor (`if ...; then probe notes create x; fi`, `{ probe ...; }`), which it missed before.

## 0.342.1

- **A folder import's agents no longer write Claude Code memories into your `~/.claude`.** Claude Code's auto memory let an import's own classifier, notes and record sessions save notes about your folder under `~/.claude/projects/<import work dir>/memory/`. Every Claude the import launches now runs with `autoMemoryEnabled: false` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` (checked live on Claude Code 2.1.296: with either one, the session's prompt carries no memory directory; with neither, it does).

## 0.342.0

- **Projects are flat: a phase of a bigger effort is its own project linked `--part-of` it, not a subproject.** `probe project create SLUG --kind K --part-of P` (repeatable) sends `part_of` links and, without `--workspace`, lets the server file the project beside its first target; `probe project list --part-of P` lists P's parts in every workspace; `probe project reference add A --to B --part-of` links an existing project (a plain add still records a reference). The old spellings keep working, hidden: `create --parent` and `list --parent` send `part_of`, `move --parent` / `--top-level` send what they always sent, and `delete --recursive` is kept: a `part_of` link never takes a project with it, but the flag still deletes the projects filed under it before part_of links, and its prompt says so. The SDK takes `create_project(part_of=[...])`, `list_projects(part_of=...)` (refusing a backend that ignores the filter) and `add_project_reference(..., relation="part_of")`; `parent_project_id` still works. The MCP project card names what a project is `part_of` and its `parts` (names and ids, from the detail's `part_of_links`), and `browse` says parts, not subprojects. The always-loaded block (v52), track-work and its copies teach the link instead of nesting, and overview-page tells a recorder to cover a bigger effort's parts. The bench's fake Probe serves `part_of` links and an older client's `parent_project_id` as the server does (the target of a project's oldest `part_of` link, null in a loop; a PATCH moves that link), and its duplicate rule compares a project's `part_of` set. The tap moves to 0.10.27 for the track-work line (`tap/companion_rules.md`, `tap/companion_reference.md`).

## 0.341.0

- **`probe docs "<question>"` reads Probe's own docs** (docs.prbe.ai), signed in or not, and is allowed in the daemon profile, which has no MCP (an outside source, like `paper find`). Its managed block names it in one sentence. In MCP sessions the same docs come through `search` with `search_in=["docs"]`.
- **`instrument-code`: one final number is logged once** (`probe.log({"test/acc": acc})`, a single-number tile), the rule `track-work` already had; agents had been searching for it.

## 0.340.1

- **The status line no longer says a recorded session is "not started" or "not recording".** Its capture reading was taken when a session started or was switched on with `/probe`, a moment before the Probe service registered the session or its recorder took it, and was taken again only at the session's next prompt or tool call; an idle session showed the wrong word for as long as it sat (two sessions on 2026-10-27, both recorded). The Probe service now follows each session whose status line it refreshes: when what that reading is taken from changes (the session's registration, its recorder starting, taking or letting go of the session), it refreshes that session's status line again, with no hook asking, and once more 10 s later; a refresh that fails is retried at most 3 times. It never refreshes a session Probe is off for (that refresh reads the server: Probe off makes no call for it), one whose request named `PROBE_BASE_URL`, or one that has ended, and it stops following before its recorders pause at a restart, so an update no longer writes "not started" on its way out. Claude Code also redraws an idle session's line now: where Probe's status line is the only one in the slot, it asks Claude Code to re-run it every 10 s (`statusLine.refreshInterval`, Claude Code 2.1.97), where it re-ran only on Claude Code's own events. A new install writes it; an install from before gets it once from the Probe service (when this update lands, or at a session's first status-line refresh in another `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), with `settings.json.probe-backup` kept as the installer keeps it; an interval you set or remove is left as you have it, and a slot that also runs your own status line gets none (it would re-run yours every 10 s). Sessions already open need no restart. The service's `service.status` answer gains `statusline.followed` and `statusline.followups`.

## 0.340.0

- **A folder import creates its runs unnamed and charts their results.** An import named each run after its folder, which locks the name for good: nothing could rename Tokenless's 1,032 imported runs, 1,008 of them hex attempt ids like `bre5b5b2d7-33c647-…-a1` (2026-10-26). Runs are now created without a name (the folder stays in `metadata.backfill.relative_path`) and are titled like any unnamed run; a run an older CLI named is still found by its folder and keeps its name. Each number read from a run's result files is also sent as a one-point series stamped with that file's time, so it draws a chart and a key-metric tile (0 of those 1,032 runs had one); sending it again stores nothing, and a changed result adds its new value at its new time. `backfill.summary` gains `metric_points` and `metric_points_failed`.
- **The import's classifier is given track-work's own lines on what an experiment and a run are, quoted, and the folders that look like runs.** Its own one-line rule ("a folder of one run's output is a run") made 1,008 attempt folders runs and left 47 real `runs/<name>/` folders as loose files. It now reads track-work's lines ("A sweep is an experiment, not a project.", "per-item detail -> artifact, never a metric", ...) and a list of folders holding a config or manifest beside a result or log file; which of them are runs is still its call.
- **An imported folder's experiments and runs are planned under a structure version.** Raising it re-plans every imported folder once on its next import (files are moved, never uploaded again); today's imports stay as they are. A re-import that names an experiment's folder again, under another slug, reuses that experiment instead of making a second.
- **A folder import now records its projects by your own skills, and the claims draft is gone.** After the files land, one session of your agent per project (one per group of experiments past 300 runs, then one for the project page) reads `track-work`, `write-summary` and `edit-notes` verbatim and names and describes the runs, writes notes and experiment conclusions, sets the project's headline metric from what its runs logged, and writes the project and experiment pages, published as the live writer publishes them, interactive or not. Its `probe` is a checked local stand-in: writes are staged in an op log and applied after the session (CAS on notes and pages, each op once), a field a person wrote is refused (re-read just before each run is written), documents are plain files in the work dir (never a symlink), and imports make no links. The "Imported file reconstruction" draft, its publish prompt and the AI Summary request are deleted. The import agents' lane `draft` is now `record` (Claude still on sonnet by default). Before: Tokenless's 1,032 imported runs were named after their folders, 93% shared one description, and no imported project had a page.

## 0.339.0

- **Probe staff can set this machine's default for new sessions to `off` or `read`, once, and it reaches machines that only run coding agents.** When staff ask (research-os control/074), the next `probe` command that hears `X-Probe-Settings-Requested` leaves a mark and a later one applies it (`probe/cli/remote_settings.py`), INCLUDING the commands the Probe service runs itself (the team note's sync at each session start, Stop and end), which the update-now and capture-repair requests skip: on a machine with the service those can be the only `probe` it ever runs. The default moves only where that is quieter than it is (a machine already `off` asked for `read` stays `off`), under the config lock, and records `defaults.session_state_set_by`; `probe session default` (`set_by`), `probe doctor` and the wizard's Defaults row say "set by Probe staff on <date>" until the person changes it. Every session louder than the value is switched to it, compared and written under that session's own lock (an explicit choice; a switch moved at the same moment is never made louder), and for `off` the Probe service is told at once for the newest 64. It applies once: the request is recorded before anything changes (nothing changes when it cannot be), a lost report is re-sent, never re-applied, so whatever the person turns back on afterwards stays on; a session whose switch cannot be written is retried alone on the next two windows before the report goes. A report that never landed is sent once even after staff canceled the request or it expired, so the server records what happened. "Set by Probe staff" shows only while the stored default is still staff's value and no environment variable overrides it. A setting or value outside this CLI's own list (anything that would turn recording on) is reported `unsupported` and changes nothing. `PROBE_SESSION_STATE` still wins and is reported `env_shadowed`. One stderr line only on a terminal. `settings.remote_applied` reports the setting, value and counts, never a session id. The three staff-request marks share one module (`probe/_shared/device_mark.py`). Both plugins' vendored `_session_marker.py` copies are re-synced (new helpers only; no hook behaviour changes).

## 0.338.1

- **`probe log` and `probe span add` refuse a run ref that is really a `key=value`, before anything is queued.** When the run argument is missing (`probe log $RUN loss=0.5 acc=0.9` with `$RUN` empty, which the shell drops), the first metric took the run's place; the write was queued with exit 0 and dead-lettered as a 404 minutes later (Bucket, 2026-10-27). It now exits 2 at once: `'loss=0.5' looks like key=value, not a run ref — the run argument is missing`. No run ref can hold `=`: the server refuses one in a run slug since this release.
- **`outbox.drained` says what the server answered each write it gave up on**: `dead_lettered_by_status` (e.g. `{"404": 1}`, keyed like `sdk.delivery.summary`'s) and `dead_lettered_no_such_run`, how many were the server's own 404 "run not found" rather than any other 404 (a run token's refusal, a swept upload). The delivery-loss alert reads the second to tell a write naming no run from a real loss; dead-letter records carry it as `no_such_run`.
- **Finding saved sessions and reviewing a backfill are about 4x faster in the Probe app.** Every saved transcript on the machine is checked to belong to its session before it is offered. That check read the first and last 2 MB of each transcript and parsed every line of the last 2 MB, which was 88% of the time. Finding sessions now reads a Claude Code transcript back from its end only until it reaches the last message, usually one line, and reads only the half a Codex or pi transcript needs. Uploads still get the full check. Measured on a machine with 628 sessions (8 GB): finding saved history 4.6–5.1 s → 1.1 s; reviewing 199 sessions (0.57 GB) 7.2–7.4 s → 2.2–2.4 s, which also hashes the reviewed transcripts on 4 threads. `probe backfill` and the wizard's import share both changes. Tap 0.10.26 carries the same identity-check code, reading only the half of a transcript it needs. One malformed transcript no longer stops the scan for every session: a line nested past Python's JSON depth limit (about 1,000 levels before 3.12), a non-string session id in an earlier record, or a Codex header that is not an object now counts as one unusable line or an unproven session. A file that cannot be hashed during the review is reported at once instead of after every other selected file.

## 0.338.0

- Research plan review is automatically included and routed in every agent profile. Remove its settings toggle and restore automatic routing on devices with the retired opt-out.

## 0.337.0

- **`probe uninstall` removes Probe from this computer and leaves nothing of it behind.** It is `probe wizard --action uninstall` (and the menu's Uninstall), with `--yes`, `--force`, `--offline`, `--discard-unsent`, `--backup-unsent` and `--json`. Before, an uninstall left the CLI, its `probe*` commands, the Probe service (still running), `~/.local/state/probe`, the daemon key (wiped, never revoked) and Probe's skills in `~/.claude/skills`, and skipped every coding agent whose binary was not on PATH. Now it refuses (exit 2, nothing changed) while Probe is still in use here (agent sessions it records, the daemon, training runs, another computer sharing this home) unless `--force`, and from inside a recorded session; stops every Probe process; sends what is queued (note edits included) and, if something is still unsent, asks to delete it, save it to `~/probe-unsent-<date>.tar.gz` or cancel (`--yes` stops unless `--discard-unsent` or `--backup-unsent`); retires this computer and revokes every key it holds (API, MCP, daemon, capture), saying which shared key was only disconnected; takes Probe out of every agent with a trace of it; deletes Probe's files and finally the CLI itself. Offline it changes nothing unless `--offline`. Killed anywhere, running it again finishes the job (or `python3 ~/.local/state/probe/uninstall/finisher.py --plan ~/.local/state/probe/uninstall/plan.json` once the CLI is gone), and so does any install (`npx probe-research`, the wizard's install and update, `probe repair`, `probe daemon install`) before it installs afresh, saving what was queued since to the backup file; while it runs nothing of Probe starts or updates, and `probe doctor` and `probe status` say so on their first line. With `--json`, the final `result` says why a run stopped as data (`reason`: unsent research, live users, inside a session, offline, busy, partly done).
- **The lifeboat now rescues a broken install even when it is on the latest release (hand-off v3).** It used to act only on a machine behind the newest release, so a CLI env that was deleted, lost its Python or no longer imported while at the latest stayed broken for good (stage 1 answered `current`, or `unknown_active` when the version could not be read). Now a keeper run whose service is still silent 5 minutes after an ask checks that the active env imports what its release has (a release older than 0.328.0 is not asked for `probe.core.adopt`, which came later). When the env is really broken (not a timeout or a kill), the lifeboat reinstalls the newest release, or the active version when not behind, beside it (in `probe-versions/<version>+g<N>/probe-research` when the version's own folder is taken, which is never deleted), and hands that the update. The update reports it as a change from `<version>+broken`, and the lifeboat as `broken_env`. A release older than 0.328.0 is never rebuilt as itself. A release is retried at most once an hour. When a freshly rebuilt copy of the active release does not start either, that release is not rebuilt again for a day. Being offline, a uv timeout or a missing uv never causes that wait. Nothing is rebuilt with automatic updates off. The v3 hand-off returns without reading, locking or installing anything while `~/.local/state/probe/uninstall/barrier.json` marks an uninstall as live. The v1 and v2 copies already on machines read `+gN` folders correctly, and a release places v3 in `current/` and keeps `known-good/` until v3 proves itself.

## 0.336.1

- **Wizard polish from a click-through of 0.333.0 in a real terminal.**
  - Diagnose says each problem once and names every agent that has it ("Claude Code and Codex: could not verify the capture credential"). It used to repeat it under each agent, and it said Codex's MCP login twice in different words.
  - Three or more coding agents read "Claude Code, Codex, pi and Kimi Code", not "Claude Code and Codex and pi and Kimi Code".
  - After an Uninstall signs this device out, its page says "Press enter to finish…", because the wizard ends there; it used to promise a menu.
  - Diagnose's agent picker says "Checks each agent you pick." instead of "One report per agent you pick."

## 0.336.0

- **A device with no Probe opens straight into setup, and setup asks who records and what new sessions do.** `npx probe-research` on a machine with no sign-in and no coding agent set up goes to the guided install instead of the menu; its one browser approval is the sign-in. The install gains a Defaults step (Who records ‹ agent | daemon ›, Probe in new sessions ‹ on | read | off ›) that writes nothing until Install: the session default is saved at the Install keypress, Who records once the agents are installed, agent by agent.
- **Switching to the Probe daemon no longer opens a browser.** Its key, and pi's capture key, are minted from this device's sign-in (one retry, then the browser approval as before for an older server or a pasted token). Because that skips the page that disclosed the daemon, the wizard shows the same consent first: five lines, every line one choice away, kept equal to the dashboard's copy by a test.
- **`probe summary edit` and `probe summary append`: change a Summary page in one command, with no checkout.** `edit --old <exact HTML> --new <HTML>` replaces one piece (it must match once); `append --html <HTML>` adds before the page's `</article>`. Both read the page as HTML and write it pinned to that version, re-applying the change to a page that moved meanwhile; a person's `kept` block, a page the credential scrubber would rewrite, or a server without HTML pages is refused with nothing written. `--version N` (the page version the text was written from) pins the first write, so a session erasure since then is refused (exit 2) instead of its words written back; a lost or unreadable reply is settled by reading the page, never by sending again, and a write that changed nothing says so. The daemon keeps checkout and push.
- **A session message is shown once, on the machine the researcher is on (G7).** The Claude Code / Codex hook and pi tell Probe `delivered_to_agent` themselves when they show a message Probe held for the session (under the lease holder's name the worker now writes into the mailbox file, with the daemon's key from the CLI config; best effort within 1.5 s, nothing without a key), and the daemon reports every message its hook took before each poll, so a restarted daemon says it for all of them. The daemon's poll now carries `X-Probe-Agent-Active-At` (its transcript's newest chat line), so Probe moves a message not yet shown to the machine whose agent was active last, and the old machine deletes its unshown copy. Only a message marked shown after the hook's output went out is reported (a claim whose output failed, or whose hook died, waits again for the next hook), receipts never follow a redirect, and one tick's receipts share a 3 s budget (each wait at most 1.5 s; one Probe did not answer backs off behind those not tried) so they never hold the poll. Every claim the hooks and pi make of an inbox message carries `shows: 1` (a hook's receipt line after a Probe service claim too), and only such a claim waits for its `shown` line; an older hook's counts at its claim. An ack Probe answers 404 now reads as gone, not as one to repeat.

## 0.335.0

- **Reinstalling Probe works over any earlier install and repairs what is broken; new `probe repair`.** Every install entry (`npx probe-research`, the wizard's install, `probe update` from a throwaway copy, `probe daemon install`) now installs the CLI beside the running one under the install lock, checks it, then switches. A plain `uv tool install` through the side-by-side link used to rewrite the active version in place. A fresh machine gets the `probe` command. uv's own folder (after `uv tool install --force`, or a reinstall by hand) is adopted. A dangling link, a stale `active.json` and migration leftovers are put right. A broken active version is rebuilt in a folder of its own (`<version>+g<N>`) and switched to. `keeper-off` from an earlier uninstall no longer disables the keeper and lifeboat for good. A CLI moved back by hand is updated at once: it used to wait up to 6 h. A daemon key of another team is released and replaced. `PROBE_TOKEN` and other credential variables that disagree with the sign-in make the install incomplete, and the variable is named. A sign-in sends queued writes before it replaces the credential. Configure no longer says "Nothing to change" over a plugin whose files are gone or that is disabled. It removes the retired `prbe-cc-tap-plugin` and the other recorder's plugin, and repairs pi's `extensions: []` and Kimi records whose files are gone. Codex's `/hooks` line is shown when Probe's hooks changed and this run could not approve them. Nothing installs while an uninstall runs. pipx installs move to uv. `probe repair [--json]` (or `npx probe-research repair`) checks all of this and ends complete, or incomplete with the reasons.
- **A training job on another machine records its run with a token that reaches nothing else.** `probe exec --detached-launcher` now mints a `PROBE_TOKEN=probe_run_…` for the job, prints it beside the run id and epoch, and runs the launcher with it, so what a launcher forwards from its environment (`sbatch --export=ALL`, Modal's `from_local_environ`) is that token, never the researcher's key. It records that one run (no other run, no project, no new run), and the job's `probe.init()` joins its run from it alone; the Hugging Face and Lightning integrations treat it as a launcher-chosen run. `--token-ttl 36h` sets its life (the run's expected length plus margin; default 30 days) and also gives a blocking launcher such as `modal run` a token. If minting fails on a server that has per-run tokens, the launcher gets an empty `PROBE_TOKEN` rather than your key. `probe run token <run>` mints one by hand (`--ttl`), `--extend 7d` lengthens every token of the run without touching the running job, `--revoke-all` stops them and `--show` prints the expiry. When a live run's token is close to expiring, the launching agent gets a run alert and the run's creator an email saying to extend it; a daemon-profile agent may run `probe run token`. The `instrument-code` skill tells agents to forward this token instead of asking the researcher for an account-wide one, and every credential scrubber (tap, SDK logs, server) hides `probe_run_` tokens. Against a server without per-run tokens, `probe exec` keeps the old hand-off.

## 0.334.0

- **Probe approves its own hooks in Codex, so Codex users no longer have to find `/hooks`.** Codex runs no plugin hook until it is approved, says nothing when it skips one, and asks again whenever an entry changes, so a Codex install recorded nothing until the person approved Probe's hooks by hand (and T3 Code, which drives Codex, has no `/hooks` screen at all). The wizard now approves them right after installing Probe's Codex plugins, a recorder switch approves the plugin it swaps in, and every Codex plugin update approves any Probe hook left waiting, so machines installed before this heal on their next update. A machine that is already set up but has hooks waiting gets the approval from a wizard re-run instead of "Already set up". The approval is the write Codex itself makes from `/hooks` (app-server `config/batchWrite` of `hooks.state."<key>".trusted_hash`, with the hash Codex reports in `hooks/list`), and only for hooks of Probe's own plugins from Probe's marketplace, loaded from their copies in Codex's plugin cache; another plugin's, a project's, a user's or a managed hook is never touched. When Codex cannot be asked or refuses the write (an older Codex, a managed config), the install still succeeds and the closing note still says to approve them under `/hooks`. Codex reads approvals at session start, so an open session picks them up in its next one.
- **Claude Code no longer locks Probe out for 15 minutes when this computer has no Probe token.** The Probe plugin's token helper (`bin/probe-mcp-headers`) exited without a header when it found no token; Claude Code then sent the request bare, the MCP answered with its sign-in challenge, and Claude Code showed "Needs authentication" for Probe AND recorded it in `~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json`, so every new session for the next 15 minutes skipped Probe without asking the helper again, even after the wizard had written a token. The helper now always sends a header: with no token it sends a placeholder the hosted MCP refuses like a bad token ("Failed to connect", with the wizard named, no sign-in flow and nothing recorded), and the next connect asks the helper again, so a session heals as soon as a token exists. Measured with Claude Code 2.1.296 against a stand-in MCP: before, the session after the token appeared made 0 requests; now it connects. Claude Code also removes credential-named variables such as `PROBE_MCP_TOKEN` from the helper's environment, so under Claude Code only the token the wizard writes counts. The hosted MCP now logs why it refused each request (`missing`, `no_token_on_device`, `rejected`) and which client sent it, never the token; until now a missing token and a refused one were the same `401 invalid_token`.

## 0.333.1

- **Probe staff can bring back session capture on a machine where a bug revoked it, with nothing for you to do.** A wizard bug (fixed in 0.331.1) could revoke a coding agent's capture credential nobody had turned off, and a new one needed your browser approval. Staff can now open a one-time repair for one machine: the server marks that machine's answers to its own CLI token with `X-Probe-Capture-Repair` (the update-report flush hears it too), and the next `probe` command there fetches the replacement credentials (`POST /v1/client/capture-repair`), writes them where the wizard's sign-in would (Claude Code's in the CLI config, and over an older tap `.token` that would hide it; every other agent's in its tap folder), lifts those agents' locks, then confirms (`POST /v1/client/capture-repair/applied`), which closes the request. Until it confirms, a lost answer or a failed write is simply fetched again next time. A capture you turned off yourself after staff asked stays off and is reported as kept off; when capture you had turned off before resumes, one line on stderr says so and how to turn it off. Never from inside a training run, the Probe service, a command the Probe daemon runs, the wizard, or under a `PROBE_TOKEN`, `PROBE_BASE_URL` or `--base-url` that is not the config's own account. `capture.repair_applied` reports the agents written, those kept off, and whether the confirmation landed. Capture tokens are now created owner-only (0600) before the secret is written.

## 0.333.0

- **Every wizard result page answers what you asked, then lists only what you must do and what went wrong.** The pages printed every step every helper took, for every coding agent. Interactive runs now show:
  - **Who records:** "The Probe daemon now records for all 4 coding agents" or "All 4 coding agents record for themselves again", then Next (start new sessions; Codex's hook approval; a daemon key kept for open sessions) and the errors. It was 13 to 25 lines: "Installed 11 skill(s) in <path>: <every name>" as the title, "Takes effect in new X sessions." once per agent, and the reasoning-summaries paragraph.
  - **Uninstall:** "Removed Probe from all 4 coding agents", "This device is signed out.", the agents, and only the errors (a token the server could not be told to revoke). It was about 34 lines.
  - **Diagnose:** the verdict ("no problems found" / "2 problems"), one line for the device and one per agent, then the problems, each once; `c` still copies the full report. It was the whole doctor report per agent, about 300 lines for four agents, most of it the device's own sections repeated.
  - **Settings:** one line per changed setting ("Automatic updates → on") and the errors, instead of a "Codex:" section per agent saying "Already set up the way you asked. Nothing to change.".
  - **Sign out, account switch, import details:**
    - Sign out is two lines plus errors.
    - An account switch is one line, with one capture warning naming every affected agent.
    - An import's detail page shows the worker's output only when the import did not finish, and drops the job id and log path (`c` copies the path).

  Also:
  - The install screen says "Session capture paired: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code and pi." once, instead of a line per agent with its device id.
  - Skills are reported as "Installed 11 skills in ~/.claude/skills." without listing every name, in scripted runs too.
  - Diagnose names a Probe daemon that records with no key, and a sign-in's capture lock as `capture off (finish Install)`.
  - Update's "Turn on session capture?" answer is one line under the headline, not each agent's configure report.

  Scripted and `--json` runs otherwise keep the full report.

## 0.332.1

- **The daemon's command spec matches the CLI again.** `cli_spec.json` (the CLI's command tree, which the Probe daemon checks commands against) carried the hash of an older CLI source after #3500, so each daemon host rebuilt its own copy in a ~1 s child process once per CLI version. Commands were never refused; this release ships a spec that matches.

## 0.332.0

- **Desktop onboarding parity.** The app can now choose or create this computer's default filing workspace before imports, using the wizard's preselection and pin writer. Account changes, deleted/read-only workspaces and conflicting workspace limits are refused. Creation retries reuse the same workspace after a lost response. The app also gains the wizard's settings-only research-plan review, pasted-image upload and reasoning-summary options through shared readers and writers.

## 0.331.1
- **A sign-in no longer leaves session capture off when you pick Update instead of Install, and Settings or a scripted re-run no longer turns capture off when you change something else.** Signing in from the wizard's first screen holds the new capture credentials behind a lock (`.disabled` saying "Awaiting confirmation in the Probe install wizard.") until Install confirms them. On a machine whose plugins were already installed, people pick Update, which never lifted that lock, and the menu called it "killswitch set", the words for a deliberate off. The menu now says `capture off (finish Install)` for that lock and `probe doctor`'s Killswitch row says it is waiting for Install to confirm capture. Update asks once, before it starts, "Turn on session capture?" for each coding agent that holds its own unrefused credential behind the lock: "Not now" changes nothing and is not asked again by the release Update hands off to, Esc goes back to the menu without updating, and `--yes` or a non-interactive Update never asks. Separately, saving Automatic updates in Settings re-applied every other capability from what it read, and a capture that read as off (that lock included) ran the full turn-off: it revoked the agent's capture credential on the server and deleted it from disk (one customer, 2026-10-26, 90 seconds after the credential was made). `probe wizard --yes` / `--action configure` re-runs with other work to do could do the same. Settings now marks every capability it did not change as left as it is (`Selection.preserve`), and a re-run with no capture flag leaves a pending lock pending, per coding agent.

## 0.331.0

- **On macOS, the Probe service no longer waits forever on a daemon host that stopped reading.** A message to the daemon host (a run's start carries the session's whole environment) was sent with `MSG_DONTWAIT`, which macOS's `send()` ignores, so a host that stopped reading held the sending thread for good and was never marked stuck and killed. Each send to the host now has its own send timeout (`SEND_SLICE_S`, 1 s, which leaves the host's reader blocking as before), so it gives up after `SEND_TIMEOUT_S` on every platform.
- **A folder import files into a new project unless this folder's work already lives in an existing one, and an unattended import no longer adds files to an existing project this folder never used.** On 2026-10-26 two throwaway folders imported with `--yes` landed in unrelated existing projects (`import-model-benchmark`, then `digits-perceptron-training`): the classifier was shown every project in the workspace, told to "prefer these", and the slug it typed was reused at creation with nothing on the review screen saying so. Now a project in a plan has one of three origins. Code reuses an existing project silently only when a previous import of this same folder filed into it (the local coverage store says so, including the projects of files `--retry-dead` sends back for review), when it is the one project whose active code source is this folder's git repository at this folder or inside it (a source on the whole repository, or two projects on the folder's code, choose nothing: a monorepo's projects are not every subfolder's), or when the import was pointed at it (`--project`). A folder an older CLI already filed into an existing project keeps filing there. Any other reuse is a checked tool call, `probe-backfill-plan project --reuse <slug>`, refused with the nearest real projects when the slug matches none; `assign` no longer accepts an existing project by name, and `project <slug>` refuses an existing project's slug. The review screen marks each project `new` or `EXISTING`, and a reuse the classifier chose shows the project's name and what it already holds ("which already has 14 runs and 52 files"); `plan.json` gives each project `existing`, `origin` (`new`, `rule`, `model`), `name`, `project_id`, `reason`, `existing_runs`/`existing_files` and `possibly_same_as`, and its totals `projects_new`/`projects_existing`. An import nobody reviews (`--yes`, the desktop's automatic imports, any run without a terminal) turns such a reuse into a new project named for the folder, or the folder-named project an earlier such import made, and says so in one line. A new slug one or two edits from an existing one is flagged on review as possibly the same project, and one that is an existing slug (the chunked naming pass, which no longer sees the workspace's other projects and names new projects only) gets a free `-2` slug instead of merging; a new project whose slug someone took after the review gets the next free one too, and a create whose answer was lost resumes into the project it made (recognised by a nonce under `metadata.backfill_create`, never by slug alone). An existing project deleted between approval and import stops that import without filing anything and sets the approval aside, so the next run reviews those files again. A lookup of this folder's own project that fails on the network now stops the import instead of giving it a duplicate project. The prompts no longer say to prefer existing projects. `backfill.plan_ready` carries `projects_new`, `projects_reused_rule`, `projects_reused_model`, `projects_reuse_declined` and `projects_near_miss`. A plan an older CLI saved and approved still resolves its projects by slug, as it did.

## 0.330.0

- **The final screen's Details hold errors only.** An install's Details listed a restart line for every agent ("Restart Claude Code to load Probe.", "Restart Codex ...", ...) and a failed agent's Details repeated its whole screen, routine lines included. Restarts are now one Next line ("Restart Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code and pi to load Probe."; after an Update, "/reload (or restart)" where that works), with only the steps besides it that matter (Codex's hook approval, sessions still on an older tap, pi's /reload). Details list errors and what to do about them, and nothing else: no "Status line: on", "Auto-update on." or "paired" lines.

- **A background import no longer reports itself stuck over a brief connection blip.** The worker sent `import_job.stalled` (`waiting_for_connection`) on its very first retry, so one transient error from the API raised an "Import stuck" alert for an import that went on to finish. It now reports a stall only once it has been waiting for 5 minutes (`STALL_GRACE_S`), then every 10 minutes as before; `import_job.finished` still carries `network_retries`.

## 0.329.4

- **The daemon writer's note for the researcher is shorter.** When the writer sets a project's headline metric or a best pick, the main agent now reads `[Probe] Tell the researcher: <P>'s headline metric is now <KEY> (higher is better).` (`lower is better`; `, best value per run` with `--reduce best`) or `[Probe] Tell the researcher: <P>'s best experiment is now <EXP> ("<reason>").` (`workspace <W>'s ...` for a workspace pick; `... is now <EXP>.` with no reason), in place of `[Probe] For your researcher, in one line: the headline metric for <P> is now ...` and `... the best experiment for <P> is now <EXP> (reason: "<reason>")`. The reason stays one line of at most 200 characters with its double quotes turned to single ones; a single period ending it is dropped, since the note's own period now follows the closing quote. `mailbox.WRITER_RELAY_PREFIX` is `Tell the researcher: ` in the mailbox, both plugins' hooks and pi; a hook from before this release (0.328.0's included) shows the new text under "The writer recorded:". In a live check (Opus 5.5, `claude -p`, the note handed over as hook context the way `reads_hook.py` does) the main agent passed the short form on in 12 of 12 runs and the old form in 7 of 8 in the same setup.

## 0.329.3

- **instrument-code: a remote job gets its own Probe token, and recording it afterwards from the launcher is named for what it loses.** An agent that would not put the researcher's login into a cloud job spec recorded the training from the laptop after it finished instead, so the run had no curves, logs, data reads or real hardware. The skill now says to have the researcher mint one in their own terminal with `probe token create --name <job> --scope read --scope write` and keep it in the platform's secret store, and to state that cost before offering a launcher-side record. `probe exec`'s Modal hint now passes the token from a Modal secret (`modal.Secret.from_name`) instead of naming `PROBE_API_KEY`, which nothing reads, and its "forward these into the job" list now includes `PROBE_TOKEN`.

## 0.329.2

- **Re-importing a folder that an older CLI imported no longer reports its hidden-folder and worktree files as absent, and no longer stalls the project write-up on them.** Since 0.328.0 a folder import skips hidden folders and nested git worktree copies, but a folder imported before that still listed those files in its local coverage store; the next import did not see them, called them "previously observed files are absent" (65,491 files under `.claude/worktrees/` for one team), and the post-import plan reconstruction (the project draft) waited for them forever, because an absent file holds its project until it comes back. The store now records the rule that leaves each such file out (`hidden_folder` or `worktree_copy`, in new `skipped` and `skipped_on_disk` columns added in place; the store keeps its schema, so older CLIs still open it). A file still on disk under a folder the walk skipped is `skipped`: neither absent nor pending. A file really deleted from disk is still reported absent, inside a skipped folder too; but one a rule leaves out no longer holds any draft: an agent's worktree removed after it finished keeps the rule recorded while it was there, and any file under a hidden folder the walk skips is placed by its path, so worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` removed before this release are covered too. A worktree outside a hidden folder removed before any import by this release reads as deleted, as before. The absent line says how many of the absent files a rule leaves out anyway. Every import recomputes the rules, so `--include-hidden <name>` brings a hidden folder's files back. Skipped files are left out of their project's draft, so a project an older CLI drafted from worktree copies is drafted once more from its own files (a project only such files fed is not drafted); and a deleted file that no plan ever placed no longer holds every project's draft. The import says `N previously observed files are now skipped (hidden folders and worktree copies); anything uploaded from them stays on the server`, the per-file report lists them under `skipped` with their rule, and `backfill.summary` carries `absent_files`, `absent_skipped_files` and `skipped_by_rule_files`. Rules follow each import's own `--include-hidden`, so a hidden folder admitted on one import and not the next leaves that project's draft the second time. `plan.json` gains a `skipped` object with the same fields as the desktop's job record (`hiddenFolders`/`worktrees` with file counts, their counts and totals, `includedHidden`).

## 0.329.1

- **The lifeboat no longer "rescues" machines that are only idle.** The Probe service stops when no session needs it, so on an idle machine it does not answer, and after each release the lifeboat read that as a service that cannot start: idle machines updated through the lifeboat, and each one posted a "Lifeboat rescued" alert for a routine update. Now, when the machine is behind and the service is silent, the lifeboat first asks the service for an update check, which starts it; a working service then updates the machine the usual way. The lifeboat installs the newest release itself only when the service still has not answered 5 to 30 minutes after that ask, as a service that crashes at start never does. This ships as a new lifeboat copy (`handoff.py` version 2): it replaces the lifeboat's current copy, and the known-good copy stays at version 1 until version 2 proves itself.

## 0.329.0

- **Something always wakes the updater now, even when the installed release cannot update itself** (plan fool-proof-updates B1-B5). The Probe service installs a lifeboat in `~/.local/state/probe/lifeboat/`: a frozen `/bin/sh` wrapper and a copy of the update hand-off that lives outside every release, in two slots (`current/`, which a release may refresh only with a newer copy that passes its selftest, and `known-good/`, which a copy becomes only after it rescued the machine itself and a later update cycle reached the latest release; two hours after a rescue by `current/` that left the machine behind, `known-good/` runs instead). The keeper unit (systemd timer, launchd agent) now runs that wrapper every minute instead of the release's own python, and the wrapper runs the active keeper after it; with no session for 6 h it asks for an update check (`update.check_now` trigger `keeper`). An update cycle keeps the service alive for as long as its update child may run (up to 30 min), not 10 min. `probe artifact`, `probe run` and `probe outbox` outside a run ask the service for an update like any command (`log`, `span` and `exec` never do). A coding agent's session start runs the lifeboat (detached, at most hourly) when no keeper unit is installed or the service did not answer, so a pod with no user scheduler recovers too. What the lifeboat did is reported once as `lifeboat.acted`, with the machine's consent. Every update that succeeded and every `probe doctor` install or refresh the lifeboat too (with the same guards), so a pod where the service never starts still gets one; turning automatic updates off stops it at its next run. Uninstall removes the lifeboat with the keeper.
- **Nothing a person leaves open holds automatic updates off for more than a day, and the Probe CLI installed with uv now updates itself unless you turned automatic updates off.** The `probe wizard` menu held the setup lock for as long as it stayed open, so a menu left open in a terminal stopped every update on that machine, for good. The menu now lets go of the lock while it waits for you at the menu and on most actions' result pages (pressing ←/→ on the Defaults row takes it for that one save); it still holds it inside an action that waits for you (the Settings screen, the import monitor, the last pages of an install). While the menu waits, an update that would replace the files it runs from (an update in place, or the first switch to side-by-side versions) waits for it; one installed beside the running version goes on. Whatever a setup holds, the Probe service updates past it once it has held it for 24 hours, without touching it. An action the desktop app or the service runs (install, sign-out, update) is stopped after 60 minutes and reported failed, instead of blocking every later update; so is one a service before it left running. A missing or unreadable `~/.local/state/probe/autoupdate.json` used to mean "automatic updates off"; for the Probe CLI installed with `uv tool install` (what `npx probe-research` sets up when uv is there) it now means on. Nothing is written for that: the file holds only what you chose. Only an explicit "off" (the wizard's Settings, or `--no-auto-update`) is off, in any state folder (it is now saved both under `XDG_STATE_HOME` and in `~/.local/state/probe`, which the service reads), and removing Probe keeps it; `probe doctor` says "yes (on by default for this install)". A `probe` installed with pip, pipx, as an editable checkout or as a project dependency is never updated unless you turned automatic updates on, as before. Where the CLI updates itself (no Probe service: pip and pipx installs), a command run outside a terminal (a hook, a coding agent's shell) now starts the update too, at most once every 15 minutes, never from a command a Probe daemon runs or while a daemon worker records, and a training run holds the update off for 24 hours at most, as the service already did (a run found after two idle hours starts its own 24 hours).

## 0.328.0

- **When the daemon's writer sets a project's headline metric or a best pick, your agent is told to pass it on.** track-work has the agent set them itself and tell the researcher in one line, but under the daemon the writer sets them and could not reach the researcher: a bench showed 0 of 4 runs told anyone, and the run's receipt said only "changed project <P>".
