Each `probe project set P --metric KEY --goal max|min`, `project set P --best EXP --reason "..."` or `workspace set W --best EXP --reason "..."` the writer runs with exit 0 now sends the main agent one note: `[Probe] For your researcher, in one line: the headline metric for <P> is now <KEY> (higher is better).` (`, each run's best value` with `--reduce best`) or `... the best experiment for <P> (or: workspace <W>) is now <EXP> (reason: "<reason>")` (the writer's reason quoted as data, one line, at most 200 characters). It is read from the command's own words and the record Probe printed, never the model's prose: a failed write (a 409 over a person's metric or pick), a queued one, a clear, a person's value sent again and a repeat of the value last told for the same project or workspace send nothing (after a clear the same value is news again), and a daemon's first look tells only writes from the last 15 minutes, so an upgrade never replays old ones, and the receipt no longer lists those writes. It goes out like a receipt (on the next prompt or tool call, never a wake, only where the agent's hooks read the mailbox); both plugins' hooks and pi show it under its own label, and a hook from before this shows the same text under "The writer recorded:". In a live check (Opus 5.5, 25 `claude -p` runs) a main agent passed this wording on in 8 of 9 runs, against 5 of 8 for "For your researcher: <fact>" without "in one line ... now"; today's receipt text was mentioned in 3 of 3 but names no metric.

- **Every update now runs in the newest release's code, so a bug in an older updater can be fixed by shipping a newer release.** An update used to run every step with the code of the release already installed: when that release's updater had a bug (a plugin step that crashed, a step that hung, an install it could not do), every later release was stuck behind it until someone updated by hand. Now the installed release only downloads the newest one, beside itself, and hands the rest of the update to it in the same process (`probe/_shared/handoff.py`, a small frozen file); the newest release switches the CLI to itself and updates the plugins, pi and the records. This holds for every way an update starts: the Probe service, `probe wizard` (its menu, `--action update`, `--yes`, `--json`), `probe update` and the automatic update a `probe` command starts. A new version is used only once uv finished installing it and its own update code loads: one whose update code fails to load is deleted and installed again by the next update, and one that loads but whose Probe service or CLI does not start is skipped for 24 hours. Also: one coding agent's plugin step, or pi's, that fails or runs past 10 minutes now fails only that agent's step (a hung step's processes are stopped), and the CLI and the other agents still update and report (it used to stop the whole update); every install and switch takes one shared install lock, and an update that has held it for 45 minutes is stopped; a version that was switched back is tried again after 24 hours, and never holds back a newer release; a pinned Python that uv can no longer use is replaced by uv's own, and `--with` packages that will not install beside the new version (for any reason) are left out as the last resort, tried again by the next update, with `probe doctor` printing the exact command to add them back; a uv receipt entry the update cannot restate is left out and named instead of blocking every update; and an update that cannot read the newest release tries again later instead of updating in place.

- **A folder import skips hidden folders and extra checkouts of the repo it is importing, and says what it skipped.** A customer's import uploaded 78,628 files, 65,491 of them from seven Claude Code agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/`: seven checkouts of one repo, each read by the classifier and uploaded. Two rules now, in the walk (`backfill_evidence.walk`): (1) a hidden folder is skipped unless it is a research one (`.hydra`, `.dvc`, `.aim`, `.neptune`) or named with the new repeatable `probe backfill --include-hidden <name>`; credential stores (`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.kube`, `.docker`, `.azure`, `.gcloud`, `.config`) stay refused whatever either says (an unknown dot-folder was imported until now), and `.dvc/cache` and `.dvc/tmp` (copies of DVC-tracked data) are skipped; hidden files are handled as before. (2) A nested git worktree is skipped when its main checkout is inside the folder and imported too, for any tool's worktrees, dot-folder or not (files only in the worktree, such as untracked outputs, are skipped with it); a submodule, a bare repo's worktrees, a worktree of a repo outside the folder or whose main checkout is itself skipped, and the folder itself are still imported. Both are still walked and counted: the plan lists them ("Skipped 7 git worktrees (N files): checkouts of a repo this import already carries.", "Skipped hidden folders: .claude (N files), .codex (M files)."), a background import's job record carries them as `skipped` for the desktop app (`docs/probe-desktop-management-v1.md`), and `backfill.scanned` gains `skipped_hidden_dirs`, `skipped_hidden_files`, `skipped_worktrees` and `skipped_worktree_files`. An import a previous CLI approved and queued finishes by the rules it was approved under.

## 0.327.0

- **A folder import now creates experiments and runs, not just projects.** The classify pass names them through `probe-backfill-plan`, checked against the walk when each call is made (a folder that does not exist, or whose files are undecided or split across projects, is refused with the nearest real folder): `experiment --slug <s> --project <p> --name ... --question ... --under <dir>` files a directory into a new experiment, `run --under <dir>` makes one folder a run and `run --each-under <dir>` makes each folder under a directory one run in a single call. The model names folders only; code reads everything else from the files: the run's name is its folder, its start and end the oldest and newest file mtime (none when every file of the import shares one copy-like mtime window), its config the top-level scalars of `*.toml`, `config*.json|yaml|yml`, `args*.json` and `params*`/`hparams*` files, its metrics the top-level numbers of `reward.json`, `*result*.json`, `outcome.json`, `metrics*.json`, `summary*.json`, `eval*.json` and a lone number in `reward.txt`/`score.txt` (a nested file's keys carry its folder, e.g. `trials/01-x/verifier/reward`; nothing is averaged), and its status an explicit `status`/`outcome`/`success`/`passed`/`exit_code` in a result file at the run's top level, else `untracked` (never a claimed success). The review screen and a new `plan.json` beside the per-file report lead with the counts (`3 projects · 12 experiments · 87 runs`, per project); nothing is created before approval. After approval the runs are created with source `backfill`, keyed by the import source and the run's folder (a re-import finds them and creates nothing); each file uploads once at its project and is then moved, by id, into its run or experiment; a run is read from, and holds, only the files a reviewed plan placed in it, and a changed file's new upload is moved again. Files imported before this release are organized the same way on the next import of their folder (asked once in an interactive import; an unattended one organizes them): they keep their project and are moved, never uploaded again. Upload (notes) agents still create nothing. `backfill.plan_ready`, `backfill.approved` and `backfill.summary` carry `experiments_proposed`/`runs_proposed`, `experiments_approved`/`runs_approved`, and `experiments_created`/`runs_created`/`runs_existing`/`runs_zero_metrics`/`files_filed`. A `.jsonl` never becomes a metric series yet: it is filed as a file.

## 0.326.1

- **A folder import's file notes now feed the project's draft, and a new draft replaces the one the import published before.** The unit agents' one-line notes (`probe-backfill-plan note`) were saved and never read. Each file excerpt the draft reads now carries that file's note (masked whole by the excerpt's credential gate, then cut to 240 characters), and described files are read first within the excerpt caps; a note never becomes a source on its own. The draft prompt treats a note as a hint for finding and connecting files, never as support (`backfill-reconstruction/4`). Publishing replaces an earlier draft only when the Overview still holds it word for word as this import published it (formatting the page renderer rewrites aside); a draft a person edited, another import's draft, prose and a README embed are left alone, and the confirmation says which. Each project redrafts once on its next completed import.

## 0.326.0

- **An install or an Update ends on a short summary instead of every coding agent's full report.** The final screen spent a page on lines like "already at the latest", "Refreshed the Probe block" and "Status line: on" around the one that mattered. It now says how many coding agents worked ("Updated 3 of 4 coding agents", "Installed Probe in all 4 coding agents"), lists them with where their plugins ended ("plugin 0.180.0 (updated), tap 0.10.23"), then a Details section with only what needs attention: what failed and the commands to run by hand, a restart or hook approval to do, a CLI or pi package failure (once), and the agents an install that stopped never reached. Scripted (`--yes` without a terminal) and `--json` runs keep the full report. **An Update no longer reports Codex's plugins missing when `codex plugin list --json` cannot answer:** on 2026-10-26 it timed out after 20 s on a Mac right after the update reinstalled both plugins, so the update said neither could be confirmed. When the list cannot be read, the update now reads Codex's own files instead (the plugins `codex plugin add` records in config.toml and the copies it installs under `plugins/cache`) and says so; the server's update report still records that the list was unreadable.

## 0.325.1

- **The daemon's compaction summary no longer carries ids the model typed: plain code appends the logbook of landed writes after it.** The writer's summary REPLACES its history, and the summary prompt asked the model to quote "every Probe write that landed, with exact ids and slugs" and "the last turn and event ids covered", so one mistyped id made a later write fail or land on a real but wrong entity. The prompt now asks for prose and no ids or slugs; after the model's text the daemon adds `## Landed writes (from your logbook, not the summary)`, built from the session's logbook: each `probe` write that ran (help, reads and shell commands left out), newest first, one line per command, target and id, with the id and slug Probe answered with and the events the run that made it covered (at most 100, the rest counted, older ones one `session` op=logbook away). A block in that shape the model wrote is cut first, and a later compaction's anchor is the earlier summary's prose alone, so the model is never handed ids to copy.

## 0.325.0

- **The daemon's ML gate and its reader gate are removed.** The worker no longer asks Probe whether a session is ML work and never pauses itself (no `<sid>.auto-pause`, no `paused: not ML` on the status line, no `auto_paused` in `probe session status`; `state_source` stays). The reader no longer asks a cheap model "look or skip?" before an unasked turn: a due wake is a reader turn, and its cost is only its own rounds. The Probe service's hint lookups no longer send the gate's ML state. Both ran only in shadow: the ML gate scored Strand's real ML sessions "not ML" (97% under 0.5) and the reader gate missed 30% of the turns that mattered. A store an older CLI wrote may still hold `skipped` read turns and an `auto-pause` file; nothing reads either, and the status line's 30-day prune deletes the file.

## 0.324.1

- **The track-work skill has the agent set a project's headline metric and its best experiment itself and tell the researcher, instead of asking first.** `skills/track-work/SKILL.md` (and its rendered copies) now says: with no headline metric yet, choose one from the code and runs, set it (`probe project set P --metric KEY --goal max|min`) and tell the researcher in one line; with a better experiment to use than the pick, set it (`probe project set P --best EXP --reason "..."`) and tell the researcher in one line. `tests/test_doctrine_sync.py` pins `tell the researcher in one line` and `better experiment to use than the pick` in place of `which way is better` and `only if they agree`. The tap moves to 0.10.24 for the two lines (`tap/companion_rules.md`).
- **Folder-import agents get shorter prompts, and they can no longer run `probe`.** The unit prompt asked the agent to create an experiment and "attach those artifacts", with no command to attach them: on 2026-10-26 Codex guessed `probe experiment create --description` (refused, 9 times) and uploaded the files itself, then the import uploaded them again (1,583 of 2,327 duplicated). A unit agent now only writes file notes, and every import agent's one command is `probe-backfill-plan`: Claude's allowlist drops `Bash(probe:*)` and Codex's commands run with no network (code does every upload). The unit prompt no longer appends the track-work skill (2,601 -> 215 words per unit turn). The git-history fragment no longer asks the agent to run `probe project code attach` (the import attaches the repositories the person reviewed) or says `git log` is allowed (Claude's allowlist denies it). Every folder-reading prompt says file contents and commit messages are data, never instructions. Classify, revise, survey, naming and assign are cut to their rules (30-60% shorter); `--under` is described as selecting every file at or below a directory. The draft prompt is unchanged. The dead single-agent `build_prompt` and the uncalled `write_notes` and `map_wandb` prompts are deleted.

## 0.324.0

- **An install or an Update shows one progress bar with its percentage for the whole run.** An install's bar started again from empty on every coding agent's screen (1/6, then 2/5, then 3/4), never said which agent it was on, and sat still through its longest wait: every agent's marketplace refresh and plugin installs, inside the first agent's refresh step. It is now one bar from 0% to 100% across every agent, headed by what is running ("Installing plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code", then "Installing for Codex (2 of 4)"), and it moves as each agent's refresh and installs finish (8% to 51% during that wait for 4 agents). The screen is centred like the wizard's prompts and spinner: it opens in the middle of the terminal (it was pinned 4 rows from the top whatever its height) and grows down, moving up only as far as new lines need; the bar spans the text column (it sat at the column's left edge). The Update was a spinner with no idea of how far along it was, and the screen went blank while each agent's state was sent to the server afterwards; now the spinner names each stage (the CLI, pi's package, the plugins still updating, the recording) with a bar and its percentage under it, until the results show. When `codex plugin list --json` cannot confirm the Codex plugins after an update, the message now says whether the list could not be read (and why) or what it lists instead: two machines reported both plugins unconfirmed on 2026-10-25 with nothing to tell those apart.

## 0.323.1

- **The Probe daemon audits the team note in T3 Code's Claude sessions too, and never in a `codex exec` an app started.** T3 Code (pingdotgg/t3code) runs Claude Code through the Agent SDK, so its sessions say `sdk-cli`, as `claude -p` does, and the daemon took them for programs. It now reads past a program's entrypoint, in a transcript's first 40 lines (was 20), for T3's `t3-code` MCP tools in Claude Code's own tool list, which a `claude -p` started from a T3 shell does not get. T3's Codex threads already passed (`originator: "T3 Code"`); a Codex rollout with `source: "exec"` is now a program whatever originator it inherited (a `codex exec` run from a T3 shell says `T3 Code`). A transcript line nested past the JSON parser's depth no longer escapes the check. The prompt hook (agent profile) is unchanged: T3's environment variables reach every program its agents start, so they prove nothing. Measured on t3 0.1.2 (2026-10-26): Claude and Codex threads started from T3 run Probe's hooks (Codex once they are approved, which T3 has no screen for: approve them in Codex's `/hooks`), `/probe on` typed in T3 turns Probe on, and both sessions reach the knowledge base.

## 0.323.0

- **Probe knows whether its hints reach your agent, and gives the daemon's reader back where they do not.** The hook (Claude Code, Codex) and pi's extension now record each message they hand the agent (`claimed/<sid>/shown.jsonl`, written only once their output went out) and leave a heartbeat (`reads/alive/<sid>.json`) whenever they run. The Probe service's hint lane reads them, with its own ledger of what it posted and took back, and sends what became of the session's hints with every `/v1/hints` request (`delivery`: posted, claimed, shown, missed, withdrawn, and whether delivery is `ok`, `unproven` or `undeliverable`). The markers that let the reader skip its prompt turns and check-ins (`<sid>.live`, `.window`) are now touched only where a deliverer is seen (a heartbeat: pi's within 10 minutes, a hook's within 12 hours) or a hint was shown in the last 30 minutes, so a session whose hints go nowhere keeps its reader instead of hearing nothing. A session whose hints keep missing their chance to be shown (two, each after two tool calls with the turn's hint slot free, on a harness that shows hints mid-turn) is `undeliverable`: the lane asks for it only at a researcher's prompt, at most every 30 minutes, until one is shown, and `probe status` / `probe doctor` name it (with the fix: quit the agent and resume the session; on pi `/reload` is not enough). A worker's start-up sweep no longer deletes another live session's status file once it is a week old, and it now takes an ended session's heartbeat and hint files with the rest of its mailbox. Plan hints-relevance T1-T2.

## 0.322.0

- **Folder imports run your agent at the model and reasoning effort the server sets, per lane, and report what each lane cost.** An import reads `GET /v1/import-jobs/agent-settings` once (5 s at most; any failure or no answer keeps today's launch byte for byte) and `PROBE_IMPORT_AGENT_SETTINGS` (same JSON, wins field by field) for its classify, import and draft lanes. Codex gets `-m <model>` and `-c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>"` (the effort only as a literal from Codex's own list), Claude `--model` and `--effort` (dropped, and named in the degraded note, on a Claude without them). An agent that refuses the setting before doing anything (a model this account cannot use: about 4 s, no output) is relaunched once without it, under a fresh session. `backfill.summary` and each background attempt's `import_job.finished` carry per lane the model, effort, source, launches, refusals, prep-cache hits, launches with no usage report (never counted as 0) and the input, cached, cache-write, output and reasoning token sums.

## 0.321.0

- **`probe outbox pause` ends by itself, after 24 h unless `--hours N` (at most a year); `--until-resume` keeps the old hold-until-resume.** A pause used to have no end: nothing resumed it, and every write the machine made afterwards (runs, files, metrics) queued silently behind it. On 2026-10-26 a folder import's abort screen suggested it, it was typed 20 s later, and the import's last 800 writes and everything after them stayed on the machine. **An update releases a stuck outbox at once, with no command from anyone:** a pause an older CLI wrote (a bare timestamp, recording no end) is over, and so is one whose end has passed. The next `probe` command of any kind deletes the marker (an SDK pinned in a job's venv reads only whether it exists), says once on stderr that uploads start again, kicks the uploader and reports `outbox.pause_lifted`; the Probe service, which starts after every update, does the same as it starts and every minute after for the default outbox (one stat; an outbox moved by `PROBE_OUTBOX_DIR`/`XDG_STATE_HOME` in a profile waits for the next `probe` command), never waiting on another process's lock, and starts the uploader for the root queue with the login shell's variables (proxies, CA bundle, config path, report switches), only when it can read them, reporting nothing itself. A marker this release cannot read (permissions, I/O, a symlink, not a file) still holds, and a JSON one without a readable end holds 24 h from its start. `read_status` reads `paused` from the marker, not from `status.json`'s copy, once per call, and adds `paused_until`; the banner says when the pause ends and that `probe outbox resume` sends now; `probe outbox ...` commands never lift first; the import's abort screen says the pause holds every upload from the machine, runs included, for 24 h. A pause an older CLI still on the machine types after this release is over too. **`probe experiment create --description` is a usage error, not a crash.** The folder import's prompt still asked for it, the SDK raised a bare `ValueError`, and one import crashed 14 times (its agents then sent 6 `probe doctor --send` reports); the prompt no longer asks, and `create` refuses the flag before any call, like `experiment set`.

## 0.320.0

- **Agents can set a project's headline metric and best experiment; the Probe daemon names its session on model calls; Codex and Kimi Code sessions count their tokens (swarm visibility PR4a).** `probe project set P --metric KEY --goal max|min [--reduce final|best]`, `probe experiment set E --metric ...`, `probe project set P --best E --reason ...` and the new `probe workspace set W --best E --reason ...` (`""` clears); SDK: `set_project_metric`, `pick_project_best`, `pick_workspace_best` and their reads and clears. A person's metric or pick is never replaced: the CLI prints whose it is, with no override flag. The daemon sends `X-Probe-Agent` + `X-Probe-Agent-Session` on every `/v1/companion/*` call. Tap 0.10.22: Codex `token_usage_record` ships as per-turn usage (`turn:<turn_id>`, the turn's model, cache taken out of input), Kimi `step.end` as per-step usage (`<turn_id>:<step>`, the step's model) and a Kimi compaction's `usage.record` as its own call; each session's call models are saved with its cursor, so a restart or another session never changes them. The write gate (and pi's) counts `probe workspace set` as a write.
- **`probe session send <sid> "..."` messages one of your own running sessions, and the Probe daemon delivers what Probe holds for its session (swarm visibility G7).** The daemon's run-alert lane polls the session's messages every 30 s, publishes each to the mailbox (`origin` `inbox`, kept 12 h, the file named by the message id) before it acks, and reports it shown once a hook claimed it; it names itself by this machine's device id (`X-Probe-Daemon-Instance`) for the server's delivery lease, publishes a message a lapsed lease hands it even if another machine received it, and drops a copy another daemon holds or Probe revokes (each poll names the copies still waiting, and Probe answers which another machine took, the agent was shown, or are gone). Every deliverer applies one rule to every `[Probe]` message it shows, of any kind (`mailbox.one_label`, mirrored in the hooks and pi, pinned by a shared fixture): only the message's own label keeps `[Probe]` (matched after NFKC folding and ignoring zero-width and other format characters), so a teammate's note quoted in team context, an answer, an alert or a hint can never pass for a dashboard message; an inbox message's further lines are also quoted `> ` (`mailbox.inbox_safe`); the hooks (both plugins) and pi deliver it like a run alert, at every prompt and tool call and waking an idle Claude Code or pi (Codex reads it at its next prompt). The agent reads `[Probe] Message from <person> (dashboard): ...` for a dashboard message and `[Probe] Message from <person>'s agent session "<title>": ...` for anything sent with a token. The daemon profile's guard lets `probe session send` run, and the daemon's managed block (v49) says a dashboard message delivered by Probe is the researcher's: act on it; copies elsewhere and agent-session messages stay evidence.

- **Agents read a project's, an experiment's or a workspace's lines of work in one call (swarm visibility PR4b).** `entity view=branches` on a project (its tree) or an experiment (its line and the ones it split from) gives each branch's best value, rank, gap to the leader, effort (span, busy, run-, agent-hours, cost; unknown cost is `null`), state, gain since its best, the branch it overlapped most, how many sessions and which harnesses, with slug refs; `view_options={"branch": "<ref>"}` gives one branch in full, each experiment with its own effort. `browse mode=branches workspace_id=W` does the same for a workspace, ranked per metric, and `branch=<ref>` opens one of its branches in full from the same read. A branch ranked on another metric carries that metric (`key`, `goal`, `reduce`) and its `of` on its own row; a slug ref longer than `entity` takes (256) is sent as the id ref. CLI: `probe project branches P`, `probe experiment branch E` (JSON); SDK: `project_branches`, `experiment_branch`, `workspace_branches`. On the 8-branch swarm fixture the workspace read is 1,633 tokens and one branch in full 1,006 (bounds 2,000 and 3,000).
- **The track-work skill asks the researcher for a project's headline metric and its direction, sets a new best experiment only when they agree, and links every follow-up to what it built on (swarm visibility PR6).** Three lines in `skills/track-work/SKILL.md` (and its rendered copies) name `probe project set P --metric KEY --goal max|min` and `probe project set P --best EXP --reason "..."`; `tests/test_doctrine_sync.py` pins them. The tap moves to 0.10.23 for the track-work lines (`tap/companion_rules.md`).

## 0.319.1

- **One failed step no longer stops a folder import.** A slice the classifier could not read (twice) used to stop the whole classification; now it only narrows what the naming step sees, its files are still filed, and the review screen counts it (`unread_slices`). A naming step that fails or names nothing used to stop it too; now the folder goes into one project named for the folder (`naming_fallback`), and the review screen says so and that the plan can split it. A background import whose upload agent stopped mid-batch used to end failed until someone pressed resume; now the job retries that batch itself with its saved progress, until the batch's 3-attempt limit, and only then reports it (`unit_retries` on the job's progress and finish event; no connection-wait stall is reported for it).

## 0.319.0

- **An Update or an install for several coding agents moves them all at once.** The wizard's Update ran the whole update once per agent: the CLI's own upgrade, the version manifest and `pi update` (git and npm) were repeated for every agent, and each agent's marketplace fetch and `plugin update` waited for the last one's. Now the CLI, the manifest and pi's package move once, then every agent's plugins at the same time, one thread each (`upgrading.perform_updates`); each agent's pass is still recorded and reported in agent order, so the merged update report and the one registration are as before. An install for several agents installs each agent's plugins with its marketplace refresh, all agents at once, after the sign-in and only for what its credentials cover; each agent's own steps still run (Claude Code's skills, the capture switch) and take those answers. `kimi --version` (~1 s) is asked once per Kimi binary instead of at every step, and an Update's own state check asks the server nothing it would not use. Measured on a 4-agent Linux machine (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, pi) with real agent CLIs against a stand-in server: an Update 18.4 s → 6.1 s, an install 8.8 s → 6.1 s; the files they leave are the same. If the first agent's install fails, the run still stops there as before, but later agents may already have their plugins, capture included: the person chose them on the confirm screen, and a re-run of the wizard finishes their setup.

## 0.318.1

- **Probe's own folder-import agents are no longer captured as the researcher's sessions.** Every agent the import launches (classifier, upload, reconstruction) now runs without the researcher's hooks (`disableAllHooks` in its Claude `--settings`; `--disable hooks` for a Codex whose `features list` names `hooks`), so no Probe plugin registers it for capture, and the past-sessions import skips any transcript that ran in one of the import's own scratch dirs, matched by their layout wherever the state root was (`import_agents` in its census), which also covers sessions an older CLI left on disk. On 2026-10-25, 45 classifier sessions had been imported as one researcher's history.

## 0.318.0

- **A folder import's classifier files files by selecting them, and no longer throws the whole plan away over a typo.** It used to answer with every path in the folder copied back "verbatim"; on 2026-10-25 a 144,178-file import mistyped two random-hex directory names out of 10,537 rows, the plan was refused whole, and 52 minutes of classification were lost. Every model step now picks through `probe-backfill-plan` (`assign <project> --under <dir>` / `--file` / `--rest`, `leave-out`, `status`, `show`, `apply --from`), which checks each choice against the walk when it is made and refuses a name that matches nothing with the nearest real ones, so the model fixes it in the same turn. The import builds a file-level plan from the tool's log, re-checked against the file list it holds in memory, never from the model's reply. A slice that files 80% of its files keeps them and the rest follow their neighbours; one that files less, or nothing (including an agent that could not reach the tool and exited 0), costs only its own files, which are named on the review screen, stay waiting, and are all the next run classifies (`partial_classification`). A correction at the review screen is one session started from the plan, not every slice again. The upload step writes every file of a unit onto the upload list in code (references decided by size); the agent only adds notes (`probe-backfill-plan note`, 2,000 characters at most), so a finished unit can no longer drop a file. `probe-backfill-plan` touches only the session's own work dir (no network, no team record) and runs on the session's PATH. Classification caches from older CLIs are ignored.

## 0.317.1

- **The daemon host checks `probe` commands without loading the whole CLI again.** The command spec shipped with the CLI (`cli_spec.json`) must match the CLI's source exactly, and any edit makes it older: 0.315.1 shipped one older than its CLI, so every host loaded the whole CLI (35 MB) instead. Now a spec older than the installed CLI is replaced, once per CLI version, by one a short-lived child process writes into the daemon's state folder (`<state>/probe/daemon/cli-spec/`); and this release's spec matches its CLI.

## 0.317.0

- **Probe hints reach a prompt sooner.** The Probe service's hint lane looks at each followed transcript every 0.25 s instead of every second (a prompt waited ~0.5 s on average before its lookup went; now ~0.125 s). Window lookups go on a thread and kept connection of their own, so a prompt that comes while a window lookup waits on the server (up to 12 s) is asked at once, not after it, and a window just sent no longer starts its session's 10 s gap for the next prompt (each kind waits after its own lookup only). With two lookups of one session now answering out of order, a hint from an older trigger never replaces a newer one waiting in the session's slot, one sharing a record with a hint delivered while it was asked is not posted, a window lookup leaves the machine's tokens to the prompts due now, and nothing is posted after the team's hints went off or the service began to close (an aborted request is not sent again). A transcript whose last line is unfinished is not read again until it grows. Every answered lookup's log line now ends `answered N ms after the trigger`, not only a posted hint's. Plan hints-latency.

## 0.316.0

- **The wizard opens in a third of the time, its check after every change takes a quarter of a second, and an install takes about half as long.** Every `probe` command used to build the ~770 generated wire models at start (~0.5 s), whether or not it sent one: the wizard, the plugin hooks, the status line, `probe --version`. The CLI now imports only the option enums (`probe._generated.enums`, split out by `scripts/gen_models.py`; every name still imports from `probe._generated.models` and `probe.models`) and loads the SDK client when a command builds one: `probe --version` takes 0.29 s instead of 0.95 s and 46 MB instead of 79 MB, and that is also what the `npx probe-research` launcher runs to check the installed version. The wizard reads each coding agent's plugins from the agent's own record (Claude Code's `installed_plugins.json`, Codex's `config.toml`: the files its `plugin list` reads, as `probe status` already does) instead of starting the agent's CLI, a Node start each, and checks the read token (`/v1/me`) through the SDK's transport instead of a whole client. "Checking what's installed on this device", which runs on entry and again after every change, went from ~1.6 s to ~0.25 s for 4 agents, and launch to main menu from ~3.2 s to ~1.2 s, on a Linux machine; the gain is larger where Node starts slower. Diagnose still asks each agent's CLI (it is there to show a `claude` that cannot start), and the install's final check asks it too before calling a plugin missing that the record does not list. An install for several agents refreshes their marketplaces (a git clone or fetch each, ~2.5 s on a first install) all at once in the first agent's refresh step, after the sign-in (nothing is written while the browser approval waits), instead of one agent after another; a retry still refreshes again. When the browser approval is refused, the marketplace step is skipped as the installs are, so no agent's config is changed. On a first install, a marketplace that `add` has just cloned is not fetched a second time by `update` (Claude Code 4.5 s → 2.5 s, Codex 3.7 s → 1.7 s); a marketplace already on disk is still updated. The install's final check asks the server once (`POST /v1/device-state`), and the old way (`/v1/me` and the capture key's status) only when that call does not answer, instead of always; the Who records check after a first setup takes a snapshot only when the agent actually moves. A first install for Claude Code and Codex, end to end with real agent CLIs against a stand-in server: ~12–14 s → ~5–6 s of the wizard's own time.

## 0.315.1

- **A pi started during `pi update` starts.** `pi update` reinstalls its clone's packages (`git clean -fdx`, then `npm install`); pi package 0.7.2's entry loads Probe's code beside it only when no pin can run, so a pi started in that second no longer fails to load the extension: it starts, and Probe runs a pinned version from the next turn once one of the clone's version exists (set up for the session it missed the start of); with none, pi says once to run /reload. On macOS, where `ps` shows a command line without argument boundaries, a Kimi Code session's own `tap watch` and a pi run from a folder whose path holds a space are now seen (before, the space split the path and they were missed), so an update never says "no restart needed" past them.

- **The Probe daemon keeps each session's state apart inside one process (groundwork for one daemon host per machine; nothing changes for a worker that runs as its own process).** The model's refusal fallback, the settings the server pushes, the HTTP client, the alert gate, the trace drain, the tool guide cache and the environment are now each run's own (`probe.daemon.runctx`), the write lease names the run that holds it (an additive `owner` field: two runs of one session in one process never both hold it), the TLS trust is built outside its shared lock (a certificate path on a hung mount stalls only the session that set it), and the worker's start splits into its process setup and `run_session`, which a host can call.
- **Every recorded session's Probe daemon now runs in ONE daemon host process beside the Probe service, instead of a `probe daemon worker` process each.** 40 idle sessions: 262 MB instead of 6 GB (measured on Linux); each session keeps its own thread and event loop, environment, model state, lease and log files, so a hung mount stalls only that session. A native crash in one session's run backs that session off and restarts the others at once (their conversations resume from disk; the tools the crashed host had started are ended first); a host over its memory budget is replaced, its sessions handing over at their next model round, as on an update. The service stays up while its host finishes a session's queue, so the host never outlives it unowned. An old tap's own `probe daemon worker` becomes a ~20 MB stand-in whose work runs in the host. The daemon no longer imports the whole CLI to check its commands (it reads the CLI's command tree from `cli_spec.json`, kept equal by a test: `make -C agent sync-cli-spec` after a command change): ~30 MB less per host. `service.status` keeps one `workers` row per session (`host: true`) and adds `daemon_host`. Off: `PROBE_DAEMON_HOST=off` in the service's environment, or an `off` file in its `daemon-host` folder; Windows keeps a worker process per session.
- **An idle session's daemon in the daemon host wakes on change instead of looking every 2 s.** A run that has seen nothing new for a minute looks every 10 s, and the host wakes it within a second when its chat log, switch, `probe ask` questions, writer requests, SDK inbox, approval answers or hand-over ask change (one watcher thread for every run, stat only). A worker that runs as its own process is unchanged.

## 0.315.0

- **Probe hints look at a long turn's work every 10 minutes, and replace the daemon reader's 30-minute check-ins where they work.** The Probe service's hint lane gains a `window` lookup: 10 minutes after the last one, the researcher's last prompt or the turn's first step (the transcript's own clock), at the agent's next step, when the agent wrote at least one message since, every message it wrote in that time goes to `/v1/hints` (newest first, at most 32, each secret-scanned before it is cut to 2,000 characters), and the server looks each one up on its own. Tool calls, their output and reasoning are never sent, and a tool call's `.probe.config` check is its folder's alone (the per-call reads walk trees). A prompt's own search already covers the prompt, and the turn's end ends its window. A window lookup goes after every other lookup due, never takes the machine's last lookup token (it waits until two are left), waits up to 12 s, and is held on its own (a 404, or a 422 naming `trigger`, from a server without window lookups: 10 minutes; a 429 or no answer: 60 s) while prompts keep asking; a failed one's messages go into the next. The session's daemon reader stops its 30-minute check-in only while window hints are proven working for it: a `<sid>.window` marker beside `<sid>.live`, touched only while its harness shows a hint mid-turn (not Kimi Code, whose hints wait for a prompt), its transcript was read in the last minute and its window clock started within 30 minutes, its server and key answered a window lookup as one with no 404 or 422 naming `trigger` since, and fewer than two window lookups in a row failed, its own or its key's. Anything else lets the marker go stale within 2 minutes of being seen, and the check-ins come back: an older service or server at once, an engine outage after two failed window lookups in a row, a turn of tool calls only 30 minutes into it. `probe ask` still wakes the reader at once (reading the newest events while the check-ins are the window's), and an explicit `PROBE_READER_EVERY_S` keeps its check-ins. The proactive paper search went with the check-ins; team-saved papers still come through hints. A lookup names at most 100 records already shown (`exclude_doc_ids`, 50 before) to a server that answered a window lookup, and still 50 to any other, which may be one that refuses more. Plan hints-window-trigger (prod bench over 83 sessions of five teams: 38% of delivered window hints useful, 0.7 delivered per active hour; the check-ins on this box gave 1 useful message in 115 since 10-08).

## 0.314.2
- **A researcher's prompt waits for the daemon writer's least gap like a turn end, as the round-7 plan approved.** 0.314.0 held a prompt back only after the writer's last 3 runs recorded nothing; that rule came from a bench reading that turned out to be noise (the check it lost is flaky on main itself). `probe ask --writer`, a full queue, the session's end and a paused run still start a run at once; the server's `x-probe-writer-prompt-waits` switch still turns it off.

## 0.314.1

- **"No restart needed" is never said for a pi Probe cannot see.** A pi on package 0.6.3 or older writes no shim record, so it was found only by its process title `pi`; its RPC mode (`pi-rpc`) and a pi as macOS `ps` shows it (`node .../pi-coding-agent/.../cli.js`) were missed, and an update could say no restart while such a session ran old code. Both count now. A pin is no longer made `current` when pi's clone moved while it was copied, and the pi package (0.7.1) looks at a turned-down `current` again at the next turn instead of waiting for the next update (a clone read mid-update kept a session on its old version).

## 0.314.0

- **The notes docs describe the server's 1,000-token cap.** The server now caps every note but the team note at 1,000 tokens (research-os, `notes_max_tokens`), and a note already over it must be rewritten under it before its next change. The CLI and SDK read every cap from the server (`notes_limit_tokens`), so the fullness line, the pre-send refusal and the compaction advice follow it with no code change; only the comments in `probe.sdk.notes` and `_notes_write` that quoted the old 30,000 / 2,000 caps changed.
- **The daemon's writer wakes less, re-reads less and runs its helpers on a cheaper model, as the server says (daemon cost round 7).** With the server's settings: a researcher's prompt waits for the writer's least gap like a turn end once the writer's last 3 runs recorded nothing (a loop, not a working session) (`probe ask --writer` still starts a run at once); a writer conversation idle past the model's prompt cache starts fresh from disk instead of re-reading it at the full price; more than 10 new files in a row (a checkout, a build's output) reach the writer as one list of paths, each one open away; `probe daemon task` helpers run on the server's `task` model once it serves one. Every setting is off against an older server. Helpers' model calls now go into the session's trace under the command that started them. New `probe notes find <words> --project|--experiment|--run <slug> [--note <title>]` prints only the paragraphs of a note that mention the words, verbatim with their heading and lines; the daemon writer's edit-notes now finds the paragraph it changes and reads the whole note only to restructure it (the main agent's edit-notes is unchanged).

## 0.313.0

- **pi sessions take a Probe update at their next turn, with no /reload.** pi loads an extension once and `pi update` rewrites its clone in place (`git clean -fdx`, then `npm install`), so an open session ran the old code, or code deleted under it, until /reload. The pi package (0.7.0) now loads through a small shim that never changes (`index.ts`, `src/shim.ts`); the shim runs Probe from a pinned copy of the package (`<state>/pi/pins/<version>-<fingerprint>/`, made by `probe update` after `pi update` finishes, or at the next pi start) and moves an open session to the newest pinned copy between turns, undoing the switch if the new version fails to load. Each pi process writes what it runs (`<state>/pi/live/<pid>.json`), and the update says "open pi sessions switch to it at their next turn, no restart needed" only when every live pi process runs the shim, the new version needs no newer shim and no skill reload, and the Probe service records its transcript; otherwise "run /reload in open pi sessions (or restart them) to apply". A session on pi package 0.6.3 or older needs that one last /reload. Pins a live pi process uses are never pruned. The tap is 0.10.21 (it carries the harness registry, where pi now `follows_updates`).

- **Kimi Code sessions take a Probe update with no restart, where Probe can prove it.** Kimi keeps the plugin manifests (hook entries, skills, MCP servers) it read at its start, and Probe's hooks already hand every event to the newly installed copy (plugin 0.175.0, tap 0.10.18). Now the rest follows too: an old Kimi `tap watch` moves to the Probe service at the next prompt (the prompt hook finds Kimi's installed tap through its `installed.json`), and the Probe service moves onto a newer Kimi tap after an update. Each Kimi process's record now keeps what it loaded at its start (the plugin and tap folders, their versions, and a fingerprint of the manifest parts Kimi keeps, never a token), and "No restart needed" is said for Kimi only when every live Kimi process loaded hand-over-capable releases and the manifests now installed, and the Probe service records its transcript; otherwise the update says "Run /reload in Kimi Code (or restart it) to apply the plugin update." (pi gets the /reload wording too). A session started before this release, or on its own `tap watch` (a sandboxed one), keeps that line until it ends. The tap is 0.10.20 (it carries the harness registry, where Kimi now `follows_updates` with the new `loaded_records` capability). The service's tap copies and the coming pi copies share one helper (`probe._shared.pins`).

## 0.312.0

- **A refused key says so.** When the Probe gateway refuses a session's capture key (401), the Probe service now stamps the tap's 401 latch (`last_401_at` and the refused key's fingerprint in its state db), which the status line, `probe session status` and `probe doctor` already read; the next answer that accepts the same key clears it, and a new key is never latched by an old stamp. Only the tap's old outbox drain wrote it, so a refused key read as "not recording" at best and nobody was told to reconnect (release gate, 2026-10-25). Offline, server errors and a proxy's page change nothing.

- **No `probe` command fails or mixes versions during a machine's first update.** That update is the one-time move to the side-by-side install and runs in place, longer than the 10 s a command waited: `probe session status` and `probe --version` answered "Probe is updating itself" (exit 75) to agents mid-work, and a command that did wait went on with old modules under the new CLI (`module 'probe.service.procid' has no attribute 'exists'`; release gate, 2026-10-25). Every command except a hook's call now waits it out (up to 90 s, under an agent's own 2-minute command limit), then runs again in a fresh interpreter on the new code. A hook's call still answers at once.

- **Per-push CI runs fast logic tests only.** A new `heavy` marker holds back 140 slow end-to-end tests (a spawned service, a real tap, packaged builds; 8–28 s each) from agent-ci; the nightly full-regression still runs them. The temporary release-smoke test that installed CLI 0.309.1 from PyPI to host tap 0.10.19 is removed.

- **The Probe service checks whether it may update the desktop app without asking macOS.** Its "can I write the app?" check used `os.access`, which on macOS makes App Management evaluate the protected bundle; a background caller's ask was refused and logged (seen on a real Mac, 2026-10-25; silent, and the install went on). It now reads the owner and mode bits instead.

- **`read` says what it does: nothing new is filed in Probe, and the conversation is still captured.** The `probe` skill (every copy), its reply templates and `probe state --help` said `read` "records nothing", while the transcript has always been captured in `read` (owner's call, 2026-10-25: keep capturing it). Only `off` stops capture.

- **A CLI below 0.303.0 is told to update.** 0.303.0 carries a security fix (an agent's own shell could approve the daemon's held actions, #3355); every machine whose CLI updates itself has had it for a day, so the manifest's recommended version moves from 0.286.0 to 0.303.0 and the rest see "This Probe CLI is missing a security fix and has stopped updating itself. Run probe wizard --action update in a terminal; if it says a setup is running, restart the computer first."
- **`probe doctor` no longer tells you to restart sessions that already moved, or that move by themselves.** Two of its lines did. The "Last attempt" row repeats what the last update wrote about sessions still on an older tap, and every release before 0.304.0 wrote "N sessions started before the update still run tap X; restart them to switch to Y": after an update from one of those releases, doctor kept printing that until the next update (hours later), although the Probe plugin's prompt hook had handed those sessions to the Probe service, which records them on the newest installed tap. Doctor now prints such a sentence as it stands: gone once no live session runs a tap older than the one it names (each `tap watch`, and each session the service records, on the tap it loaded); "they move to Y at the next prompt, no restart needed", counted afresh, while some still do and every one of them moves by itself (the same rule `probe update` uses: Claude Code or Codex, a user-scope install, not Windows, a tap with the hand-back, the Probe plugin installed for a watcher from before it); word for word otherwise, and whenever the sessions could not be looked at. A sentence that names no agent (a record of one pass) is judged against every agent that captures, not only the one doctor runs for, so a Kimi Code session that does need its restart is still told. The warning for a tap behind the published one ended "a session started before the update keeps running the old copy until it restarts" on every machine; where open sessions follow an update it now says they move to it by themselves, with no restart. Found by the release gate (C8): every machine updating from CLI 0.285.2-0.302.0, and every machine between a tap's publication and its install.
- **The Probe service exits as soon as the last session ends, also when a session's switched-off stretch cannot be settled or its recorder keeps failing.** A session switched off and back on has its off stretch settled (read past) before it is recorded again; while the server refuses the key or cannot be reached, its recorder tries again after 5 s, doubling up to 5 minutes. It waited for its next try on a wake that neither the session's end (`SessionEnd`, `recorders.finish`) nor its agent exiting ever set, so it noticed the end only at that try and kept the service running up to 5 minutes after the last session ended (and a SessionEnd that waited for it got `finished: false`). Now it looks every second during that back-off (a try to settle still waits for the back-off), and the session's end, its agent's exit and `probe capture off` wake it: it finishes the session at once (finalized, or dropped when the server refused it for good, its gap file kept, or, while the server cannot be reached, left for a later service to finish after its last three tries, which stay 2 s apart however often it is woken). A recorder whose passes keep failing (a refused key) whose agent exited made its last tries at the same back-off: they are 2 s apart now too, and a wake ends its wait. Found by the release gate (C8) on a machine whose key the server refuses.
- **Security: another process can no longer end or take over a session to switch off the daemon-session check, nor post into or take from a session's mailbox (#3360, #3361).** Any process of this user reaches the Probe service's socket, the coding agent's own shell among them, and `session.list` names every session's id and generation. That shell could end its own session (`session.end`) or register it again as `inline` (`session.register`), after which `action.run` no longer found the daemon session it runs in and changed the device for it: the machine's default Probe switch, the wizard's configure, sign-out, uninstall. It could also post a message into any session's mailbox, which that session's agent is shown as Probe's (`mailbox.post`), or take another session's messages so they were never shown (`mailbox.claim`). The service now decides by the process the kernel names behind each connection, never by what a request says. A session is ended, given another owner, or moved out of daemon mode only by the process that registered it (its `tap watch`) or by the service itself (a recorder it hosts); anyone else gets `refused` with reason `not_registrant` while that process and the session's agent run. Any other register from another process with the owner unchanged still goes through, as the recorder hand-offs need, but it can no longer move the session's state folder or its report consent. A registration nobody holds any more (a session that was open when the service was updated, one whose registrant exited, or one the service registered and no longer records) is taken up by the next process that registers it. A coding agent's process once registered in daemon mode stays refused until it exits, whatever later registrations say, and is never dropped from that list to make room; every registered session the caller runs under now counts, so a registration forged beside the real one cannot hide it. Only a process that looks like a coding agent (called `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, `kimi` or `kimi-code`, or running pi's, Claude Code's or Codex's package) is remembered this way, so a fake registration naming the desktop app ends with that registration; one naming another running agent still sticks to that agent until it exits. The action's child also resolves the caller's own session from its process, registered or not, as `desktop.request`'s child already did. A mailbox post is accepted only from the session's daemon worker (a worker the service started for that session, or one under the process that registered it), and a claim only from under the session's agent process or from a hook host the service runs; anyone else gets `refused` with reason `not_session`. Every client refused this way already did the step on the files itself, so delivery, capture and the hooks keep working with no restart: an open session's hooks, a worker left from before an update, and an older tap are unaffected or fall back to the files. The guard refuses the agent's shell calling `session.end` or `session.register` itself, as it already refused the mailbox calls, when the command names Probe's service (its client or its socket): the same method names in another protocol (WebDriver BiDi's `session.end`) are not refused. **Two running agents on one session id** (`claude --continue` or `--resume` in a second tab while the first still runs, `codex resume`): the older one now keeps the session until it exits, where before the newer one took it over. The newer one's recorder is refused at each retry (every 2 s), and the service logs that once per session and process every 10 minutes. Capture, message delivery and the daemon check still work for both. Residual, as before: a same-user process that leaves the agent's process tree and clears its environment, or edits the service's files directly, is not stopped by this. An agent that was registered in daemon mode and is then switched to `inline` has its service-routed actions refused until it exits; `probe wizard` then runs the action itself, as on any refusal.
- **The status line says a session is not captured when the server refuses the key.** Its capture reading (`not capturing session transcript: ...`) is local, but the refresh wrote it only after a good read of the session's work from the server, so on a machine whose key the server refuses the segment read a green "tracking" while nothing the session wrote reached the server, and `probe session status` and `probe doctor` said so; offline it froze at the last good read. (Offline, or with the server failing, the session is still captured locally and sent later, so the segment rightly stays "tracking".) The refresh now writes the capture reading whatever the server answers, keeping the project of the last good read (no flicker to "untracked" when the wifi drops). Sessions already open get it at their next prompt (the plugin's hooks follow updates). Found by the release gate (C8).

## 0.311.0

- **Probe off is honoured by every `tap watch`, not just the Probe service (tap 0.10.19).** CLI 0.307.0 stopped the Probe service capturing a session whose switch is `off`, but only inside the service: every `tap watch` process drains every session of the shared journal, so another session's watch (a sandboxed session's, one under `PROBE_TAP_HOSTED=0`, one whose service could not start, or a CLI on Python 3.10, which the service cannot host) still uploaded what an off session wrote, and so did an off session's own watch before it handed the session to the service. Now the tap reads the switch and the session's off stretches itself, in every process: a session that reads `off` (its own `/probe off`, `probe session state off`, or the machine's default) gets no new batch from any drain, the gap sweep never adopts it, and nothing is asked of the server about it; every line written while it was off is read past as nothing, so the server's cursor moves past it and no process running this tap can send it later, its title and the "line too long" placeholder included (a CLI 0.307 to 0.310 service still gates its sessions with its own wraps, which send that placeholder, as before). A session's own watch records its off stretches in the same file the service keeps (`<sid>.gaps` beside the session's state), from where the switch was last seen on, within a second of the move, and closes the stretch when it reads on again, so whichever process records the session next (the service, or another watch) never sends the stretch. If that file cannot be written (a full disk, a read-only folder), the watch keeps the stretch in memory, sends none of it itself and writes it as soon as it can; where the folder cannot be locked at all (no lock daemon on a network folder) it writes without the lock. Once the server has everything past a closed stretch, the watch drops it from the file. The service and a watch can write that file at the same moment during a hand-over: every write now takes the session's lock file (`<sid>.gaps.lock`) and the service merges what a watch wrote instead of writing over it. A watch of a session that is off from its start claims nothing and asks the server nothing, and hands the session to the service, which holds it; one that ends while off is finalized without its off stretch. The service no longer wraps a tap that gates itself; taps 0.10.0 to 0.10.18 are wrapped as before, and CLI 0.307.0's service hosting this tap gates it as it did. Sessions that are already open get it with no restart: those the service records once it loads the new tap, and a `tap watch` started from now on. A `tap watch` process already running an older tap keeps its own code until it ends: it hands its session to the service within about a minute while one runs (taps 0.10.13 and later), is moved at a prompt (older ones), or ends with its session; until then it can still upload an off session's stretch, as can a sandboxed session's older watch for its whole life. A compaction summary written after switching back on can still repeat what was said while off, and a Claude Code resume that copies earlier history into a new session id is not checked. A session whose recorder stopped while it was off (and nothing records it when it is switched back on) sends nothing written after the switch back on until something records it again: that process's first look closes the stretch there, so those lines are skipped, never sent later. `PROBE_TAP_WATCHER_DIR` now names the folder of the tap's watcher files on every operating system (Windows only before), and the tap's hooks, `probe`, the status line and pi all look there; unset, nothing changes.

## 0.310.0

- **A closed desktop app is updated by the Probe service, with no app process started and nothing to click (macOS).** Until now a closed Probe app was skipped by the update cycle (`skipped: app_closed`) and updated itself at its next launch, so the person waited for the update there. Now, when the app's 6-hour update check is due and the app is installed but not running, the service fetches the same `latest.json` the app's own updater reads, picks the entry that updater would pick (`darwin-<arch>-app`, then `darwin-<arch>`), and never installs a version older than or equal to the installed bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`. It downloads the archive next to the bundle (same volume; 10 minutes, each read included, and 256 MB at most; https only) and verifies its minisign signature exactly as the app's updater does, against the same public key (desktop's `tauri.conf.json`, pinned in `appinstall.py`): the key id, `ED` (BLAKE2b-512 of the archive, what Tauri's signer makes) or `Ed`, the global signature over the trusted comment, and the trusted comment's `version:` equal to the announced version (build metadata compared literally, as the semver crate does). It unpacks only plain files, folders and links that stay inside the bundle (every link resolved through any chain of links; no `..`, absolute paths, hard links, devices, setuid bits or duplicate names), checks the bundle id `ai.prbe.desktop`, the version and the executable, and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict -R` against the Probe team's Developer ID (the Developer ID CA intermediate, a Developer ID Application leaf, team `2HDWBQ9P3D`). **The service never renames, swaps or deletes the app's bundle itself**: macOS App Management blocks a change to a notarized app by code not signed by the app's team and notifies the person. The new release's own helper (`Contents/MacOS/probe-swap`, prbe-ai/desktop, signed by the same team) does it, started as its own responsible process (`posix_spawn` with `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`; a macOS without that call fails the step before anything is downloaded, and the app updates itself at its launch): it takes the app's instance lock, checks the app again under it, finds no process running from the app, swaps the bundles in one atomic rename (two journalled renames where the volume cannot swap; the service start and every cycle have the same helper finish a swap stopped halfway, before anything looks for the app), verifies the new app and swaps back if it does not verify or an old copy started meanwhile, and the new app's helper deletes the old bundle (`--remove`) once nothing runs from it, as it does what a stopped removal left (`.deleting`). The service reads the helper's answer by its machine words (`result`, `reason`), never its text, deletes only a staged copy that still holds the new release with nothing running from it, and counts an answer that is not `swapped` as installed when the app already reads the new version only when the answer was lost or an old copy started (never when the new app failed its checks after the swap). The old app is removed right away only after a `swapped` answer; otherwise the sweep looks at it later. The cycle's `app` step event and the app's record carry the helper's answer (`helper: {result, reason, undo_failed}`), and a release its helper refused for a reason that stays the same (`unsigned`, `not_newer`, `not_probe`, `quarantined`) is skipped as `refused_release`, not downloaded again for a week or until another release is the latest. On a volume that cannot swap in one step (a network home), a swap stopped while being undone is put right by the old app's own helper when the new release's helper refuses (the old app goes back in). If an install's undo failed after the new app failed its checks, the service remembers it: the app is never reported current while it fails `codesign`, the same release is installed over it (the helper now repairs an app that fails its signature check with the same version), old bundles are kept until then, and `probe doctor` says to reinstall Probe. A release without the helper (every release before it) is skipped as `no_helper`, not downloaded again, and the app updates itself at its next launch as before; so are a bundle or folder this user cannot write (`not_writable`), a running app or a held instance lock (`app_running`), and macOS refusing the helper's rename (the helper's `not_permitted`, retried after a week). A release found without the helper is remembered until the app is current or installed, or a different latest release appears; a failed check keeps it. Never a prompt. The cycle's `app` step reads `installed` (with `version_before` and `version_after`), `current` or `failed`, `update.status`'s `app.last` says `via: service_install`, and `probe doctor` gains a "Desktop app" row. The app's next launch finds its check done and does not update again. An update an open app downloaded but never installed (the app was killed before its quit) is installed the same way once the app is gone. Someone opening the app during the install gets the app as always (its launch check is handed to it and the staged copy is thrown away); an old copy that starts in the milliseconds of the swap itself opens its window and waits for the instance lock only at its update gate, and the helper swaps back under it. Linux and Windows have no desktop app: their app step is unchanged. `cryptography` is now declared in the `cli` extra (it came only through `mcp`; the service runs only from the CLI's env).

## 0.309.1

- **The desktop app opens even when this computer's workspace limit names a deleted workspace.** The app's account read (`probe desktop request` `profile`) no longer carries the limit, so the API's `workspace_limit_unknown` refusal can no longer lock the person out of the Settings where the limit is changed.

## 0.309.0

- **A fix to the session capture hooks reaches sessions that are already open, at their next event, with no restart (tap 0.10.18).** A coding agent keeps the hooks it loaded when a session started, and each capture hook ran its script from the tap folder of that start, so a tap update reached only new sessions: the Python 3.11 picker of tap 0.10.16 never reached a session that was open when it shipped. From this release, each capture script (session start, the prompt check, turn end, session end) first hands the event to the installed tap's copy of the same script when that is another folder: under Claude Code the one its install ledger lists (a rolled-back release is followed too), under Codex the newest version in Codex's plugin cache, under Kimi Code the one Kimi's plugin list records. It decides without running any program, with regular expressions only (never a shell pattern over the whole list: macOS's bash 3.2 makes those grow much faster than the text), and a move costs one shell start. Measured under bash 3.2, each hook took 3 ms more at an 8 KB install list (20 plugins) and 5 ms more at 37 KB (100 plugins), and 3-5 ms more again when it moves: the session end hook keeps well inside Claude Code's 1.5 s. A copy is taken only when it holds every file its scripts read, and under Codex only once Codex has stopped writing it (5 s). Anything unexpected (no ledger, two copies listed, a copy still being written, a Windows path) runs the event where it is, as before. The hooks.json entries themselves do not change, and are now pinned by a test: Codex trusts each entry by its exact text and skips a changed one until you approve it again in `/hooks`. Sessions that started on tap 0.10.17 or older keep their old scripts until they end (the Probe plugin moves their recording to the Probe service).
- **Kimi Code sessions follow plugin updates, and keep their hooks past the weekly cleanup.** Probe installs each version of a plugin into Kimi as a folder of its own and removed versions older than a week once two newer ones were installed, so a Kimi session open longer than that lost every Probe hook with no word, and no Kimi hook ever ran the installed version. Now a removed version folder is replaced by a link to the version kept, so a session that started on it, including one from before this release, keeps its hooks and runs the kept version's. A session that starts on this release also hands each event to the copy Kimi's plugin list records (the Probe plugins' hook adapter and the capture scripts, the way Claude Code's and Codex's hooks already move), and a hook whose folder is gone altogether runs the newest installed one instead of nothing. Uninstalling removes the links too, and installing a version again makes it a whole folder again.
- **The Probe service records sessions from its own copy of the tap, so a Codex tap update can no longer break it mid-session.** The service imported the tap from the plugin folder the first session named, often Codex's plugin cache, which keeps one version of a plugin and deletes its folder when it installs the next. The tap reads some of its own files long after it starts (modules it loads the first time they are needed, its data files), and those reads failed once the folder was gone. The service now copies the tap package into its own folder (`taps/<version>-<hash>` beside `recorders.json`, made once per tap version and reused) and loads it from there. It keeps the copy in use and the three most recently used, and removes copies unused for a week. If the copy cannot be made (a full disk), it loads the tap where it is, as before, and says so in `service.log`.

- **Limit Probe on a computer to one workspace.** `probe workspace limit <workspace>
  [--team-items show|hide]` makes the CLI, SDK runs, the Probe daemon, the Probe service
  and the Probe MCP on this computer read only that workspace (keys and permissions are
  unchanged; anyone on the computer can change it); `--team` sees the whole team again and
  `probe workspace limit` shows the current setting. Every API request and every MCP header
  copy (Claude Code's helper, Codex, Kimi Code, pi) carries `X-Probe-Workspace-Limit`, and
  the hosted MCP forwards it. `PROBE_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=<id|slug>` (or `team`) limits one job.
  While limited, `probe workspace use` / `project use` will not move this computer's
  workspace elsewhere, "not found" says when the limit hid something, and with team-wide
  items hidden the team note leaves CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md. `probe status --json` adds
  `account.workspace_limit`; the Probe service gains the `workspace_limit` action and the
  desktop interface the `workspaces` op (every workspace, listed without the limit); the
  capture tap's copy of the service protocol carries the two new names. A Codex signed in
  through the plugin's own OAuth stays unlimited (rewriting its entry would sign it out);
  `probe workspace limit` says so and names the fix.

## 0.308.0

- **Where a Probe hint serves the session, the daemon reader no longer takes a turn at each prompt; everywhere else it still does, and its check-ins read the work now.** The Probe service's hint lane touches a small marker for every session it can hint (followed by the service's recorder, a key from the session's own CLI config, the server neither refusing that key nor lacking the hints route), at most every 30 seconds. The session's daemon counts hints as live while that marker is under 120 seconds old, says so on every chat request (`x-probe-hints-live: on | off`), and skips the reader's prompt turn only when hints are live and the server agreed (`x-probe-reader-prompt-wake: off`). A session no hint serves (Probe's `read` mode, a sandboxed one, `PROBE_HINTS=off`, an environment with its own Probe key or address, a stopped service) keeps the reader's turn at each prompt, and goes back to it within 2 minutes of hints stopping. With prompt turns off, nothing reads a busy session's backlog turn by turn any more, so a check-in or an answer to `probe ask` reads the newest window of events (400 events at most) and older unread ones drop off, instead of reading a window that could fall hours behind. `PROBE_READER_PROMPT_WAKE=on` or `off` on the machine still wins.

## 0.307.0

- **Probe off now stops the Probe service capturing the session.** Switching a session `off` (`/probe off`, `probe session state off`, or a machine default of `off`) stopped Probe's calls and the daemon, but its transcript kept uploading. Now the Probe service holds an off session instead of recording it, and none of its own recorders send the stretch written while off. Switching back to `on` or `read` captures from when the service sees it (at once from `/probe` or `probe session state`, up to a minute when nothing tells the service, as on Windows or for a machine default; lines written in between are skipped); the off stretch is never sent later (the server's record skips it as nothing). The stretch is kept in a small file beside the session's state (`<sid>.gaps`), so a service restart, a pruned `.state` or a later resume does not send it either, and `probe import` skips a session switched off itself or with a stretch written while off (a machine default of `off` skips nothing there). A session that ends while off is finalized without the stretch, retried by later services while the server cannot be reached, and dropped when it is refused for good (no login on the machine, or the Probe gateway itself answering 401, 403, 404 or 422; a proxy's refusal, any other status and a momentary failure are retried), its stretch still unsent; one that never sent anything sends nothing. This reaches sessions already open when the update lands, with no restart. An off session keeps no service running: the service no longer answers it `owner_gone` and gets asked again every minute, and the background keeper no longer restarts the service for it. `probe session status`, `probe doctor`, the status line and pi's `/probe-status` say "not capturing session transcript: Probe is off"; pi's footer says "off". Until the next tap update the off stretch can still be uploaded by another session's `tap watch` process, by an older tap's own `tap watch` until it hands the session to the service, and for any session the Probe service does not record (sandboxed, `PROBE_TAP_HOSTED=0`, no service or a service backing off, Python 3.10 CLIs), which `tap watch` records instead; a compaction summary written after switching back on can repeat what was said while off. With taps up to 0.10.17 an off session's start still starts the service once; it goes idle at once. `read` is unchanged: its transcript still uploads.

## 0.306.0

- **Probe staff can ask your machine to update, and it does, with nothing for you to run.** When the Probe team asks one of your machines to update (for example after its automatic updates got stuck), the server says so on the answers to requests the CLI already makes. The CLI notes it, and its next `probe` command hands an update to the machine's own updater: the Probe service where it updates (macOS, Linux), else the CLI's own updater, now even when every `probe` command comes from a coding agent's hooks and never a terminal. At most once every 15 minutes while the request stands, never from a run-scoped command (`probe log`, `probe exec`, ...), never into a run that holds the update lock, never while automatic updates are off, and the updater's own deferrals still apply; without the Probe service (Windows, pip installs), where the update lands in place, also never from a command a Probe daemon runs or while a daemon is recording. Silent: it prints nothing. Older servers never ask, and nothing changes.

## 0.305.0

- **Writes set aside with `probe outbox discard` are no longer deleted by the outbox's cleanup.** A job that ran with its own `PROBE_TOKEN` queues its writes in a folder of their own, and that folder is deleted once it has been idle for an hour. Writes discarded from it stayed inside it, so they were deleted with it, by this release's cleanup and by every older one's, including an older SDK in a training job's own environment. Discards now go to the outbox's main `discarded/` folder, which nothing deletes. The cleanup never deletes a folder that still holds discards, and moves at most 1,000 of them each time a background sender starts, so a large old backlog never holds up delivery (the background rescue moves the rest). A move cut short, or two at once, never leaves a write under two names. The background rescue that the CLI starts now also starts when such a folder holds discards, and moves them to the main folder, so writes an older release set aside are kept from then on. A request's tombstone in a receipt folder stays where its recovery reads it.

- **Throwing writes away is reported.** `probe outbox discard` (`--held`, `--held --credential`, or dead letters) sends one `outbox.discarded` event with the reason, how many writes, uploads and bytes, how many closed a run, how many credentials, and how many were queued on each of the last 14 days. It never sends a fingerprint, a path or a write's content, and it says which coding agent ran the command, if one did. Moving older discards to the main folder sends the same event with the reason `relocated`. A program that sets requests aside with `discard_delivery` counts them in its delivery summary (`discarded`) instead of sending an event each. Like every outbox event, nothing is sent with `PROBE_TELEMETRY=off`, to a self-hosted server, or when the writes were going to more than one server.

- **A refused credential with no writes left no longer says "auth-blocked".** When a revoked token's writes left the outbox any other way than delivery (a discard, an older release's cleanup), its refusal stayed on record. Every `probe` command then printed "auth-blocked since … sign in again", `probe doctor` showed it, the background rescue kept looking, and `outbox.stuck` was reported every six hours for a queue with nothing in it. A queue with no writes waiting (none in `ops/`, no multipart upload) now reads with no refusal and nothing held, each queue on its own before the outbox's totals are added up. `probe outbox discard --held` also forgets the refusal of a credential whose writes it all set aside. A credential that queues writes again is refused at most once more.
