The wait is kept in the transcript journal, so it holds across restarts and for every recorder on the machine (`tap watch` and the Probe service's), and it belongs to that session alone: other sessions keep uploading at their usual pace. It ends when the server accepts the batch or the batch changes. Protocol restarts, deleted sessions and every other error are handled as before, and `probe import` still tries such a batch once per run.

- **pi's tool guard asks the Probe service first (pi package 0.6.0).** Before a `bash`, `write`, `edit` or Probe MCP call runs, pi sends it to the Probe service, which runs the same pre-tool hooks Claude Code runs (from the Probe plugin that ships beside pi's package, in the service's warm hook host: about 20 ms a call) and refuses it when they do, in the same words. So pi now also refuses what only Claude Code refused before, such as a `probe` write typed into the shell of a session set to `read`. pi's built-in guard still runs on every call and its own refusals always stand, so the service only adds refusals; when the service gives no clear answer within 300 ms (not running, a CLI from before this release, a hook that failed), the built-in guard decides alone, exactly as before. A session set to `off` never contacts the service. New Probe service method `hooks.run` (API v1, additive): runs one hook event for a Probe plugin folder and returns its merged output.
- **Tap 0.10.1.** Ships the tap's `tap service socket` command that pi's guard uses to find the Probe service (the tap code merged under 0.10.0, so existing installs had not received it).

## 0.287.1

- **`probe wizard --action configure --agent codex --reinstall` no longer crashes on a real install.** The repair edits Codex's `config.toml` with `tomlkit`, which was used since 0.277.0 but declared nowhere, so every installed CLI failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomlkit'` (the test environments had it for another reason). It is now a dependency, and a test fails the build when the CLI side imports a package the CLI does not declare.

- **The Claude Code status line no longer replaces a `settings.json` it cannot parse.** Installing the status line read a file with a JSON error (a trailing comma typed by hand) as empty and saved that back: the file became just the status line, losing env tokens, permission rules and hooks, and the `.probe-backup` (taken only once) did not hold the newer contents. It now leaves such a file, or one it cannot read, untouched and says why (`probe statusline install` exits 1; the wizard reports it and goes on).

## 0.287.0

- Report completed update stages through the existing JSON step stream so the desktop app can show update percentage inside its button. Failed CLI or integration stages remain failures; only the final completed result finishes progress.

## 0.286.1

- **pi's `settings.json`, Claude Code's `settings.json` and Codex's `config.toml` stay symlinks when Probe edits them, and keep their permissions.** After 0.285.1 fixed CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, two more writers still replaced a symlinked file with a plain one: installing, removing or switching Probe in pi's `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, and the integration repair (`--reinstall`) restoring plugin on/off flags in Claude Code's `settings.json` or Codex's `config.toml`. Both now write to the file the link points at. Probe's edits of these files, of the status line settings and of CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md now keep the file's permission bits (a `0600` file is no longer left `0644`, and a repair no longer forces `0600` onto Claude Code's settings or onto a dotfiles `config.toml`; `~/.codex/config.toml` itself is still tightened to `0600`), and go through a uniquely named temporary file instead of a fixed name beside the file. Saving Probe's MCP sign-in token into Codex's `config.toml` still replaces a symlinked file rather than writing through it (a `~/.codex` folder that is itself a link is not covered).

## 0.286.0

- **The Probe service records your sessions itself (tap 0.10.0).** Each agent session used to get its own recorder process (`tap watch`, with a shell wrapper around it); now SessionStart asks the Probe service, which records the session on a thread of its own: the same recorder code, one process for the whole machine, warm, with the session's own environment, log file and daemon worker. A service restart (an update, a newer recorder plugin) pauses every recorder and the next service picks each one up where it left off: nothing is uploaded twice and the session's daemon worker hands over to the next one instead of ending the session. One recorder per session still: a session whose own `tap watch` is still running is left to it. `probe status` reads such a session as captured; if the service is gone (a crash), the next prompt or turn end starts it again. Where it cannot (Windows, a session with no known agent process, an older Probe service, or `PROBE_TAP_HOSTED=0`), `tap watch` records as before. Only Probe's own settings and credentials, and where files and the network are, are passed to the service; an agent's own credentials are not.
- **CLI updates install beside the running version, and switch back if the new one will not run.** An update now installs the new CLI as its own environment next to the running one, checks it starts, and switches the tool path to it in one rename; a run or a daemon worker keeps the version it started on, so updates no longer wait for them. The first such update on a machine waits for a quiet moment once (it moves the existing install aside). A guard then starts the new Probe service and watches it for a minute: if it will not start, crashes or answers as another version, the machine switches back, and that version is skipped until a newer release. `uv tool list` no longer lists the CLI once an update has switched it (uv skips a tool folder that is a link); `probe update` and `probe --version` are unaffected.
- **If the Probe service stops while it records, the system starts it again.** On Linux a systemd user timer, on macOS a launchd agent, runs a one-second check every minute: when a session the service recorded still has its agent running and no service answers (a crash, an out-of-memory kill), it starts the service, which picks every session up where it left off. The prompt and turn-end hooks do the same sooner. Installed by the service itself, only for the account's own home folder and only where a user manager or GUI session exists; Uninstall removes it; `PROBE_SERVICE_KEEPER=0` keeps it off.
- **Hooks start faster.** The Probe plugin's hooks run in a warm process the Probe service keeps for each plugin folder (forked per event, with the event's own environment, folder and output), instead of a fresh Python per event; an event the warm host cannot take within 300 ms runs as before, and never twice. A caller inside an agent's sandbox is never hosted (its event runs where it is).

## 0.285.2

- **The daemon profile's guard holds up when a session tries to slip past it.** A red-team of the released guard found two ways a coding agent the Probe daemon records for could get around it: writing Probe's own per-session state files (`<id>.state`, `<id>.inline`) to forge `on (inline)` and switch the guard off, and running a refused command through a shell form the hook does not read as `probe` (`eval`, `$(echo probe)`, a renamed copy, a Python import). Two fixes: (1) the hook now refuses a tool call that writes into Probe's per-session state folder, the same tripwire it already uses for the daemon's question folder; (2) the CLI itself now refuses, in a daemon-profile session, exactly what the hook refuses (a read, write or removal of the team's records), so a command that rebuilds its own name is still caught once it actually runs `probe`. The daemon's own calls, a run's own writes, `--directed` writes, `session initialize` and the commands with their own refusals (the switch, `mcp call|tools`) are unaffected. Both stay tripwires, not boundaries: the server-side key is the real limit. pi's guard follows.

## 0.285.1

- **A CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md symlinked into a dotfiles repo stays a symlink.** Probe writes its section (and the team note) by writing a new file and swapping it into place, which replaced a symlink such as `~/.codex/AGENTS.md -> ~/.agents/AGENTS.md` with a plain file on the first write, so the machine quietly stopped following the repo and the next team-note sync undid any re-link. The wizard, the team-note sync and the opt-out now write to the file the link points at (a link whose file is missing gets it created there). To repair a machine already hit: move the Probe sections into the repo copy if you want them, then re-create the link.

## 0.285.0

- **A machine that always has a Probe daemon recording still updates.** The Probe service used to wait for every daemon-recorded session to end before it updated the CLI, so a machine that always had one never updated. Now, when a newer CLI is out, it holds new daemon workers back, asks each live session's worker to hand over at its next safe point (it finishes the model round it is in; its queue stays in its store), updates, and the recorder starts the workers again on the new version. When the CLI is already current it updates the plugins only and leaves the workers alone. The worker of a session that has ended is never cut short: it finishes its queue first. A worker that will not stop within 10 minutes, a training run, or one of the service's own actions still defers the update, but none of them for more than 24 hours: after a day the update goes ahead in place, as Probe's updater did before the service. A pip or pipx install the service cannot start from keeps the old updater.
- **One Probe service per machine, also when machines share a home folder.** On a cluster whose nodes share one home folder, only one node got a service and it could not see the others' sessions. The service's folder, socket and locks now live under `~/.local/state/probe/service/<machine key>/`, keyed by a hash of the OS's machine id (Linux `/etc/machine-id`, the Mac's hardware UUID), so every node runs its own. Clients from before this change (a session started earlier, a desktop app not yet updated) still reach it at the old socket.
- **An agent the Probe daemon records can no longer change Probe's settings through the service by leaving its session out of the request.** The service now checks who is calling: the caller's process ancestry against the sessions it tracks, and, on Linux, the caller's own session variables (which a detached `nohup`/`setsid`/`tmux` job keeps). Switching who records, signing out, uninstalling and updating are refused from inside a daemon-recorded session; any other session is named to the action, so it refuses what it refuses there.
- **The stored sign-in goes only where it was meant to.** An action or status read through the service runs with a `base_url` (or `PROBE_BASE_URL`) only when it is https and the endpoint the CLI's current sign-in is for (or Probe's hosted API when it names none); anything else is refused and the desktop app runs the CLI itself.
- **Scheduled updates work behind proxies and package mirrors, and find agents installed with nvm or volta.** The service reads the login shell's proxy, certificate, package-index and agent-folder settings, and its PATH, fresh for each update (and its PATH for each action), the way the desktop app does. Nothing read is stored or logged.
- **A hook no longer times out waiting for an update.** A `probe` command waits for an update in progress for at most 10 seconds, and now at most until the deadline of the hook that started it.
- **Sessions with their own `XDG_STATE_HOME` are seen by the updater.** A session tells the service its state folder when it registers, and the service looks for running setups, runs and daemon workers there too.
- **The Probe service always runs; it has no off switch (tap 0.9.25).** `PROBE_SERVICE` and the config's `"service"` key are no longer read anywhere: `probe.service.client.enabled()` and the client's `--if-enabled` flags are gone, `tap watch` always registers its session, pi always starts the service at `session_start`, and the CLI and the plugin's SessionStart hook always ask the service to update on POSIX (the old detached updater stays the fallback where the service cannot run). A session whose Probe mode is `off` still never starts or holds it. With the service on, agent sessions register with it, the desktop app's Active agents column fills in from its live-session registry, and it is the machine's one automatic updater (only on a quiet machine: no daemon-recorded session, run, setup or action in progress). Tests never reach a real service: the agent suite's HOME is a throwaway folder with no `runtime.json`, and the tap suite stubs `service_link.start`.
- **A Codex session left open across Probe updates now runs the newest installed hooks.** Codex fixes a session's plugin folder when it starts, so a Codex session kept open for days went on running the guard and hooks of the release it started with, while Claude Code sessions already moved to the installed copy. The dispatcher now hands each Codex event to the newest version of the same plugin in Codex's own plugin cache (by version number; only a whole copy, with Codex's manifest, beside the session's own folder and inside that cache). Nothing to approve: the hook entries are unchanged.
- **The recorder plugin has one SessionEnd hook, the one that waits for the last upload (tap 0.9.25).** Every Probe plugin now keeps exactly one hook entry per event. The recorder had two for SessionEnd: the original quick one, kept only because Codex re-asks approval for any changed entry, and the one that waits up to 15s for the session's final delivery. The quick one is gone. Claude Code needs nothing. A Codex user who had approved only the old entry must approve the remaining one once: in Codex, type `/hooks` and approve the Probe Research hooks; `probe status` says when this is needed (and `probe status --json` carries it for the desktop app).
- **`probe status` says when Codex is not running Probe's hooks.** Codex silently skips a hook it has not approved, so a Probe update that changes a hook entry turns it off with nothing in the session to say so. Where Probe's Codex plugins are installed, `probe status` now asks Codex itself (the answer `probe doctor` reads), at most once every 10 minutes and for at most 2s, again after a Probe update or a change to Codex's settings, and prints a "Codex hooks" line telling you to type `/hooks` in Codex and approve Probe's hooks. `--json` gains `codex_hooks` (`state`: approved, needs_approval, unknown or none; the waiting hook keys; when Codex answered; and the newest Codex session that expected Probe's hooks and never ran them, read from the hooks' own heartbeat files when Codex cannot be asked).
- **On Windows, the recorder and pi no longer try to start the Probe service (tap 0.9.25).** The service runs on macOS and Linux only for now (it listens on a Unix socket), so every Windows session tried, and failed, to start it. Capture on Windows works as before.
- **The desktop app's Overview says why it has no live session counts.** "The local live-session registry is unavailable" now says what is going on and what to do: the Probe service is not running (it starts with the next coding-agent session, or run `probe service start`), is starting, is installing an update, refused the request (and why), did not answer, or does not run on this system yet. `desktop request` `delivery` also returns this as `serviceState`.

## 0.284.1

- **An agent the Probe daemon records for is told it can look at its own runs.** The Probe section in its CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md and the guard's refusal said "you only instrument your runs", so the agent kept asking the daemon about runs it had launched itself, though 0.284.0 opened reading one run by its id. Both now name `probe run get <id>` (the block also `probe metrics plot <id>`); the daemon does all other reads and writes. Installed blocks are rewritten the next time the hooks sync the team note (pointer version 47); pi's guard follows.

## 0.284.0

- **An agent the Probe daemon records for can run Probe's own upkeep again, and read its runs.** The daemon plugin's guard refused every `probe` command outside a short list that had gone stale, so `probe update --check`, `probe wizard --action update`, `probe service status` and `probe token list` were refused although none touches the team's work. The list now holds Probe's own upkeep (`update`, `status`, `service`, `outbox drain|retry|watch`, `flush`, `token list`, `context show`, `statusline status|show`, `notes sync`, `agent-rules refresh`, `workspace list|get`, `draft edit`, `file preview`, ...), plus the wizard's update and diagnose with no flag that changes a setting. The agent can also read one run by its id: `run get|series|metrics|inputs|upstream|reproduce`, `get`, `bundle`, `events`, `metrics wide|plot|export|grouped`, `span list|get`, `trial list|get`, `artifact tree|versions` and `snapshot-show` (not `run reproduce --materialize|--export`). Still the daemon's or the researcher's: listing and searching the team's records, writing them (naming or filing a run included), deleting anything, signing in or out, switching the context, workspace or project the daemon records into, minting or revoking tokens, discarding, pausing or resuming queued writes, the team's permissions and workspaces, the MCP token, the status line's install, the daemon's own commands and ledger, `deny` and the switch. A command word the guard cannot read, or one added later, stays refused until a test sorts it. pi's guard follows. Sessions pick it up when they start or restart.

## 0.283.1

- **A session deleted from your machine after you approved an import no longer fails it.** Claude Code deletes transcripts nobody has opened for 30 days (`cleanupPeriodDays`), silently, after any session starts, so a sweep that ran between review and upload left the import unable to open the approved file: the session failed with "reviewed snapshot: local transcript access failed (FileNotFoundError, errno 2)", the job stopped, and the "Session import stopped" email said to resume, which could never work. Such a session is now a skip in background and foreground imports alike, reported as "N removed from this machine before upload (nothing sent)", and counts toward the import's progress, so the import finishes. It stays a failure when the error names another file, when the folder that held the file is gone too (an unmounted drive, a moved config directory), when the absence cannot be proved (a permission error), or when an upload of the session is still in progress (sent but not finished, or staged to send), so those still stop the import and reach you.

## 0.283.0

- Derive desktop/service configure agents from the shared harness registry, including canonical status ids and every installable agent's aliases.

## 0.282.0

- **A folder import whose files were redacted on upload now finishes.** Uploads replace credential-shaped spans before they are hashed, so such a file lands under its redacted digest, and the import's receipt check, which compared it with the approved file's hash, failed it on every run ("Delivery receipt does not match the approved file, bytes and destination"). Every outbox receipt for an upload with an expected hash now carries the digest of the source its snapshot was read from (`source_content_hash`, taken from that same read, so a file edited and reverted mid-staging can never be stamped as approved), and the import accepts the approved file's redaction as delivered. Receipts from before this release carry no stamp; they were held to the same check at staging and are accepted on the next resume, without uploading again. The project-summary step accepts the same receipts; its text excerpts are redacted with the upload's own check before they reach the drafting model, which is given the stored file's hash, never the original's.
- **A word like "Token" or "password" inside a JSON value no longer masks the next field (tap 0.9.24).** The key-name rules let the gap before `:` run on into the next key, so a glossary such as `[{"term": "Token"}, {"term": "Amazon US"}]` uploaded with "Amazon US" replaced by `<redacted:anchored-secret>`, and a transcript row `{"input": "...forgot password should", "output": "..."}` lost its whole output. The gap no longer leaves a value that is closed by `"}`, `",` or `"],` with more words in it, and never crosses a line. A name/value pair is still caught: a name that runs on past the keyword (`{"name": "DB_PASSWORD_PROD", "value": "..."}`), and a label with words after it (`"Password for DB"`, `"API Key (prod)"`, an AWS tag's `"Key"`) when the next key is a value slot (`value`, `string_value`, `data`, `val`, `default`/`defaultValue`), quoted or not, before `:` or `=`. A value that merely ends in the keyword (`"I forgot my password", "output": ...`) is still masked. Copies already uploaded keep the masked text.

## 0.281.0

- **Capy support is removed.** The installer no longer finds, offers or configures Capy; `--agent capy`, `--capy-project` and `probe capy connect/status/setup` are gone, as are the Capy thread sync, the tap's Capy catch-up (tap 0.9.23), the `capy` skills profile and the mirror's `capy/` plugin folder. `probe wizard --action recorder --who-records daemon --json` no longer gives an agent with no daemon profile a result row (its row could never be ok), so the run reads `complete: true` and the Mac app's recording step no longer ends "Setup did not finish". A machine that connected Capy capture is cleaned up on its own, by the old timer's next `probe capy sync` (and `probe capy disconnect`), the next `probe wizard --action update`, or signing out: the Capy capture credential is revoked with the server it was paired to, `~/.local/state/probe/capy` (the saved Capy key and thread mirror) and Capy's upload journal are deleted, and the launchd agent / systemd timer is removed. It never deletes a folder an environment variable names, and never fails an update. A crontab line you added by hand stays yours to delete (`crontab -e`), and so does what you set up inside Capy: its Probe plugin, a `PROBE_TOKEN` (revoke that token too) and the Capy API key you gave Probe. Sessions already uploaded stay in Probe.

## 0.280.0

- Include the explicitly selected daemon’s scoped credential in the desktop’s existing one-use sign-in exchange, avoiding a second browser approval during app installation. Inline installs keep their existing grant set.

## 0.279.0

- Report signing out of a machine as `wizard.signed_out` (`probe wizard` › Account, `--action logout`, the Mac app's Sign out, `probe logout`), attributed to the person by pinning the identity before the token is revoked. `wizard.install_settled` now names the run's `agents`, the `agents_added` it installed, and `was_configured` (Probe was installed on the device before the run; a sign-in alone does not count), so a coding agent added to a set-up machine can be announced once.

## 0.278.0

- Add approved transcript producer IDs and a separate live activity stream to desktop backfills. Keep the newest 200 public progress/state changes with timestamps, credential redaction and explicit truncation; retain final reports separately and never expose raw worker stdout/stderr. Older workers provide their current progress snapshot without invented history.

## 0.277.0

- Add explicit selected-agent integration reinstall through Configure `reinstall: true` and `probe wizard --reinstall`. Repair refreshes only the current profile's owned plugin files, preserves disabled capture/tracking and all recorder/account/default settings, and reports incomplete failures with safe retry recovery. Local/custom pi packages and non-owned plugin registrations remain untouched; repair telemetry uses its own event family.
## 0.276.0

- Automatically hand the current conversation to inline recording when the daemon receives a confirmed budget-exhausted response. Read-only conversations stay read-only, active daemon work stops, and resumes keep the handoff without changing new-session defaults. Updated hooks, pi, and tap explain the change and prevent stale supervisors from repeatedly restarting a read-only daemon.
- Let the desktop acknowledge a fully completed installation to the dashboard through a bounded, authenticated request pinned to the signed-in account and team. Retries preserve onboarding flow and cannot skip earlier website setup.

## 0.275.0

- Respect desktop telemetry privacy through a boolean-only CLI policy read and fixed Finder environment imports. Human desktop actions keep existing wizard/import event names with explicit desktop provenance across service actions and background import workers; noninteractive prompting and automated updater attribution stay unchanged.
- Add `probe desktop request --json` for the native management app: account-scoped backfill history, reviewed session prefixes and folders, durable background start/resume/cancel, authenticated profile reads, and live local agent counts. Desktop admission shares the setup lock; old reviews cannot follow an account or workspace switch. Delivery receipts remain explicitly unknown when unavailable.

## 0.274.0

- **`probe.core`: the desktop app's actions and status as one library, and `python -m probe.core.run <action>` to run one as a child process** (Probe service, step 1). `probe.core.configure(request, sink)`, `recorder`, `logout`, `uninstall`, `update`, `session_default(state, sink)` and `status(refresh=False)` take small typed requests (`agents` claude|codex|pi with `tracking`/`capture`/`auto_update`/`agent_rules`, each true, false or left out, and left out means what the flag left out means to `probe wizard --yes`: on for a fresh device, kept as it is on a configured one, so a request that does not name capture never turns it back on; `who_records` agent|daemon; `state` on|read|off) and call today's code: each action is `probe wizard --action <a> --yes --json` with exactly the flags the app passes, and `status` is `probe status --json`, which now calls it. `python -I -m probe.core.run <action>` reads the request as one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin, to its end (empty means `{}`; an unknown or repeated field, a wrong type, an unknown word, bytes that are not UTF-8 or nesting too deep to read is refused, exit 2, never ignored; a request built in Python is checked the same way), writes the same NDJSON events v1 on stdout with `done` last (`status`: the `probe status --json` object, byte for byte), sends everything else to stderr, and exits as the wizard does (0, 1, 2, 75 while another setup runs, 130 when stopped during a browser approval). `session_default` runs `probe session default` itself, so it keeps that command's refusal from inside a session the Probe daemon records, and reports a `result` row with the default a new session now gets. Every wizard action is refused (exit 2, nothing changed) from inside a session the Probe daemon records, as that profile's guard refuses `probe wizard`; the researcher's terminal, the app and the Probe service carry no such session. `import probe.core` loads no typer, prompt toolkit, HTTP client or `probe.cli`. The event module moved to `probe.core.events`; `probe.cli.json_events` is the same module, and the wire format is unchanged. Terminal output is unchanged, byte for byte.
- **The Probe service (behind `PROBE_SERVICE=on`, off by default): one light process per user per machine, started by the first agent session and gone a few seconds after the last.** `python -m probe.service` (never through the `probe` entry point) serves JSON-RPC 2.0 lines on `~/.local/state/probe/service/service.sock` (0600 in a 0700 folder, fixed under `$HOME` whatever `XDG_STATE_HOME` says; a path over 100 bytes moves to `/tmp/probe-<uid>/service-<hash>.sock`), holds `service.lock` for life (a second instance exits 0 at once), stays in `discovering` for 15 s after start, then exits 5 s after nothing holds it: a session whose mode is not `off` and whose owner runs, or a client that said `keepalive` (the desktop app's window). Owners are `{pid, start_time}` (a recycled pid is a dead owner) watched by the kernel (pidfd on Linux, kqueue on macOS, a 2 s poll elsewhere), or heartbeat-only with a 120 s TTL; a higher `generation` replaces a session's owner, a lower one is refused. The registry is kept in `sessions.json`, so a restarted service knows its live sessions at once. Methods: `service.hello` (first on every connection), `service.status`, `service.stop`, `session.register|end|list`, `events.subscribe` (`session.started`, `session.ended`, `service.stopping`), `status.get`, `action.*` and `update.*` (below). The start path imports the standard library and its own modules only (about 65 ms of imports, 25 MB RSS after 100 requests on the devbox), and the peer's uid is checked where the platform says it (SO_PEERCRED, LOCAL_PEERCRED). API v1 is pinned in `probe.service.protocol`.
- **The Probe service runs the desktop app's actions: `action.run|status|events|cancel`.** `action.run {action, params, client_request_id, context?, base_url?}` checks `params` as `python -m probe.core.run` does (strict), answers `{action_id}` before any work, and runs the action as a `probe.core.run` child with the CLI's own interpreter, the request JSON on stdin and its NDJSON events streamed to subscribers (`action.event`, `action.done`). One action at a time: a second gets `busy` naming the holder. Everything is journaled to `~/.local/state/probe/service/actions/<action_id>.jsonl`, so `action.status` and `action.events {since}` answer after a lost connection or a service restart; the same `client_request_id` within 24 h returns the existing action instead of running it twice; an action whose child died with the service reads as `error{interrupted, "service stopped"}` + `done{ok: false, complete: false, exit_code: null}`, and a child that outlived its service (a stop never kills one: plain `Popen` children, not asyncio's, whose transport SIGKILLs a running child as the service exits from Python 3.13) still holds the slot until it exits. An `accepted` line that cannot be journaled refuses the action. `action.cancel` sends SIGINT only while the action waits for a browser approval (`device_prompt`), else it is refused (`writing`); `action.status.cancelled` is true only when the child then exits 130 (it ignores a SIGINT that misses the wait). The child's environment is the service's clean one plus the request's `context` (a fixed set of variables, the desktop app's: where Probe and the agents keep their files, proxies, TLS trust, package indexes, plus each agent's session-id variable, which a request from inside a session must name so `probe.core.run` refuses there what it refuses) and `base_url`, never the launcher's tokens; the context is never journaled. An `update` action reports as `trigger` (default `manual`), and when it moved the CLI the service restarts as after a cycle. An action in progress keeps the service alive, `service.stop` is refused while one runs, and a restart for a new CLI waits for it.
- **`status.get` reads from a `probe.core.run status` child, cached 30 s per request context** and refreshed after any session start or end, any action and any update cycle; `refresh: true` runs the slow checks (`probe status --refresh`), `max_age: 0` a fresh child without them. `probe.core.run version` (new) prints the CLI version a fresh process imports.
- **The Probe service is the machine's one automatic updater while it is on.** After its discovery window if the last check is 6 h old, then every 6 h, and on `update.check_now`, and only while automatic updates are on: (1) one `probe.core.run update` (the wizard's Update, which moves the CLI's uv tool env and every agent's plugins and pi's package), only on a quiet machine -- no daemon worker holding its session lock and no live session registered in daemon mode (a session with `XDG_STATE_HOME` keeps its lock out of the service's sight), no run lock, no `wizard.lock`, no action of its own -- checked, then `update.barrier` raised, then checked again; the barrier names the update child once it runs, so a service stopped mid-update leaves it up until the child is done; (2) the desktop app, when `Probe.app` (`/Applications` or `~/Applications`) is `ai.prbe.desktop` with `ProbeBackgroundUpdate` in its Info.plist, has been opened once (no `com.apple.quarantine`, else `quarantined`) and is not running: `open -n -g -j <app> --args --background-update`, then the app's `app-update.json` for this attempt, 12 min at most (a `current` with an error is an app that found itself already running: `running`, asked again next cycle); (3) when the CLI version moved, the service finishes, says `service.stopping{update}` and exits, and the next `ensure` starts the new code. A busy machine defers step 1 (`update.deferred`, a skip `probe doctor` shows, a retry 2 s after a session ends and again at 4, 8 ... s up to 15 min while its worker drains, and every 15 min after). A running cycle keeps the service alive for at most 10 min. Every module the cycle needs is imported before step 1 replaces the files. `update.check_now {trigger}` names what asked (`app`, `cli`, `session`, `schedule`), recorded as given and reported to the server as `session_start` or `cli`. Events `update.started|step|deferred|done`; `update.status`; `probe service status` prints the updater's state. `probe.cli.autoupdate` is now `probe._shared.autoupdate` (the same module under both names), so the service never imports the CLI.
- **`probe` and `probe daemon worker` wait for the update barrier.** While the service's update step runs, a `probe` start waits up to 10 s before importing anything of the CLI, then exits 75 (`probe daemon worker`: 5, so the tap respawns it later); the update's own child processes pass. One `stat` when no update runs. A worker looks again once it holds its session lock, so one that passed the barrier just before it went up never starts recording under the update.
- **With `PROBE_SERVICE=on`, the CLI and the plugin hook ask the service instead of spawning an updater.** The CLI's update spawns (the every-command check, pi's session start, a run's end) run `python -I -m probe.service.client check-now --wait-for-pid <the command>` detached, which sends it once the asking command has exited (as the old spawn's wait did); the plugin's SessionStart hook runs `probe service check-now --trigger session` and falls back to `probe wizard --action update --yes` when that fails (an older CLI, or a service that does not start), but not on 75 (the barrier: an update is running). The Probe service's folder is private to the daemon's shell, like the approvals board. New: `probe service check-now [--trigger]`. Nothing changes with the switch off.
- **`probe.service.client`: `ensure()`, `register()`, `end()`, `call()`.** `ensure` connects, or takes `start.lock`, tries again and spawns the CLI's own interpreter (`runtime.json`, which every CLI start from the uv tool env now writes when it changed; else the uv tool path) detached with a clean environment (no tokens, endpoint or PYTHONPATH from whoever launched it), without waiting for it; three starts in a minute and it stops trying. The tap carries byte copies (`tap/service/`, `make sync-service-client`, `tests/test_service_client_sync.py`), and `tap/owner.py` now records owners with the same identity function the service checks them with.
- **`tap watch` registers its session with the service while it is on (tap 0.9.21).** A thread of its own calls `ensure` once, registers with the session's mode (`daemon`, `inline` or `off`) and its owner, re-registers every 20 s and at once after the service restarts, raises the generation when a resumed session's owner changes, and sends `session.end` on the way out. An `off` session never starts or holds the service. pi starts the service at `session_start` (`python -m tap service ensure`, detached) and names its own process as the session's owner for the tap (`PROBE_SERVICE_OWNER_PID`).
- **`probe service status|start|stop`.** `status --json` prints `service.status` (exit 1 when none runs); `start` starts it whatever the switch says and waits up to 2 s for it to answer; `stop` asks it to stop now.

- **The daemon writer's commands live in its skill, and the daemon's newer prompt text is cut to the minimum.** `track-work`'s new `versions/commands.writer.md` (a piece of the writer's version shown only with the `bash` tool set) says how to read files, skills and data files, how to change a draft with `probe draft edit` (the exact heredoc in a fenced block, one edit per call, nothing after `EOF`), the session commands, and that independent reads go in separate calls of one response; `versions/task.writer.md`, shown only while tasks are on, gives a big read to `probe daemon task` as a heredoc (the reader's `bash` shows the same), since a quoted question with a backtick or `$` is refused. The writer's `bash` description keeps only the skills folder's path. The task instructions (754 -> 371 chars), the reader's, audit's and task's `bash` text, the parallel line, the replies of `probe draft edit`, `probe daemon task` and a probe heredoc, and the `edit` tool's description are shorter. Most refused commands in the bash benches were malformed `probe draft edit` heredocs.

## 0.273.0

## 0.272.0

- **`probe wizard --json` (and `probe install --json`): a run a program can read.** stdout carries only NDJSON events, one object per line, flushed, each with `"v": 1` and an `event`: `step` {name, status: started|done|failed|skipped, message, agent}, `device_prompt` {verification_uri, verification_uri_complete, user_code, expires_in} before the approval is polled, `onboarding_required` {url}, `result` {action, agents: [{agent, requested, actual, ok, message}], complete} for configure, login, logout, recorder, uninstall and update, `error` {code: busy|usage|failed|interrupted, message}, and `done` {ok, complete, exit_code, steps} last. `done` ends every run short of SIGKILL: arguments that do not parse, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP included (`--help` is not a run: it prints its help and no events). Everything else the run prints goes to stderr, child processes included: fd 1 itself points there, and what is left in the real stdout's buffer is flushed there before `done`. `done.complete` is false when a step failed or was skipped (the persistent CLI install and plugins that could not be verified included), a result row is not ok, or the account must finish onboarding on the website first (which still exits 0). A marketplace refresh that failed is a `done` step ("used the copy already on this machine (refresh failed: ...)"): the install goes on from the copy on disk, and a plugin that cannot install from it fails its own step. A Who records switch that the server refuses, or that leaves an agent on its old recorder, is a row with `ok: false`; so is a configure that leaves tracking or capture on after being asked to turn it off. Signals: SIGINT stops a json run only while it waits for a browser approval (exit 130, `error` code `interrupted`); anywhere else it is ignored, and child processes inherit that, so it never lands in the middle of a config write or a plugin install. SIGTERM and SIGHUP stop it anywhere (exit 143 and 129, `interrupted`) and still write `done`; a child process running at that moment is stopped with it. A json run asks for a lone missing MCP grant that a headless run skips: the program shows the approval link. Without `--json` the output is unchanged, byte for byte. The desktop app drives setup through these.
- **`--agent` is repeatable.** `--agent claude --agent pi` configures both in one run behind one browser approval. Every value it took before (`both`, `all`, `claude,codex`, an agent's name) means what it meant, and an unknown one is refused with the same words.
- **One Probe setup changes a device at a time.** Every wizard action that can change it, and `probe login`, `probe logout`, `probe update` and the auto-updater, hold `~/.local/state/probe/wizard.lock`, an OS lock the kernel drops when its holder exits (a killed run leaves nothing to clean up); a second one prints "another Probe setup is running", changes nothing and exits 75 (`error` code `busy` under `--json`). Diagnose and the headless listings (account, settings, defaults, imports, Who records without `--who-records`) do not take it. An update turned away (`probe wizard --action update`, `probe update`, the detached auto-updater after it has waited out the command that spawned it) also records a skip that `probe doctor` shows. The wizard's own Update action holds the lock already and is not turned away by itself.
- **`probe status --json`: this device's one Probe install as one JSON object** (`"v": 1`), for the desktop app and agents, so they show what the wizard's menu shows: the CLI, the account (signed in, context, base URL), every agent (binary found, configured, its plugin, capture, MCP state and why, who records for it), Who records, the new-session default and any environment override, auto-update, versions, the daemon (key, AI libraries, today's tokens, recent errors), whether a `probe wizard` holds the run lock, and `errors` for anything unreadable (a corrupt config or `autoupdate.json` is an error entry, never a fresh device; a corrupt config makes everything read from it null: the account, each agent's plugin, capture, MCP and recorder facts, Who records, the default, the daemon key). Composed from the menu's own readers (`doctor.collect` per agent). The default read is local only: files, no network and no subprocess (no `ps` on macOS either), and the every-command notices (background refresher, auto-update, outbox drainer) are skipped, so a hung agent binary cannot slow it. `--refresh` adds the agents' own CLIs (every agent's plugin list at once), the server's `/v1/device-state` (an older server: asked the old way once for every agent) and the MCP token check, all inside ONE `--timeout` budget (default 10 s) and reported as `{state, checked, error}`; a binary that timed out is not asked again and is killed with its children. Two probes at once never read each other as a running setup. Exit 0 whatever the state, 2 for a usage error. Without `--json` it prints a short summary. The schema is `probe.cli.status`'s docstring, pinned by its tests.
- **No ancestor walk for a harness session nobody recorded.** Every `probe` command looked for a Kimi Code session among its ancestors, which runs `ps -A` where there is no /proc (macOS); with no harness process recorded on the machine it now looks no further, and `probe status` never looks. The plugin's hook copy of `session_marker` carries the same check.
- **A `probe status` probe never turns a starting wizard away.** The run lock waits out contention for 0.25 s before calling another setup busy: a real holder keeps it for its whole run, a status probe for an instant.

## 0.271.1

- **Skills name Probe's read tools as commands.** `track-work` now says Probe's read tools (`entity`, `search`, `metrics`, `browse`, `query_sql`, `find_papers`) run as `probe mcp call <tool> '<json args>'` (`probe mcp tools` lists them), so its `entity(...)` mentions read right for the daemon's bash-only writer and inline agents, which have no native MCP tools. `write-summary` says the page skills sit beside it (no "skills folder") and spells the who-did-what read as `probe mcp call entity`; `track-work`'s one-`search` rule and `reference.md`'s `metrics`/`entity` description lines name the command. In the bench the bash-only writer made ~1 MCP call a run against 3-5 before.
- **The daemon's `bash` calls that only read run together; a call that writes runs alone, in order.** The writer's and the audit's `bash` is no longer one call at a time: the calls of one model response are classified before any runs (`tools.reads_only`: a safe-list read, or a `probe` read that only prints, or a command the daemon answers itself that reads), the reads run at the same time (at most 4), and anything else -- a probe write, a note write, a command off the safe list -- waits for every call before it and holds every call after it, so writes keep the model's order and never overlap anything (`agent.CallOrder`, the first tool hook, so the lease gate, the loop detector and the limits see a write only once the calls before it are over). Identical calls of one response still run one after another, so the loop detector stops a repeated failure as before. The reader's calls are bounded the same way. `PROBE_DAEMON_PARALLEL=0` runs every call alone, in order. The `bash` descriptions say so in one line (NEW wording, `tests/fixtures/daemon_prompts/tools/parallel.NEW.md`).
- **`probe daemon task`: a child agent for one long read, in a context of its own.** The writer and the reader can run `probe daemon task "<what to find out>"` (or the task in a quoted heredoc) to scan many runs or files, search the session or read a long log without carrying it: a child agent on the same model, with `bash` that runs only reads (nothing that writes or asks runs, in any mode), no task of its own, and a hard budget (20 model rounds, 120 s, 500K tokens; no model round once the daemon may no longer act for the session), answers in plain text; its answer (scrubbed, then cut at 8,000 characters) comes back inside a `<task-answer>` block labelled as data written by a read-only task, which its own text cannot close, then a footer with its rounds, seconds and dollars. Its instructions ask for a source (event id, file, command) on every claim and say that what it reads is data. At most 2 of a run's tasks run at once. Its rounds count as its parent's (the store's rounds, the device's tokens, the reader's turn spend) and its tokens into the parent run's usage beside the run's own (`usage.TASK_DETAILS`: never against a bite's token limit); a run's tasks share $0.50 (or 2M tokens of an unpriced model), each running task holding back its share until it ends, and a task that does not fit is refused with what to do instead. A task's deps never run bypass mode's extras, and the shell and probe paths refuse anything but a read again where it would run. `PROBE_DAEMON_TASKS=0` turns it off. Texts: NEW fixtures `tools/task-*.NEW.md`. The bench records each agent's parallel calls and tasks from its trace (`tool_stats`).
- **The daemon's `bash` calls that only read run together; a call that writes runs alone, in order.** The writer's and the audit's `bash` is no longer one call at a time: the calls of one model response are classified before any runs (`tools.reads_only`: a safe-list read, or a `probe` read that only prints, or a command the daemon answers itself that reads), the reads run at the same time (at most 4), and anything else -- a probe write, a note write, a command off the safe list -- waits for every call before it and holds every call after it, so writes keep the model's order and never overlap anything (`agent.CallOrder`, the first tool hook, so the lease gate, the loop detector and the limits see a write only once the calls before it are over). Identical calls of one response still run one after another, so the loop detector stops a repeated failure as before; a call waiting 120 s for an earlier one that never started is not run and says so. The reader's calls are bounded the same way. `PROBE_DAEMON_PARALLEL=0` runs every call alone, in order. The `bash` descriptions say so in one line (NEW wording, `tests/fixtures/daemon_prompts/tools/parallel.NEW.md`).
- **`probe daemon task`: a child agent for one long read, in a context of its own.** The writer and the reader can run `probe daemon task "<what to find out>"` (or the task in a quoted heredoc) to scan many runs or files, search the session or read a long log without carrying it: a child agent on the same model, with `bash` that runs only reads (nothing that writes or asks runs, in any mode), no task of its own, and a hard budget (20 model rounds, 120 s, 500K tokens; no model round once the daemon may no longer act for the session), answers in plain text; its answer (scrubbed, then cut at 8,000 characters) comes back inside a `<task-answer id=…>` block labelled as data written by a read-only task (the id is new for every answer, so its own text cannot write the closing line, and the label says the block ends only there; every `<` inside, and every character that looks like one, is escaped), then a footer with its rounds, seconds and dollars. Its instructions ask for a source (event id, file, command) on every claim and say that what it reads is data. At most 2 of a run's tasks run at once. Its rounds count as its parent's (the store's rounds, the device's tokens, the reader's turn spend) and its tokens into the parent run's usage beside the run's own (`usage.TASK_DETAILS`: never against a bite's token limit); a run's tasks share $0.50 (or 2M tokens of an unpriced model); each task may spend at most its share ($0.25, priced round by round: told to answer at 80%; once told, for any reason, it gets exactly one more model round to answer in, even past its share, and no other; untold, no round at 100%), a running task holds back that share until it ends, a task that does not fit is refused with what to do instead (before it waits for a slot only what is spent counts; after, the running tasks' shares too), and once the run's budget is spent no task sends another round. A task's deps never run bypass mode's extras, and `shell()` itself (before any route a write could take, the team-note question included) and the shell and probe paths refuse anything but a read again where it would run. `PROBE_DAEMON_TASKS=0` turns it off. Texts: NEW fixtures `tools/task-*.NEW.md`. The bench records each agent's parallel calls and tasks from its trace (`tool_stats`).

## 0.271.0

## 0.270.0

- **A code snapshot never captures a folder that declares itself a cache.** A folder holding a Cache Directory Tagging Spec `CACHEDIR.TAG` (cargo's `target/`, uv venvs, Gradle and pytest caches) is skipped by the code snapshot (outside git, and inside git whether its files are tracked or not) and by run-output capture, and reported once as `generated`. The folder importer is unchanged: its classifier decides what an import keeps. The name list (`.venv`, `node_modules`, ...) stays; this catches caches with ordinary names, which went up as a run's code before (3,674 files of cargo's `quadread/target/` on 2026-10-17). An explicit `include=` still captures one.
- **instrument-code tells the agent to keep a run's code capture to what a rerun needs.** Before the first run in a folder the agent writes a `.probeignore` (gitignore syntax; `!` re-includes) keeping the code the run executes, its configs and its build and dependency files, and leaving out what those rebuild (build output, venvs, caches), data and checkpoints, other projects in the folder and earlier runs' outputs. Ships in the plugin's skills (a plugin release) and in the CLI the daemon reads them from.
- **The daemon's agents get one tool: `bash`.** The writer, the reader and the team-note audit each have `bash` and their `final_result`, nothing else. What the other tools did is a command the daemon answers in its own process: `read` -> `cat` / `sed -n` / `head` / `tail` (the Probe skills folder is read-only on the safe list, hard-linked installs included) and `probe file preview <path>` for a CSV/JSON/Parquet/NumPy file; `edit` -> `probe draft edit <path>` with the change on stdin from a quoted heredoc (`<<<<<<< OLD` / `======= NEW` / `>>>>>>> END`, found exactly once, drafts only); `session` -> `probe daemon session open|outline|search|logbook|status`; the reader's `feedback` -> `probe feedback send`; the native Probe MCP -> `probe mcp call <tool> '<json>'` / `probe mcp tools` over the daemon's key (the reader still names its session and leaves it out of search; the audit still refuses `find_papers`), with the MCP's instructions kept in each agent's instructions. The reader's `bash` refuses anything but a read, in every mode, and runs only a listed set of `probe` reads. A one-line command map rides under the `bash` description, a skill's `entity`/`search`/`metrics`/`browse`/`query_sql`/`find_papers` named as `probe mcp call` (`PROBE_DAEMON_COMMAND_MAP=0` drops it). A `probe draft edit` heredoc in any other shape is refused in every mode, bypass included. `probe run reproduce --export` / `--materialize` (they write a file wherever pointed) are the researcher's, never the daemon's; checkout bookkeeping names are refused however they are spelled (any case, quotes, globs, a folder in other case on macOS/Windows). The daemon's shell also gives a heredoc after a command's first line the every-mode check (a body naming a Probe setting or `probe` ran in bypass mode before). `PROBE_DAEMON_TOOLS=classic` restores today's tools. The shell's logbook now records `bash -c` (it always ran `/bin/bash`); `probe approvals` reads both. `probe draft edit` and `probe file preview` are ordinary CLI commands too.

## 0.269.0

- **`probe project delete`, `probe experiment delete` and `probe run delete` take `--dry-run`.** It resolves the ref like the delete, asks the same route with `?dry_run=true` and prints the server's answer (what would go to the trash, whose it is, when its newest work last changed) with no prompt and nothing moved. A server without the trash refuses it, in the SDK too: `delete_project`, `delete_run` and `delete_experiment` raise before sending a `dry_run=True` DELETE to a server that would ignore the flag and delete for good. The dashboard assistant's approval card shows it for every trash delete it proposes.
## 0.268.0

- **The MCP says when hiding the caller's own session work left a listing short.** `browse` of runs, notes, datasets or checkpoints adds `hidden_own_session_work: N` (and `hidden_own_session_work_more` when a runs count stopped at 200 rows) instead of an empty page that reads as "nothing here". The dataset card keeps `producer: null` and the version's `preview_artifact_id` explicit.
- **The agent links a run to the exact dataset version, checkpoint save or source revision it used.** `probe dataset use`, `probe checkpoint use` and `probe dataset add --from` refuse a ref that names whatever is newest (a bare `dataset:<name>`, `@latest`, `@best`, a `source:<key>` with no `@<revision>`): linked after the fact it could pin a newer version than the run read. The refusal names `probe dataset show`, `probe checkpoint list --run` or `probe source list` to find the fixed one (`dataset:<name>@<N>`, `checkpoint:<run>@step<N>`). Both use commands take `--reason` and, like `probe edge add`, a repeatable `--evidence EVENT_ID` (a session event the use rests on, stored with its session); `checkpoint use` takes `--role` (`init`, or `eval` for the checkpoint an eval run evaluated) and prints the save the server pinned. In a script, `run.use_dataset` / `use_checkpoint` / `use_mixture` and `log_dataset(composition=...)` naming such a ref are never queued for later when Probe is unreachable, or on an offline run: they warn and record nothing. `probe run input dismiss|pin|reset` and the SDK's `Client.correct_run_input` are removed: Probe no longer links reads to data by matching bytes, so a wrong data link is removed with `probe edge remove` and the right one added (the `instrument-code` skill now says so).
- **track-work tells the agent how to set a run's data links.** Weights a run started or resumed from: `probe checkpoint use REF --run R`; a checkpoint an eval run evaluates: `--role eval`; name the exact version or save (`dataset:N@3`, `checkpoint:RUN@step400`). `probe run inputs` lists each read and the stored copies of its bytes (several copies name none), and a link later work contradicts is removed with `probe edge remove` and the right one added. The reference no longer says the server matches reads to writers. Ships in the plugin's skills (a plugin release) and in the CLI the daemon reads them from. The daemon bench's fake Probe serves `POST /runs/{id}/uses`, `GET /runs/{id}/inputs` (with `stored_as`), the checkpoint list and dataset reads, `source` ends and `relates_to`, and drops rows the retired byte match derived from a fixture.

## 0.267.2

- **MCP: a series page leaves room for the heaviest cursor it can carry.** A page of metric series is fitted to `token_budget` with a stand-in for the delivery cursor that replaces its native one. Base64 of the cursor's compressed identity hash takes 120 to 146 tokens depending on the hash, and the stand-in measured with one fixed hash (130) was outweighed about half the time, so a tightly fitted page went out as JSON fragments. The stand-in is now the heaviest of 64 sampled hashes for the read's own request, plus an 8-token slack (`Budget.fits(..., reserve=)`).
- pi: the five page skills (`overview-page`, `overview-contract`, `overview-charts`, `artifact-diagramming`, `artifact-design`) are in `PACKAGE_SKILLS`, so a daemon-profile pi session drops them from the main agent's prompt like the package's other skills.

## 0.267.1

- **The page skills are named by their path, to be read before a page is edited.** `write-summary` now says "Before you edit a page, read `overview-page/SKILL.md` ... and `overview-contract/SKILL.md` ... in your skills folder" (and the three others by path). In the first live daemon test on 0.267.0 the writer never opened them, so it touched up an old short page instead of writing a full one; the daemon's `read` opens a skills-folder path like these (`daemon/tools.py` `_in_skills`), and an inline agent finds them beside `write-summary`.

## 0.267.0

- **The page skills ship: a recorder writes a summary as a full page.** `write-summary` is replaced by the full-page version (the page is free: no TL;DR or word cap; load, read the part you change, edit it in place, push once), and five page skills join it, a `read` away for the daemon and plain skills for the main agent, inline agent and pi: `overview-page` (what the page says, in what order), `overview-contract` (the HTML, CSS and chart rules push enforces), `overview-charts` (when and how to declare a chart), `artifact-diagramming` and `artifact-design`. They are in `skills/profiles.json` "full", the daemon plugin's `inline/` copies (`INLINE_SKILLS`), pi's `package.json` and `mirror-package.json`, and the plugin hooks' telemetry list.
- **`probe summary checkout` never replaces a draft holding unpushed edits.** In either format, with or without a session id: it exits 2, prints JSON naming the draft (`refused: "unpushed edits"`) and says to push or check out again with `--steal`. Before, a session's checkout overwrote its own draft and base, and dropped the other format's draft, so the daemon's automatic checkout could erase a writer's edits. The erasure, missing-base and other-server messages now say `--steal`.
- **The first write's own checkout is bounded.** One attempt per request and 5 seconds for all of them (`FIRST_WRITE_LOAD_S`); past that, the reminder line as before.
- **The daemon loads summaries only when they need it.** Before a run it checks out an entity with no draft, or whose clean draft's version is no longer the server's (one plain summary read, `probe_api.summary_head`; nothing when that read fails); it skips the Metrics-center question (`--no-visuals`), and version reads and checkouts together stop at 20 seconds. A checkout the CLI refuses for unpushed edits is outlined as such. The outline never quotes a person's kept text as the page's opening, and the `edit` tool compares draft folders without case on macOS and Windows.

- **`probe summary checkout` hands over the full page.** Against a server with full pages (`GET .../summary?format=html`) the draft is `<session>.html` (`<session>.daemon.html` for the daemon): one file holding the page's chart declarations as a `<script type="application/json" data-probe-series>` block, then the page as HTML, with each person's block between `<!-- kept: hN -->` and `<!-- /kept -->`. The closed set the declarations may name (each run's metric keys and point counts) is written beside it (`<session>.chartable.json`); the checkout's JSON names it (`chartable_path`, and `chartable` counts) and says `format: html`, with the draft as `html` in place of `markdown`. `probe summary push` sends the draft by its extension (`.html` as `html`, `.md` as `markdown`) and merges a moved page with the same three-way merge. A server without full pages ignores the parameter: the draft is Markdown, as before. A checkout removes the session's draft in the other format. `Client.get_summary(format="html")` and `Client.put_summary(html=..., series=...)` are the SDK's side.
- **An agent's first write to a project or experiment checks its summary out.** In a session the agent records itself (inline), the first `probe` write landing on an entity whose summary the session has not checked out now checks it out and prints the draft's path on stderr (`Summary of <entity> checked out for this session (vN): <path> - edit it, then probe summary push ...`), in place of the reminder line. No server answer, a refused read, or unpushed edits in the session's draft for it: the reminder line as before, and the write never fails. Under the daemon the reminder stays: its worker loads the writer's summaries.
- **The daemon loads its writer's summaries and shows outlines, not their text.** Before each writer run the worker checks out every project and experiment the session's writes landed on or created (the logbook, by each command's own arguments; an experiment's creation touches its project too), at most the six touched last, with no model round, and never replaces a draft holding unpushed edits. The run's message starts with an outline per entity, once per change: kind, label, version and size, the draft and the push that sends it, who edited it last and when, its headings, its opening paragraph (400 characters), what the session's writes did to it since that version (a conclusion, a new experiment, runs it started and how they ended), and whether the draft has unpushed edits. It replaces the pin of one summary's whole text. The writer has a new `edit` tool: an exact find-and-replace in a checked-out summary or note draft (`old` found exactly once; any other path, the team note and the checkout's bookkeeping refused), answering with the changed lines; it runs alone, like `shell`. The outline lines and the tool's description are new wording (`bite/summary-outline.NEW.md`, `tools/edit.NEW.md`).
- A three-way merge into a draft with no final newline no longer reads as "file changed while merging".

- **MCP: an agent can read a file's text by id, whatever it is filed under.** `entity artifact:<id> view="content"` returns the file's text in 40-line sections (page with `start_line`, search with `grep` + `context_lines`), with its sha256. It works for run-, experiment- and project-filed files, not only shared ones; before, a reader could list a file's id and hash from `view="artifacts"` but had no way to read its bytes. Binary files, files over 2 MiB and references refuse and name `probe artifact download <id>`. A non-shared id now resolves to its full card (name, hash, size, metadata) from `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}`, not an id-only stub.
- **`probe summary checkout` and `push` on a team still at `lane` say the summary door is closed, not that the overview lane writes the summaries.** The overview lane was deleted on the server (writer-owns-summary R2), so a `lane` team has nobody writing its summaries; the note now matches the server's `summary_writer_off` words and says to ask Probe (support@prbe.ai) to switch the team to recorder. `(mode lane)`, the mark the daemon reads, is unchanged.

## 0.266.5

- **The daemon no longer crashes on a command that names an over-long path.** The folder check reads paths out of the agent's shell commands; before Python 3.14, `Path.is_dir()` raises `OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long` on a name over 255 bytes, and the worker died on every restart. A heredoc holding a dict with a secret-scan marker (`<redacted:anchored-secret>`) did it: the marker's `>` read as a redirect and the 300-character dict after it as the file written. One strand-ai session went unrecorded for 13 hours. Those checks now answer "not a folder", and a command the check cannot read is skipped.
- **A Probe MCP tool that keeps returning errors no longer fails the whole bite.** pydantic-ai fails a run on a tool's third retry in a row ("Tool 'entity' exceeded max retries count of 2"), losing every round of the bite. That call now answers the model with the error (`tool error (entity): failed 3 times in a row; not retried.`), and a second model round that runs out of retries, whatever the tool, fails the run as before (its events stay queued and the next try backs off). A reader turn whose tool runs out of retries is now a failed turn, retried with backoff, no longer read as the model's prose answer with its events passed over. Arguments the daemon's own tools refuse to accept still fail the run as before.
- **A reader turn the size guard wraps up is not reported as stopped.** Past 180,000 tokens (or the message cap) the reader is told to end its turn; when it then does, with its answer, the status stays OK and #eng-alerts gets no "Reader turn stopped". Round, time and loop limits still report.
- MCP: a cursor that does not decode is refused as not copied exactly, no longer as a changed request (see the root CHANGELOG).

## 0.266.4

- **Recorder-written summaries are a short TL;DR** (the daemon's, and a main agent's or pi's when it records). `write-summary` now asks for one sentence on what the project or experiment is, one or two on where it stands (the answer, its number and run, what's next) and up to three one-line bullets per dated entry, under 150 words (was 500; the oldest entries are cut once shrinking is not enough), in plain words. Conditions go in a few words ("one seed, one split"); setup, file names and what couldn't be checked stay out (notes take them only as edit-notes says). On the companion bench, summaries fell from 140 to 78 words on average, the summary gate passed 5 of 6 runs, and the writer cost 7% less a session. `overview-visuals` now says how the list reaches `probe visuals set`: `probe visuals options` writes it to a file, you edit it, then set.
- **`probe doctor` and the setup wizard now mark a CLI before 0.261.0 "UPDATE NEEDED", with the reason** (`client-version.json` `cli.recommended` and `message`): every team's project and experiment summaries are now written by its daemon or agent, which a CLI before 0.261.0 cannot do, so that team's summaries would stop updating.

## 0.266.3

- **The Probe question dialog no longer shows each option twice, and the feedback question asks first.** The agent was told an option's description could be empty or repeat its label, and Claude Code agents repeated it, so every option showed twice (`Send it` / `Send it`). Agents are now told to leave it empty (`""`), and the approvals hook refuses a description that repeats the label. The feedback question now reads "Send this feedback to the Probe team?", then who wrote it and the text, then what else is sent, with a blank line between each. A feedback question asked under the old wording and still unsent at upgrade no longer matches its re-rendered words, so it is voided, not sent.

## 0.266.2
- The MCP's `NoteCatalogKind` and the generated `NoteKind` lose their `group`/`artifact` tombstones: no server produces either since files and sweep groups stopped carrying notes.

## 0.266.1

- **A `probe visuals set` no longer puts back a tables version this session's own `probe summary push` had already moved past.** Every write of the remembered version now takes one lock beside the draft (`<session>.visuals.lock`), the push re-checks it under that lock, and a set never moves it backwards. Before, a set that finished just after such a push could leave the next set refused (exit 2) until `probe visuals options` ran again. One narrower window stays open (a set landing while the push merges, before the push re-reads): the same exit 2, and `probe visuals options` still recovers it.

## 0.266.0

- **The installer repairs a Codex marketplace whose config entry was deleted.** Removing `[marketplaces.research-os-agent]` from `~/.codex/config.toml` (or the whole file) left the checkout in `~/.codex/.tmp/marketplaces/`, and from then on `codex plugin marketplace add` refused ("already added from a different source"), `upgrade` refused ("not configured as a Git marketplace") and both plugins were "not found in marketplace". Re-running `npx probe-research install` could not get out of it. The installer and `probe update` now remove that orphaned checkout and add the marketplace again. A name Codex still lists (a fork, a local checkout) is never removed; the error names it and the `codex plugin marketplace remove` that would replace it. When adding and refreshing the marketplace both fail, the installer prints both errors, not only the refresh's.
- **Notes caps are counted in tokens** (plan notes-carriers P2; needs the matching server). A project's, an experiment's and the team note's notes (and their sub-notes) are capped at 30,000 o200k_base tokens, a run's note (and its sub-notes) at 2,000, with a looser character backstop beside each (150,000 / 10,000). The fullness warnings, the `notes show`/`checkout` read advisory and `probe notes status` read the server's token numbers and print "(N of M tokens, R left)"; `notes status` ranks by tokens and says how many documents it could not rank because the server has not counted them yet. `notes append`/`edit` refuse before sending with the packaged tokenizer (a text whose UTF-8 bytes fit the cap is never tokenized) and check the character backstop too; a server's refusal in either unit, a sub-note body's included, still gets the compaction advice. `--json` output gains `stored_tokens`, `limit_tokens` and `remaining_tokens`; `remaining`, `limit` and `stored_chars` keep their character meaning (now the backstop). Against a server older than token caps, or for a note the server has not counted, no fullness is printed rather than one read from the character fields, and the pre-send check holds an older server to its character cap as before. MCP: sub-note cards, notes-view sub-note rows, `browse(mode="notes")` rows and the team note carry `tokens`/`limit_tokens` (and `remaining_tokens`) instead of the character fields; an unknown count is left off.

## 0.265.1

- **Uploaded checkpoints come back byte for byte.** With `PROBE_CHECKPOINTS=upload` (or `checkpoints="upload"`), the credential scrubber masked the vocabulary id in BERT's `tokenizer.json` (`"password": 20786` was stored as `"password": <redacted:anchored-secret>`). The stored file was not valid JSON, so `from_pretrained` on the download raised `JSONDecodeError`, and `download_checkpoint` still reported every file verified, because the recorded hash was of the masked copy. Three changes: (1) a number after a quoted `"password"`/`"passwd"` key is no longer read as a credential; `password=123456` and `"password": "123456"` are still masked. (2) A checkpoint's files are never rewritten: one holding a credential the scrubber would mask is refused (a warning, and the file reads as not stored, so the download names it) instead of being stored changed (`Run.log_artifact(..., verbatim=True)`). (3) `Client.download_checkpoint` warns (`ArtifactRedactedWarning`) when any file it restored was stored masked; `probe artifact download --checkpoint` already printed a note. Checkpoints already stored masked stay masked: download them to see which files the warning names, and upload them again.

- **What Jev ran is never missing from `probe approvals`.** The daemon now logs an approved shell command before it runs, then how it ended, so a command whose worker was killed while it ran is listed as "still running, or the daemon stopped while it ran" instead of not at all; one that raised is listed as failed while it ran, and one stopped before it started is logged as not run, no longer as ran. "More not shown" names the sessions the hidden ones are in. A logbook line in a shape the daemon never writes is counted and said, instead of dropped or crashing the list, and a store that exists but cannot be read is counted as unreadable. Invisible characters (variation selectors, the combining grapheme joiner, Hangul fillers, tags) now print as escapes too, in the held questions as well, so a command cannot carry a part the researcher does not see. The footer no longer says `probe companion log` shows each command's output; it does not.

## 0.265.0
- **Files and sweep groups no longer carry notes** (plan notes-carriers P1). Notes live on projects, experiments, runs and the team note. Every `probe notes` command loses `--artifact` and `--group`. `probe artifact add --notes` (and a manifest row's `"notes"`) and `probe group create --notes` are hidden and ignored with one stderr warning, so an older skill's upload or group still lands; `probe artifact set`, whose only option was `--notes`, and `probe group set --notes` exit 1 saying so (`group set --name/--spec` still work, and now send only those fields). SDK: `log_artifact(notes=)`, `create_group(notes=)`, `update_group(notes=)` and the client's upload doors (`upload_file`, `presign_upload`, `upload_fingerprinted`, `enqueue_artifact_upload`, `enqueue_artifact_reference`) accept `notes` with a `DeprecationWarning` and never send it; no upload path sends `notes`, and an outbox op an older client queued with one still delivers, without it. `NOTES_ENTITIES` is project, experiment, run. MCP: file and group cards and file listings carry no notes excerpt, a group has no `notes` view, and the catalog's `artifact`/`group` kinds stay one release as tombstones, never produced. The daemon's note anchors drop `--artifact`/`--group`. Skills (track-work, edit-notes, every copy): say what a file is, and where it lives, in its run's notes, never in its name; the folder import keeps its per-file lines in the manifest for the project's writer and uploads none. Pairs with the server half (notes writes on files and groups answer 410; upload `notes` is accepted and ignored).

## 0.264.2

- **The daemon profile no longer refuses the commands Probe itself sends the agent to.** Every CLI command's outbox banner said "see `probe outbox status`" and the guard refused it; the SDK's capture warning named `probe run check`, an offline run `probe sync`, and `instrument-code` `probe artifact download`, all refused too. Those four now run, with five diagnostics that read no team records: `probe daemon status`, `probe whoami`, `probe context list`, `probe wandb discover`, `probe wandb key status`. Every other `outbox`, `context` and `daemon` verb stays refused. A new test fails when a daemon-plugin skill names a `probe` command the guard refuses.
- **`probe shared add|share|unshare`, `probe metrics backfill` and `probe trial export` are writes.** They were classified as reads, so `read only` let them record and `--directed` could never run them in the daemon profile. `probe metrics delete` and `probe shared delete` are removals, never refused, like every other `delete` (`off` refused them as reads).

- **`log_dataset(stats=...)` no longer loses the whole dataset over one unknown key.** The server keeps a closed list of counts (`files`, `bytes`, `rows`, `tokens`, `removed`, whole numbers >= 0) and refused the entire registration over any other key, so the SDK warned, returned `ref=None` and the script exited 0 with no dataset. The SDK now drops a key outside the list (or a count that is not a whole number >= 0) with one warning and records the dataset; the docstring names the list.
- **`log_dataset(composition=...)` takes sources.** A dataset built from external data (`{probe.source(hub_uri): 0.8, probe.source(csv_uri): 0.2}`) carries its mixture itself instead of only on the producing run's `use_mixture` (needs the matching server).

## 0.264.1

- **`probe visuals set` is no longer refused for the same session's own `probe summary push`, nor the next push merged for its own `visuals set`.** Both writes bump one page counter but each keeps the other's half (a push keeps the tables, a set keeps the text byte for byte), so once this session's write lands on the exact version the other half was read at, that half moves to the new version. Before, every tables set after a summary push in the same bite was refused (exit 2) and redone after another `probe visuals options`: 21 of the writer's 42 visuals commands a session on the companion bench. A version anyone else moved still refuses or merges as before.
- **The daemon no longer refuses `probe visuals set --help` (or `summary push --help`).** The scan of the file a document command sends looked for it even on a help request, which sends nothing, and refused for want of a `visuals options` with the same flags: 4 of 6 bites on the bench.

## 0.264.0

- **`probe approvals` lists what Jev ran without asking you.** After the questions (or "nothing is waiting for you"), it shows the shell commands the daemon ran on Jev's yes in the last 24 hours, by session, newest first: when, Jev's lowest score, the exit code (or that it timed out, was stopped, or was cut short while it ran), and the whole command, line breaks kept. At most 20; it says how many more ran (each is in `probe companion log <session>`) and when a session's logbook could not be read. Until now such a yes was seen only in the daemon's logbook. Only the rows the daemon writes on a Jev yes count, matched whole, so the daemon's model cannot list its own `probe` writes there by naming Jev in their reason. A coding agent's shell, and the daemon's, sees only its own session's. Characters a terminal would act on (escape sequences, carriage returns, bidi overrides) now print as escapes, in the held questions too, whose later lines are now indented so none reads as a question of its own. A Jev-approved command cut short now keeps `auto-approved: Jev p=…` in its logbook reason.

## 0.263.1

- **A `Users/` or `home/` folder no longer erases a file's name.** Artifact names went through the prose scrubber, whose home-path rule read any `/Users/<x>` or `/home/<x>` folder in a repo path as a home directory and cut the rest to `<path>`: every file under `apps/web/pages/Admin/Users/` was uploaded as `apps/web/pages/Admin<path>`, overwriting the others, and the next one 409'd as superseded, so a folder import could never finish (one customer, 10-16, CLI 0.260.0; since 0.173.0, #1698). Names now get the credential scrub only (`Client.upload`, `Run.log_artifact`, the outbox, `probe artifact add`'s multipart door). A folder import frozen under a cut name is reissued once on resume, under the file's real name; its old request -- dead-lettered, or still queued when the import was cut off -- is discarded instead of retried forever. Artifacts already stored under a `<path>` name stay in the project until deleted.

## 0.263.0

- **The daemon's shell reads anywhere on the machine without asking, secrets and history excepted.** Most of the 53 shell commands one pi researcher's daemon held in 14 days were reads outside the working folders (`find /Users/x/Repos/other/outputs -name '*v2*'`, `ls -la` in `$HOME`, `cat /tmp/x.json`).
