The read programs (`cat head tail nl wc stat ls find du diff grep rg cut paste sort uniq tr tac numfmt jq`, the digests, and new: `gzip -cd`/`gunzip -c`/`-l`/`-t` and, on Linux, `zcat`) and `cd` may now name a file or folder anywhere; a `<` from outside feeds a read program only. Outside the working folders these still ask: a hidden file or folder; `~/Library`; for a content reader, a folder (read whole: `rg x DIR`, `rg x` or `grep -d rec` in an outside folder) and a name nothing is at; a walk for names (`find`, `du`, `ls -R`) of `$HOME`, a folder above it or a credential place (`find ~`, `du -sh /`, `find -- /`, BSD's `find -f ~`, and a walk of the current folder when a word may be an option's value: `cd ~ && ls -laR --ig /tmp`, `cd ~ && ls -RaI /tmp`). Names and metadata of any other tree run. Everywhere, inside the working folders too, a content read that names a pipe, socket or device, or a file with a second name (a hard link, which may be a credential's), asks; a pnpm or uv tree hard-linked into a repository asks for reads of its named files' text (the files a search walks to inside the working folders are not checked one by one). Everywhere, like a credential: shell and REPL history (`.zsh_history`, `.bash_history`, `.sh_history`, `.python_history`, `.node_repl_history`, `.psql_history`, `.mysql_history`, `.sqlite_history`, `.lesshst`, `.viminfo`), all of `/proc` and `/sys`, `/dev`, `/run/secrets`, `/run/user`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/gshadow` and `/etc/ssh`; credential paths, Probe's key and state and `.probe.config` `off` paths are refused as before. Every such name and place is matched in any case (`client.PEM`, `ID_RSA`, `.ENV`: macOS's disks ignore case) and in macOS's other spellings (`/private/etc/ssh`, `/System/Volumes/Data/...`); a bind mount is not covered. The `.probe.config` tree check now also sees `find -H DIR`, `find -- DIR`, `ls --rec`, `grep -d rec` and a recursive `ls`/`du` that may walk the current folder, and looks where bash runs the read: a `cd` in a pipeline moves nothing (`cd /x | rg -I KEY .` searches here) except as the last part under `shopt -s lastpipe`, which adds its folder, and a tree read without file names (`rg -I`, `grep -h`) is checked from every folder it may run in (a `;` stuck to a word, `cd /o;rg -I T .`, split as bash splits it). Not covered: a bind mount, a hard link a search inside the working folders walks to, and a file swapped for a symlink between the check and the open. git still needs a repository inside, and the `read` tool and the reader stay in the working folders; the read tool's refusal now says that a plain file outside is a `cat` through the shell away. `gzip`/`gunzip` without `-c` (or `-l`, `-t`) write, `gzip -c` alone compresses, `-r`/`-f`/`-S` and every other option ask, and a name that is not a file asks (gzip would read NAME.gz in its place). Also closed: `ls -R` with `-L` follows symlinks out (refused, as `find -L` is); `grep -d rec`, `--dir rec` and `-d RECURSE` recursed (GNU grep takes any start of `recurse`, BSD any case), so only `-d read` and `-d skip` run; macOS's `ls` reads `-I` as a flag, so the word after it is checked as a name there.

- **The daemon asks Jev before it asks you about a shell command.** A command the daemon's safe list does not clear is first sent to Probe's command check (`POST /v1/companion/command-check`, five yes/no questions to Jev: no network, no secret, writes nothing, nothing hidden, no process or system control), in every permission mode except bypass; bypass auto-approves as before. When Probe answers `approve`, the command is checked once more (the same real programs, the same verdict, no credential, private or policy path, still no script: a link pointed at a key while Jev answered is caught) and runs without a question; the logbook says `auto-approved: Jev p=<lowest score>`. Any other answer, an error or a 3-second timeout asks the researcher exactly as before. Jev judges only inline Python: `python -c CODE` (no option that turns the safe path off) on a Python 3.11+ read from its real file's name, never by running it, found on PATH outside the working folders (and never while PATH holds a folder of the session), alone or after plain `cd DIR`s, with nothing the checker's strict reading refuses (`$`, backticks, globs, braces); its whole code is in its text. Every other command the safe list rejects -- `kill`, `curl`, `make`, `cut -c`, `gzip`, `pip` -- is asked: four review rounds of a list of read-only programs each found an option that writes, runs a helper or reads names the command doesn't show. Also always asked: a command refused in every mode; one naming a credential-shaped file anywhere in its words (`Verdict.credential`); a hidden file or folder or a whole tree's contents (`rg`, `grep -r`, `diff -r`: `Verdict.private`); the notes folders, the team note, Probe's config or state; any command that runs a script file; and one a question already waits for or the researcher said no to. The shell now runs every command with `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. A yes is bound to the real files the command's programs are when Jev is asked (path, inode, size, change time): a program pointed elsewhere, replaced or written in place while Jev answers is asked. Probe sees the command, its folder, the safe list's reason and the working folders: never a file's contents, never the daemon's own reason.

## 0.262.1

- **Update cannot report a removal.** `probe wizard --action update` changes versions, never settings, so a tracking plugin or capture it does not see is now registered `unknown` (the server keeps what it knew) instead of `absent`. Updates spawned by a session's start see the agents on that shell's PATH, so one reaching fewer agents than the last report posted a false "Probe removed from a machine" and the next put it back (one customer, 10-15, CLI 0.258.0). Needs the server that keeps known values on an `unknown` report (this change's own server half); against an older one an update can show a known value moving to `unknown`.

## 0.262.0

- `probe summary`: the lane mode a checkout or push saw is kept per server (the active context's, or `--base-url`), so a team still in lane mode on one server no longer quiets the summary reminder on another.
- **Plugin: the `write-summary` and `overview-visuals` skills reach the main agent, `/probe inline` and pi** (plan writer-owns-summary D2, after CLI 0.261.0 shipped `probe summary` and `probe visuals`). The main agent with Probe on keeps project and experiment summaries (`probe summary checkout`, edit, `probe summary push`) and sets an experiment's tables and charts at Close (`probe visuals set`); track-work's copies carry the same three approved edits as the CLI wheel's (the researcher's `document` block, the project description from the summary's first line, the Close line). The tap's vendored rules and the lean daemon plugin's inline copies follow.
- **Folder imports can leave out what is not research.** The classifier now answers `left_out` (a file or folder, with a short why) beside `assignments`, and is told what that covers: code for a shipped product (its web or mobile app, CLI or service, with that product's tests and assets), vendored code, build output and caches; research code, configs, notebooks, results, logs and checkpoints stay, even inside a code repository. Every prompt used to require each row to land in a project, and the naming step asked for a project of "build noise", so a product monorepo's import uploaded its Rails + React web app, TypeScript harness, Go CLI and iOS app file by file (2,858 web-app source files, none read by a model). The review screen lists each left-out row with its file count and why; nothing in it is manifested or uploaded, and **Change the plan** can bring it back (large folders included: the correction now reaches every slice). Left-out files are recorded as `excluded` and stay settled when their bytes change, so editing a product does not reopen the import; `probe backfill --review-excluded` classifies them again, and the report says so. Only rows the classifier names are left out: a file it forgot follows the nearest real project (or stays unplaced for the next review), a left-out root row (`.`) covers the root's own files only, and a file named on its own inside a left-out folder keeps its project. Coverage percentages leave excluded files out of the denominator.
- **An import's uploads tell the server they are an import.** Requests sent with backfill attribution (the wizard's importer, including writes the outbox drainer delivers later) carry `X-Probe-Attribution: backfill`, so #probe-usage reads `backfill` instead of `sdk`.

## 0.261.0

- **The MCP reads a project's or experiment's sessions, and a summary's history.** `entity(refs=["project:P"], view="sessions")` (and `experiment:E`) lists the captured sessions that worked on it, newest first, with each row's `title` (the agent's own name for the session), owner, first and last sighting and `direct`; `next_cursor` walks past the route's page of 50, and the daemon's reader still never sees the session it reads beside. `view="summary_history"` lists the summary's versions (who, when, through what, how long) newest first, and `view_options={"version": N}` reads one version's markdown; any other option is refused by name. `view="overview"` gains `markdown`, the page as recorders read and write it, left out on a server without the summary route. A `search` with `project_id` that reaches transcripts (`search_in` names them, or is omitted and so asks for every corpus) now says in `note` that transcripts are not project-scoped (the scope drops every transcript hit) and points at the sessions view plus `view_options.grep`; the `project_id` parameter says the same. Against a server before the paged sessions routes, the sessions view reads the uncursored page as the capped list it is (`sessions_beyond_server_limit`), never as a complete walk. SDK: `list_project_sessions`, `list_experiment_sessions`, `get_summary`, `list_summary_versions`, `get_summary_version` (one name for both anchors: `project=` or `experiment=`). Needs the server with the sessions routes (this release) and, for summaries, the one that stores them.

- **`probe summary` and `probe visuals`: whoever records a session keeps its projects' and experiments' summaries, and their Metrics-center tables and charts.** `probe summary checkout --project P` (or `--experiment E [--project P]`) writes the summary (the Overview page as Markdown) to a draft file and prints JSON with its `path`, `version`, `markdown`, `you`, `today`, `edited_by`, `edited_at` and `mode`; edit the file, then `probe summary push` with the same flag. The draft is one per session (`<state>/summaries/<kind>/<id>/<session id>.md`, 0600; the daemon recording that session keeps `<session id>.daemon.md`), so two sessions on one machine never overwrite each other; a shell with no session id gets one shared file per entity, claimed as `probe notes` does. A draft checked out from another Probe server or key is never pushed. A push onto a page that moved merges locally (`merge3`) and asks for another push (exit 2 on a conflict); a page an erasure changed since the checkout is not merged: check out again (exit 2), and there is no `--force` to carry erased text past that check; a refusal (422, or 503 while the overview lane still writes the team's pages) exits 1 with the server's words. `probe visuals options` prints what tables and charts may name and writes the current list to a draft; `probe visuals set [--file F]` sends it against the version `options` read (exit 2 with the current list when the page moved since). Both writes take `--directed`, which reaches the server and the daemon-profile guard admits. SDK: `get_summary`, `put_summary`, `list_summary_versions`, `get_summary_version`, `get_visuals_options`, `put_visuals`, for both anchors. Needs the server's summary and visuals routes; an older server is said to predate them. The plugin hooks' `_session_marker.py` copies and pi's guard port learn the two command groups, so they ship with the next plugin release; the skill copies in the plugins, pi and the tap follow in their own change once this CLI is on PyPI.
- **The daemon's writer keeps summaries.** Its instructions carry the new `write-summary` skill whole beside `track-work` and `edit-notes`; `overview-visuals` (the recorder's copy of the lane's skill, its caps written from the server's by `make sync-visuals-caps`) ships in the CLI wheel for the writer to read before `probe visuals set`; track-work names `document` (the researcher's block on a summary) as theirs, the project description as coming from its summary's first line, and setting an experiment's tables and charts at Close. The writer's shell may write summary drafts but never a checkout's base copy, version or lock (nor a note's); the pre-checks scan the draft a push or a `visuals set` sends, refuse `--steal`, and point a refused `--summary` at `probe summary`. The last summary the writer checked out comes back once, scrubbed, at the start of its next message (`# Summary of <slug> you loaded (v<N>)`) when lean history or a compaction dropped the checkout's output. A run that creates a project or experiment, or sets an experiment's conclusion, without a summary push that landed is sent back once (once more for an eligible experiment's tables) when the team's summaries are the recorders'; what it owes survives a pause into the next bite. While a team is still in lane mode, once a checkout or a refusal says so, the writer's `probe summary` and `probe visuals` commands are not run at all.
- **The first write of a session to a project or experiment whose summary it has not checked out says so**, once per session per entity, on stderr: `Summary of <X> not loaded this session - probe summary checkout --<kind> <X>`. The entity is the command's own `--project`/`--experiment` (an experiment write names the experiment); no server is asked. Not inside a run, in a shell with no session, in a session the daemon records for the agent, or for a day after this machine's last checkout or push saw the team's summaries still in lane mode.
- The companion bench's fake Probe serves the summary and visuals routes with the server's status codes and shapes (`--summaries-by lane` plays the lane's 503), and `score.py` reports S1-S4 (the main result on each touched summary, top-down shape, tables on finished experiments, unsupported numbers in summaries) with their absolute bars, apart from the checks a comparison reads; a summary also counts as a recorded document. `--compare` now also fails when the new arm's summary gate fails on any run or its $/run is over 1.25x the base arm's on any fixture.

## 0.260.1

- **The daemon names and describes a run when it starts again.** #2755 (0.249.1) had it run `probe run set RUN --name ... --description ...` at a run's start, since the server's title and description come only when a run ends; #2787's shorter track-work (0.252.0) dropped that line and brought back "Don't name runs", so live runs kept their script name and no description for hours (Willow's 400-update RL run, 10-15). track-work says it again, leaving out a locked name or description (an agent write replaces a person's words but keeps their lock; a name a script set outside an agent's environment reads locked too, and stays), and a researcher's own name or description goes in a command of its own with `--authored-by human` on a project, experiment or run; a test pins both. The daemon's checker now asks the researcher before ANY `--authored-by human` (it guarded only `run set` and `experiment set`, so `project create/set` and `experiment create/fork` could lock a name as a person's forever unasked), and no longer refuses a pointer to a file over 5 GB (`--reference`, or a manifest row the CLI records as one; a pointer sends no bytes, and the skill says to use one over 5 GB). A code kind is still refused over 5 GB: the CLI uploads it whatever `--reference` says. Other contradictions fixed in the same pass: the reference said to record a pointer over 100 MB (the skill and the daemon say 5 GB), taught the deprecated `run child --relation retry` for a relaunch (now `--parent RUN --relation retry`), and said project and experiment uploads always block (over 64 MB they queue); the writer was taught `dataset add --upload`, which the daemon is refused (now: only when the researcher asks); the reference's INDEX and three pointers named skill sections that no longer exist; the project line "The server writes the title and description" now says it is a project's description. Repeats removed: the session-status check (the main agent's header only: the daemon's worker already stops on `read`/`off`), the outbox queueing rule, the paper-link definitions, the provisioning note, the workspace/Shared upload rules, and the writer header's restatement of its job.

## 0.260.0

- Export native Miles dashboard telemetry and safe rollout/token diagnostics to Probe in the background when `--dump-details` is enabled. Upload immutable stream segments with durable retry cursors, and provide a repair command for existing dumps.

- **The daemon's shell runs checksum programs and `du` without asking.** 8 of the 74 shell commands held for the researcher in the 14 days to 10-15 were `shasum -a 256 FILE` (7) and `du -sh DIR` (1). `shasum`, `sha1sum`, `sha224sum`, `sha256sum`, `sha384sum`, `sha512sum`, `md5sum`, `b2sum` and `cksum` run at once with the options that pick the algorithm, the digest length, the read mode and the line style; anything else asks: `-c`/`--check` (it opens every file a checksum file names, which the check never sees, in any cluster or abbreviation), the options that only matter with it, `-z`, `shasum -0`, `cksum --raw`/`--base64`, and a word starting with `+` (shasum is Perl, and its option parser reads `+c` as `-c` and `--CHECK` as `--check`; a `sha256sum` wrapper may run it). `du` runs at once without `--files0-from`, `-X`/`--exclude-from`, `-L`/`-H`/`-D`/`--dereference(-args)` or `-0`/`--null`; with no name it walks the current folder, which must be a working folder, as for `ls` (bare `du` in `$HOME` asks). Both get `cat`'s file checks: every name inside the working folders; credential paths, Probe's config and key, hidden folders and `.probe.config` `off` paths refused as for `cat`. `sha224sum`, `sha384sum`, `b2sum`, `cksum` and `shasum` now count as reading the files they name, as `md5sum` and `sha256sum` did, so a `read` path one of them hashes carries the "to read" note.

- **The daemon asks the researcher about fewer routine commands.** Its `probe session status` and `probe companion log|trace|report` name the session it watches (`PROBE_DAEMON_SESSION`) when no coding agent's session is set, instead of failing with `no session id` (62 times in 14 days for one pi user, each followed by a `printenv`/`env` hunt that waited for the researcher); the switch commands never fall back. Run by the daemon, `probe session status` starts no capture and reports `capture`, `effective` and `writes_allowed` as null with a `note`: they describe the coding agent's own shell. A shell path through the shared skills' folders outside the working folders (`cat ~/.pi/agent/git/.../track-work/reference.md`) is refused with a pointer to the read tool instead of asked (14 questions in 14 days); a bare word (`grep -rn track-work`), a git `rev:path` and a note's text still go as before, and bypass mode still runs it. A help request the CLI's own parser takes as help (`probe artifact delete --help`) is a read, not a delete question; `--help` as an option's value (`probe notes delete --note --help`) is still a gated delete. The CLI's write gate reads help the same way: `probe notes create --title --help ...` is no longer let through under read only or daemon. In the daemon profile the agent may run `probe approvals` to list the held questions (its shell answers none, and now points both answers at the researcher's own terminal); `probe deny` stays the researcher's (both plugins' guards and the pi package).

## 0.259.1

- **Updating Probe updates pi's package while pi runs.** It waited until no `pi` process was left ("not updated while pi is running ... it updates after pi exits"), so a researcher with pi agents running around the clock never got the package. Now it runs `pi update` as pi itself allows and says `updated 0.4.0 → 0.5.0 (open pi sessions pick it up when restarted)`. pi's session start no longer waits for pi to exit before a retry; an update held back by an older CLI is retried at the next pi session start or run end, and one that failed or was killed at most every 10 minutes. Checked in real pi 1.0.0: with the package updated 0.4.0 → 0.5.0 under a running session (and with its `node_modules` deleted), turns, `/new`, `/probe-status`, `/probe-mcp-login` and the capture watcher kept working, and `/reload` loaded 0.5.0; killed mid-`npm install`, the orphaned npm still finished. A pi started in the second or two in which `pi update` has removed `node_modules` fails to load the package and exits 1: an automated pi launcher should retry an exit 1 right after an update.

## 0.259.0

- **The setup wizard asks "Where should this computer's work go?", and everything on this computer files there.** After every agent installs, `probe install` / `probe wizard` lists the team's workspaces (starting on this computer's current one, else your saved one, else the newest you made, else the oldest), offers "Create a new workspace", and saves the choice as this context's pin, the same setting `probe workspace use` writes. A team with one workspace is not asked; `--yes`/no-TTY runs (an agent running the install) never guess between several: they keep this computer's pin, else take your saved one, else leave it unset and say how to pick. It never blocks a finished install. The SDK now honours it: `Client.create_project` and `probe.init(..., workspace=)` send `workspace=` (a slug or an id), else `PROBE_WORKSPACE`, else this computer's pin, so `run()`'s auto-create, offline sync, folder imports and the W&B/miles importers all file there. A team with several workspaces and none set raises `WorkspaceRequired` (422 `workspace_required`) before anything is created, so a training script fails at `probe.init` rather than mid-run; existing projects keep working with nothing set. Once per computer (never after `probe workspace use --clear`), a member whose server-side saved default (CLI 0.254.1) moved their work gets it pinned here instead of the error, with a line saying so. `PROBE_WORKSPACE` may be a slug everywhere, and `probe project use` says when it moves this computer's workspace. `probe workspace list` shows `this_computer` instead of `default`; `probe workspace default` is gone (`probe workspace use` sets this computer's workspace); folder imports with no workspace set use the team's only workspace and otherwise stop with the fix instead of guessing the newest one you made.

## 0.258.0

- **Agents, the daemon included, set an experiment's conclusion when the work answers its question.** track-work's Close step: `probe experiment set EXP --conclusion "..."` with the answer and its evidence (both sides' numbers for a comparison), changed when later work changes the answer; the experiment row and reference §1/§2 name the flag and its shape. In the replay A/B the daemon set a conclusion whenever the work answered the question (4/4) and never otherwise (0/2); the answer then often sits in the conclusion rather than the notes (sxs-mlp 9/12 counting conclusions, 6/12 without; control 9/12). The companion bench's fake Probe stores conclusions (with the server's agent-over-person 409) and its scorer counts an agent's conclusion as a recorded document; a cut fixture's clock stands still at the cut.

## 0.257.1
- `probe provenance --steps` prints each output of a step on its own line with its own note (the server's `outputs_detail`); a step that made two dataset versions printed one note, the other version's. `probe checkpoint list` says `in Probe` in WHERE for a checkpoint Probe stores, instead of its internal `r2://` blob address; a reference keeps its host:path or uri.

- **instrument-code tells a script under `probe exec` to pass its config.** It said to call `probe.init()` with no arguments when `PROBE_RUN_ID` is set, so a customer's RL trainer joined the run and sent no config, though the SDK merges `config=` into the joined run. It now says `probe.init(config=args)` with nothing that names the run (all six arguments that raise), and to pass the whole config object as is (a Hydra `DictConfig`, never a resolved copy), without credentials, unless a trainer integration already records it.

## 0.257.0

- **`probe experiment set EXP --conclusion "..."` records an experiment's answer.** `""` clears it; `@file` and `-` read it like `--summary` (not both from stdin at once). SDK: `update_experiment(conclusion=)`. The MCP experiment card shows it under the question with `conclusion_source` (who wrote it), and local search matches it. An agent's write over a person's conclusion is refused by the server (409) and the CLI prints its reason. The daemon cannot mark its own text as a person's: its checker refuses `--authored-by human` on `experiment set` as on `run set`, now also when an unknown flag comes first. visualize-progress's stage table names the conclusion, and the SDK examples ask a real question (`does temperature 0.7 beat 1.0 on DockQ?`). The track-work/edit-notes wording that would have the daemon set it is held. Needs the server that stores conclusions (#2857); an older one refuses the field (422).

## 0.256.0

- **The daemon's reader sees a changed file as one line, and a session's first daemon catches up only its last 2 hours (daemon cost round 6).** (1) The reader is sent a file change as its first line (`changed train.py (1,200 -> 1,350 bytes) · 24 more lines: session op=open event_id=...`); the new file's start or the diff stays one `session` call away. File bodies were 76% of the text the reader was sent on strand-ai (150 turns, 10-14). The writer still gets the diff. (2) When a session's first worker finds history already there (Probe switched to the daemon late, or an old session resumed after the daemon became the default), events stamped more than 2 hours before the newest are context: the writer's window and `session` still show them, but they are never new, and the reader starts at the current turn (or at the first new event when that turn began earlier). Before, the daemon replayed the whole history: 13 sessions 1-38 days old in one week, one of 29 days in 1,980 model calls. No bite or reader turn runs until the history is read. A restarted worker never judges again. `PROBE_DAEMON_CATCH_UP_S` changes the window. Bench (gpt-6.1-sol, main vs this, 2-3 runs each): reader recall, asks and grounding equal, reader prompt 4-7K tokens smaller on a session writing 54 files; with the daemon switched on 2 h into a 2.7 h session (30-min window), writer checks 5.3 vs 5.5 of 7 at $0.32 vs $0.48 a session.

## 0.255.0

- **`probe paper add --relates-to <paper id|none> --relates-reason "<how the two relate>"` records the earlier paper in the project the new one connects to.** `--relates-provenance` defaults to `inferred` (`human` when the researcher said so); a paper id without a reason is refused before the write, naming `--relates-reason`. SDK: `add_paper(relates_to={"paper": ..., "reason": ..., "provenance": ...})`. `probe edge add --relation relates_to` works (the generated models know the relation), and `paper edges` and `paper graph --include-discovery` show the links. track-work's Papers section now asks for `--relates-to` on every paper, and rule 5 points paper similarity there. Needs server 0357; an older server ignores the field.

## 0.254.1

- **`probe workspace default <slug>` makes a workspace yours: where your writes that name no workspace land, on every machine and agent.** The server now files an unaddressed create in the caller's own default workspace (the first one they created) instead of the team's oldest; this command changes it (`PUT /v1/workspaces/{id}/default`, SDK `Client.set_default_workspace`). `probe workspace list` shows `default` for yours, and `probe workspace create` says on stderr when the new workspace became your default (your first). `probe workspace use` still pins one CLI context and wins over it. Folder imports with no workspace selected pick your default first. Older CLIs get the new server rule without upgrading.
- **Data catalog gaps: the daemon reader's own checkpoints hidden, hosted uploads that restart, checkpoints under `hash`, and the track-work skill.** (1) MCP `browse(mode="checkpoints"|"datasets")` under `X-Probe-Hide-Session-Work` (the daemon reader) now leaves out the session's own work, as `runs`, `notes` and lineage already did: a checkpoint whose run the session created (run-less: whose project it created), a dataset file its run logged or a dataset whose newest version that run wrote. A page of only those reads the next (up to 5, then `page_hidden_as_own_session_work`), the checkpoint `totals` are not sent while anything is hidden (they count those saves), and a server that cannot list what the session created marks the page `session_work_exclusion_unsupported`; `sources` name no run and are unchanged. (2) A hosted dataset blob over 64 MiB whose upload Probe gave up on (idle, expired, superseded) used to restart through the generic Shared multipart create, which refuses the reserved `.probe/datasets/<sha256>` name (422), so `log_dataset(upload=True)` / `probe dataset add --upload` failed; the restart now goes back through the hosting door (`POST /v1/catalog/datasets/uploads`), which re-stages the blob and answers a fresh upload (or `have`), and the new upload is the one waited on for verification. (3) A checkpoint saved under a `.probe.config` `hash` rule was not recorded at all (`log_artifact` refused every excluded path); a reference (`reference=True`, as the Hugging Face and Lightning integrations write each save, or a `uri` alone) of a `hash` path is now recorded with its identity in `meta` (`identity_only`, `fingerprint`: a file's sha256 or, past 1 GiB or the run's hashing budget, a fingerprint; a folder's manifest identity; `identity`, `rows`), staying a hashless reference so best/deleted refreshes still update it in place. `checkpoints="upload"` uploads no member there and warns once that `hash` keeps the bytes local, and reference mode's throwaway-disk warning there no longer suggests `checkpoints="upload"` (it says the checkpoint is recorded by reference only); an upload of a `hash` path is still refused, and `off`/`read` still record nothing. (4) track-work names datasets and sources: a `hash` path bullet, `probe dataset use` / `run.use_dataset` / `run.use_mixture` for what a run trained on, data steps as runs (`probe dataset add --note`, `probe exec --input/--output`), `dataset add --upload` for a dataset folder, and reference §1 lists `dataset` and `source` (deleted from the dashboard only, refused while runs use them) and makes the Shared folder read and delete only; the skill no longer teaches the writes the freeze refuses (`--workspace` / `--shared` on `probe artifact add`, workspace and Shared uploads in reference §3 and §4): Shared and workspace files are read-only, team data goes in `probe dataset add`. Synced to every copy (plugin, pi, daemon inline, the tap's companion rules and reference) and the approved renders.

## 0.254.0

- **The daemon's writer can run on a lean history and an index of the new events (daemon cost round 5, off unless the server turns it on for a team).** Two switches, pushed per team on every chat answer (`x-probe-writer-history: full|lean`, `x-probe-writer-events: raw|index`; `PROBE_DAEMON_WRITER_HISTORY` / `PROBE_DAEMON_WRITER_EVENTS` override them). LEAN: when a run completes, its saved conversation keeps only what the writer was sent (and a compaction's summary) and drops its own answers and tool traffic; the next message starts with the writes it made since (from the logbook, written once), so each run's request extends the last run's first one byte for byte -- the only prefix the model's prompt cache was measured to serve. A paused run keeps its tool results until the run that finishes it. INDEX: a run's new events reach the writer as one line per step with event ids, made by a cheap model on the server's new `index` lane (30 s, no retries, no refusal fallback); the researcher's prompts, the main agent's requests, the reader's messages and the daemon's notices are shown whole by plain code, an id the indexer was not given is removed, and any failed call shows its events raw. A run's trace carries `layout` (both switches, `cache_reset`, the index's calls, failures, bad ids and cost). Bench: the fake Probe forwards the server's `x-probe-*` settings. On a 2.9 h session (2 runs each): today's writer $0.72 a session and 6.0 of 7 checks; lean + index $0.60 and 7.0.

## 0.253.0

- **Agents stop searching Probe for facts it never stores.** The managed CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md block called Probe a knowledgebase where "all the team's data is semantically indexed", and the MCP instructions called it "this team's store of all ML research", so agents searched it for outside facts such as cloud GPU quotas by region (10-14). The block now says only what the team recorded is in Probe, and its "Do not call Probe for" list (and the daemon reader's copy) names facts from outside the team: cloud quotas, GPU capacity or pricing, vendor docs, public benchmarks. The MCP instructions say the same (`POINTER_VERSION` 46). The MCP wording ships with the hosted MCP's deploy.

- **A Claude Code session left open across plugin releases runs the installed hooks, not the ones it started with.** Claude Code fixes a session's plugin folder (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) when the session starts, while the managed CLAUDE.md block and the CLI keep moving. A session open since 10-11 on daemon plugin 0.129.0 was told by the current block to run `probe paper find`, and its 0.129.0 guard refused it as a read (10-13). Now `dispatch.py` checks Claude Code's install ledger (`installed_plugins.json` under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`) before every event. When the ledger lists another version folder of the same plugin (`<plugin>@<marketplace>`, user scope only, resolved inside the plugin's own cache folder), that copy's `dispatch.py` is imported in the same process and runs the event, with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` and the routes' module path pointing at it. The copy must be complete: `routes.json` parses and every script it names exists. If it will not import, the session's own copy runs the event. The Stop wake (`claude-reads.json`, which bypasses the dispatcher) hands over the same way in `reads_hook.py`. Because the hand-over follows the ledger, a rolled-back release also stops running in open sessions. Events stay in the session's own copy under Codex, with no ledger, with two copies or a project-scoped entry listed, or with a `--plugin-dir` checkout. `hooks.json` is unchanged. Cost: about 0.5 ms per event when the ledger lists the session's own copy (a byte scan, no `json` import), and about 8 ms per event in a session that hands over. Sessions started before this release keep their old dispatcher until they restart.

- **The data catalog: datasets, checkpoints and sources from the SDK and the CLI, and a `hash` level for data Probe must not read.** `probe.source(uri, revision=, license=, kind=)` registers a Hub dataset, bucket, URL or base model (upsert, returns a ref). `run.use_dataset(ref, role="train", share=)`, `run.use_checkpoint(ref)` (role `init`) and `run.use_mixture({ref: share})` (one request that replaces the run's train shares; shares sum to 1) record what a run used (`POST /v1/runs/{id}/uses`); a bare `dataset:<name>` pins the version current now. `run.log_dataset(path_or_uri, name, ...)` records a file, folder or remote uri as the next version of a team dataset: a folder is identified by its manifest (each file's path, size and sha256 within the run's 10 GB hashing budget, else its fingerprint and the version is `partial`; `hash="full"` reads everything; links are never followed), sent as gzip JSON to `PUT /v1/catalog/manifests/{sha256}` (queued in the outbox ahead of the registration when Probe cannot take it now: new op kind `catalog_manifest`), then one `POST /v1/catalog/datasets` that carries the run's file; the hashing spends the run's one 10 GB budget and runs on a worker the call waits for at most 2.5 minutes (1 hour for `hash="full"` or `upload=True`); a remote uri is a `pointer` (`sha256("uri\nrevision")`). It waits at most 10 s, then returns `DatasetRef(pending=True)` that fills in when the registration lands. `register=False` returns the run file's `artifact:<id>`; `publish=True` is for read-restricted projects; `composition={ref: rows}` (shares computed) or `{ref: share}`; `upload=True` hosts the file or folder in Probe (`POST /v1/catalog/datasets/uploads` answers which blobs it already holds; the rest go up by one PUT each or the multipart doors over 64 MiB), and a 402 over the hosted-data cap says so. A dataset kept outside Probe gets a 100-record (or 256 KiB) preview sample uploaded as `.probe/previews/<file id>` with `meta.preview_of`, with one line saying so (`preview=False` to stop; never for a `.probe.config` path that is not `on`). `client.checkpoint("latest"|"best")` now skips a save from a range a rewind abandoned (`meta.rewound`); releases up to 0.252.1 keep picking by step. Every one of these warns once and returns quietly on a server without the catalog, a network error or a refusal: none raises into a training job. The Hugging Face callback records the Hub base model (`init`) and Hub datasets (`train`, `eval`) as sources the run used, ids and revisions only, off with `capture_reads=False`. CLI: `probe source add|list|show`, `probe dataset add|use|list|show|download`, `probe checkpoint list|use` and `probe provenance REF [--down] [--depth N] [--steps]`; `dataset add --from REF --step NAME` records a step done by hand as a finished run, filed under `--project` or the `--from` version's project (refused with neither); `dataset download` fetches a hosted version file by file through the existing download batch, or prints where a reference version lives. The daemon may register datasets, sources and uses, never `--upload`, and its `dataset add` uploads no preview sample. Under `PROBE_MODE=disabled` every verb answers an empty ref and sends nothing. A 402 `hosted_data_bytes` prints sizes and the reference way out; once the server freezes loose workspace and Shared files (its 410), `probe shared add|share|unshare` and `probe artifact add --workspace|--shared` say where files go now instead of "upgrade". `.probe.config` gains the level `hash` (`<pattern> @probe hash`, or `@probe hash` above the lines it sets): the SDK still opens the run and records each file's identity only -- path, sha256 (or the >1 GiB fingerprint), size and row count, no hash below 64 bytes -- and never uploads, previews, captures or snapshots it; a run whose folder or script is at `hash` does not capture its console log, nor does `probe exec` when its command names a `hash`, `read` or `off` path; the daemon treats `hash` exactly as `off`. Row counts come from the same hashing read (`.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`; csv/tsv without the header; `.parquet` from its footer only when pyarrow is already imported), are cached per machine (new table `h3`) and sent as `rows` on run reads and writes. `probe exec --input PATH --output PATH -- CMD` (repeatable, globs) hashes a shell step's named files when it starts and exits. **Releases up to 0.252.1 (CLI, SDK, daemon and plugin hooks) read `hash` as `off`**, the safe direction. The plugin hooks' `_probe_config.py` and `_session_marker.py` copies change, so they ship with the next plugin release.

- **Hosting a dataset of more than 1,000 files, or one with a file over 64 MiB, and downloading an older dataset version now work against the server.** `run.log_dataset(..., upload=True)` and `probe dataset add --upload` ask the hosting door again until its `deferred` count is 0 (the server answers at most 1,000 files per call, 500 of them over 64 MiB), at most `ceil(files / 500) + 4` calls, with one stderr line per round (`hosting round 2: 1,000 file(s) to send (4.1 GB), 2,000 more after this round`); before, a dataset past one call's worth sent the first 1,000 files and its registration was refused (409 `hosted_incomplete`). Each round now waits for Probe's verifier to hash its files over 64 MiB (up to 1 hour, looking every 5 s) before the next call or the registration, which was otherwise refused the same way, and one door call may take 60 s (was 10 s), since it can open 500 multipart uploads. A confirm the server refuses, such as a stored file larger than the size the door reserved, names the file and the server's reason. The registration names the producing run (`hosted: {manifest_hash, run_id}`): the SDK's run, or `--run`/`--from`, which `dataset add --upload` no longer refuses; from a read-restricted project it then needs `publish=True` / `--publish`, like every other registration. `probe dataset download dataset:<name>@<N>` of an older version of a one-file team dataset downloads it through the files list's `download: {artifact_id, version}` (`POST /v1/artifacts/{id}/versions/{n}/download`) instead of saying it is kept outside Probe; the live version and hosted files still come through the download batch, and a file it refuses says why.
- `probe provenance --steps` prints a step's run name when the server sends it as `label` (servers before the methods-view fix), never the run's ref.

## 0.252.1

- **The daemon's reader never stops to summarize its history; it starts fresh instead.** When a turn's new events would take the reader's kept conversation past its size (120K tokens), the reader used to make a summary call before the turn's first step. On gpt-6.1-sol that call took 140-310 s, inside the turn's 420 s limit, so one failed attempt and a retry cut the turn with nothing read (strand-ai, 2026-10-14: "reader turn stopped: 420 seconds", twice in 15 minutes). That turn now starts the conversation fresh, told what the reader already sent, the same as rule A already did when a turn ended over the size. The reader has no compaction step at all; instead a turn ends once a round's request reaches 180K tokens (or 1,800 messages), so it can never grow into the model route's 260K ceiling and lose its whole turn. A conversation an older CLI compacted starts fresh once. The writer still compacts.
- **Agents can read the data catalog over the hosted MCP, with no new tool.** `browse` lists `datasets` (named team datasets, plus run-logged dataset files nobody registered), `checkpoints` (every checkpoint team-wide, with byte totals) and `sources` (Hub ids, buckets, URLs, with how many runs use each); each mode takes only its own route's filters and refuses the rest, naming the mode that reads them. `entity` opens `dataset:<name>[@<N>]`, `source:<uuid>` or `source:<key>[@<revision>]`, and `checkpoint:<uuid>` or `checkpoint:<run>@best|latest|step<N>`: `card` shows a dataset with one version (a checkpoint with its metrics at the save step), `versions` lists a dataset's versions or a checkpoint's other saves, and `lineage` walks the provenance graph up to the sources (`view_options`: `direction`, `depth` 1-8, or `steps: true` for the ordered methods view). A dataset version that does not exist answers `no_match` with the versions that do. `artifact:<name>` is still the Shared reuse check, and it still sees catalog datasets. Under `X-Probe-Hide-Session-Work` the lineage graph and the methods view leave out the caller's own runs and every edge to them.

## 0.252.0

- Shorter, simpler daemon prompts so notes stay short: `edit-notes` makes every write an in-place, top-down update (what this is, then the latest or most important thing) instead of a new section per event; `track-work` is ~60% shorter and leads every human-facing write with the most recent or most important thing; the writer no longer records every caveat the main agent states, and the main agent's Probe block drops "Say your caveats ... the daemon records what you state" (`POINTER_VERSION` 45).

## 0.251.0

- **Runs launched together to compare settings get an experiment, even when nobody wrote the question down.** track-work's "No question, no experiment" was read literally: one session filed six SFT arms of one base run project-direct, one by one. Note 2 of section 2 now reads: arms, variants and branches of one run answer one question even if nobody wrote it down, so the writer creates the experiment with that question and files them in it; with no such question it still opens a project-direct run. A `run move` that files a branch of a run outside any experiment now adds one fact line when two or more branches of that run sit that way (`N runs branch from <run>; none is in an experiment`), from the writer's own logbook (Richard's approved text). The replay bench tied main on this (writer-filing-a/-b, 100% vs 100%); shipped on Richard's call (10-14).

## 0.250.0

- **A captured session is named the way Claude Code names it (tap 0.9.20).** Claude Code titles a session after its first exchange (the terminal tab, e.g. "Research-os live run titles") and keeps re-appending that title to the transcript as an `ai-title` line, or a `custom-title` line after `/rename`, which wins. The capture tap reads those lines and, after a batch is accepted, sends the newest title to the gateway's new title door (`POST /ingest/v1/sessions/{source}/{session_id}/title`) whenever it changes; credentials in it are redacted first and a leading `[DONE]` or status glyph is dropped. It travels beside the batch, never in it, because the engine's receipts door digests every batch key. `probe import` sends it the same way. Other harnesses send none yet.

## 0.249.3

- **A cursor keeps the arguments of the read that returned it.** Page two of a transcript read sent without its `view_options` (the grep) was refused as a changed request, and the refusal said to repeat the read without cursor, so the agent started the read over. A cursor from `entity`, `search`, `metrics` or `find_papers` now carries the call's optional non-default arguments (up to 160 bytes of them; past that it stays hash-only, as before, so it never costs a page more than ~150 tokens). An argument a continuation leaves out is taken from the cursor; one it changes is refused by name before anything is read ("`view_options` differs"), telling the agent to send the same arguments with the cursor. `token_budget` may still change, `refs` stays required, and cursors already in transcripts still continue. `browse` cursors are unchanged. `query_sql`: a result cut to `token_budget` now says `rows_fetched` (rows the server returned) beside `row_count` (rows kept), and its description says a byte_limit cut means raise `token_budget` (up to 8000), select fewer columns, use DISTINCT, aggregate or filter harder. Ships with the hosted MCP's deploy.

## 0.249.2

- **The daemon can describe a run when it starts.** 0.249.1 told it to, but its command check still refused `probe run set --description` ("a run's description is written by the server once the run finishes"), so on the first live Willow runs it set the name and dropped the description. The check dated from when the daemon's writes locked the server's description out for good; they are `agent` now, so the server still replaces the description when the run finishes. Project descriptions stay the server's.

## 0.249.1

- **Live runs get a readable name and a description when they start.** The `track-work` skill told the daemon's writer "Do not name runs" and "Descriptions are server-written", so a run kept its script's name (`willow-sft-Adecay-real-sol-20261013`) and an empty description until it finished. It now says to set both when a run starts (`probe run set RUN --name --description`), and to add `--authored-by human` when the researcher chose the words. The daemon's own writes now count as `agent`: its `probe` calls carry no coding-agent marker, so every name and description it wrote arrived undeclared and was locked as a person's choice (the experiment it filed that Willow run under is one). Agent-written text is still replaced by the generated title and description when the run ends; human-written text never is.

## 0.249.0

- **The main agent can ask the daemon's writer to change the record, and hears what it did.** `probe ask --writer "<request>"` files a request for the WRITER (file runs, make or regroup an experiment); before, `probe ask` reached only the reader, which cannot write and answered "I cannot", while the writer treated the agent's words as data. A request starts a writer run at once (wherever it sits in the queue, never held by the writer's least gap; at most one such run a minute, a later request goes with the next run), and the run that saw it answers with its own sentence plus what it recorded and did not, taken from its logbook since the first attempt that saw the request (`Recorded: ...` / `Not recorded: ... (failed: <the error>)`): `[Probe] The writer's reply:`. `--wait` prints that reply; without it, Claude Code's Stop wake and pi's poller hand it over like an answer. A request that will not run fails with the reason and what was already written (`[Probe] The writer did not run your request: ...`) and is never run later (a paused writer conversation that saw it ends with it): no run took it in 45 minutes, Probe went read only, inline or off, its run was cut short and skipped or will not finish, or the session ended. A run that recorded structural writes (create, fork, move, set, delete, edge) and had no request sends one receipt of at most 600 characters naming them (`[Probe] The writer recorded: ...`), so the agent learns what the writer filed on its own; none where the agent's hooks read no mailbox. Receipts stay `message`s with `origin: writer`: hooks from before this release show one as an unasked message and never wake for it. A request in a session the ML gate paused as not ML work lifts the pause, for good. The reader can now search the writer's logbook commands (`session` op `logbook`; not its lookups, which hold files the reader may not open), so it can say what the writer filed. Requests live in the mailbox's own `requests/` folder, never `asks/`, so a daemon from before this release never hands one to the reader; `--writer` is refused under `read only (daemon)` and while a daemon from before this release runs (a worker says it takes requests in `requests/<sid>/.worker.json`, written as it takes the session's lock). The companion bench's fake Probe now files a run into an experiment sent as `experiment_id` (every `run move --to <experiment>` was refused as a no-op), and the bench replays the writer channel (`writer-request-a`, `writer-filing-a`; W1-W5, F1-F3). The daemon profile's managed block (pointer 44), the write-refusal text and `probe ask --help` name `--writer`; the writer's and the reader's instructions gain one line each (Richard's approved text).

- **A checkpoint's score lands on its training run, not on a new run.** An agent scoring a training run's checkpoints opened one new run per score, so the scores sat apart from the run they measure. instrument-code gains one line: a score of a training run's checkpoint is a metric on that run at the checkpoint's step (`probe log RUN key=value --step N`), not a new run (Richard's approved text). A live `claude -p` check (claude-sonnet-5-5, a toy run with 3 checkpoints): 3/3 logged on the training run with `--step` vs 0/3 before (each opened a new run).

## 0.248.0

- **Agents hear about their runs' alerts.** In the daemon profile, when a run the session launched or wrote to crashes, is still running with a flagged metric, or was flagged and then stopped, the agent gets a `[Probe] Run alert` message naming the run and what happened: the same alerts, and the same gates, as the alert email. The daemon asks Probe every 30 seconds (in `on` and `read only`), sends each alert once, and puts a batch in one message (ten runs listed, then "and N more runs."). An idle Claude Code or pi session wakes for it; Codex and Kimi get it at their next prompt or tool call. An undelivered alert waits 12 hours. Claude Code's Stop hook now also waits while the daemon serves the session, for up to 7 days, and stops at the next prompt or once the session's daemon is gone. Until the server serves the alerts, the daemon finds nothing and stays quiet.

## 0.247.3

- **The Capy install can open Capy on the plugin's Add box.** On a Mac with the Capy app and the hosted Probe (not over SSH), the installer's last page offers **Open Capy >**, which opens `capy://app/settings/mcp?github=…` (the plugin URL percent-encoded; Capy ignores a raw one) so the step is Continue, Only me, Add plugin, Connect. It opens only when chosen, after the step is on screen: Capy's box defaults to Organization, which signs every teammate in as you. Windows is left out until its deep links are checked. The plugin manifest no longer sets `connection: member`, which Capy ignores.

## 0.247.2

- **The daemon's writer no longer misses the first [Probe] message after the reader's mailbox is swept.** The claim log is deleted after a week idle and made again by the next claim; the new file often gets the old inode number back, so the writer read it from the old cursor and skipped its first message(s). It now compares the bytes just before its cursor, as it does for the chat log, and reads a new log from the start.

- **Kimi Code can ask Probe's questions again.** Plugin 0.142.1's answer hook allowed only Claude Code's spelling of a question's fields (`multiSelect`), so every Probe question put through Kimi's question tool (`multi_select`) was refused. Both spellings pass now.

## 0.247.1

- **Only the researcher answers a Probe question, and only as asked.** A shell that carries a coding agent's session (a pseudo-terminal included) lists `probe approvals` but answers nothing; the answer hook refuses a question whose options carry any description but their own label; `PROBE_DAEMON_SESSION` in an agent's own shell no longer makes its feedback read as the daemon's; and a yes that a daemon from before 0.247.0 voided is still sent. The note-audit hook now finds `probe` the way the other hooks do (`PROBE_BIN` first).

## 0.247.0

- **Agents can send the Probe team feedback about Probe, with the researcher's yes.** `probe feedback send "<text>"` (at most 1,000 characters) is open to every coding agent, the daemon's writer, and the daemon's reader through a new `feedback` tool. Nothing is sent until the researcher says yes. The text becomes a question on the approvals board (policy `feedback.send`): Claude Code and Kimi ask it with their question tool, pi in its own dialog, and on Codex the researcher answers with `probe approvals`. It is asked in every permission mode, bypass included (the one exception to "bypass means bypass"), and is refused under `off` and where there is no session to ask in (Capy). The question shows the whole text, after credentials are redacted, and says what else is sent: the researcher's name and team, the coding agent, the CLI version and the session id. One feedback question waits per session at a time. Hidden characters (control codes, bidi overrides) are removed first, so a terminal or dialog cannot hide part of it. A yes starts `probe feedback flush`, which sends it with the researcher's own credential for the account it was asked under (`POST /v1/feedback`, keyed so it lands once); a send that fails for now (offline, a server without the route yet) stays unsent, and session start runs the flush again when a yes is unsent, pi included. The daemon leaves these questions alone and keeps their text out of its writer's prompt. The dashboard assistant's direct send is accepted only from its own turn credential. Both CLAUDE.md blocks (pointer 43), the writer's and the reader's instructions gain one FEEDBACK line.

## 0.246.3

- **Capy setup is one step.** The installer's last page, `probe capy setup` and `probe wizard --action manual` now say: in Capy, Settings > MCP & plugins > Add > From GitHub repository, paste `https://github.com/prbe-ai/research-os-agent/tree/main/capy`, choose Only me, Add plugin, then Connect. The plugin carries Probe's MCP server and the skills, so the separate MCP server, `npx skills add` and AGENTS.md steps are gone (Capy shows every skill's description to the agent). Its server now asks Capy for one sign-in per member (`connection: member`), and its bundle ships `audit-team-note` instead of the `notes-audit` stub. A self-hosted Probe, whose MCP server is not the plugin's, still gets the server and skills steps.

## 0.246.2

- **An auto-update no longer reports Probe removed from a machine.** Update runs once for each coding agent on the machine, and the server keeps one record per machine. Each pass used to send only its own agent's capabilities, so on a machine with Session capture in one agent and not another, every update reported capture `absent` and then `installed` a few seconds later. Each `absent` posted a false "Probe removed from a machine" to #probe-usage: all 3 of one customer's removal pings from 2026-10-02 to 10-13, and 37 of 444 across all machines in 30 days. Update and Settings now send one report after the last agent. Install's final report works the same way. A capability counts as installed when any agent in the run has it, and only each agent's latest state counts. An agent whose step did not finish can make a field `unknown`, never `absent`. An Update that stops with an error sends nothing, so the record keeps its last state. A run that names one agent (`--agent codex`) still reports that agent alone.

## 0.246.1

- **The mirror's `capy/` folder carries a Capy plugin manifest.** `plugin.json` (also at `.codex-plugin/` and `.claude-plugin/`) and `.mcp.json` declare Probe's MCP server (key `probe`) and the folder's skills, with probe-research's version, generated by `tools/mirror_render.py`. Capy has not published its plugin format, so the installer still prints the in-Capy steps until a real Capy accepts the folder.
- **The agent's own writes move the status-line project too.** In inline mode, for a `--directed` write under the daemon, and in any session the daemon does not record, a `probe` command that lands and names a project or experiment (the same commands as the daemon's, plus `run start`, `sync DIR` and `exec` with `--project`/`--experiment`; `exec` as soon as its run opens, not when the job ends) now stores that project for the status line, through the CLI's own client and credential; deleting the labelled project clears it. Same rules as the daemon's: only with the status line or notice installed, never for a failed or queued write, `--help`, a bare `tag` listing or `sync --list`, at most 5 s. Before, only the daemon's writes moved the label, so it stayed on the daemon's last project while the agent wrote elsewhere.

## 0.246.0

- **`visualize-progress` in the daemon profile.** The STATUS block and ASCII research timeline now work when the Probe daemon records: the lean plugin (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi) and pi's daemon profile ship a daemon copy of the skill that gets its facts from one `probe ask --wait` and `probe session status`, since the agent there cannot read Probe itself. The drawing is the same doctrine, held to the canonical skill by `tests/test_visualize_progress_daemon.py`; a run's captured inputs, which no read reaches in this profile, draw as `?`, and the local upload queue is left out.
- **The daemon's writer ends a run in the same model response as its last writes.** pydantic-ai already runs the commands that come before `final_result` in one response, but nothing told the writer it could, so every run paid one more model round, re-reading the whole conversation, only to end (about 30% of writer spend on strand-ai, 2026-10-12). `record_session.md` now says so. A write in that ending response that did not land (a nonzero exit, a pre-check block, a refusal, a write skipped after `&&` because the part before it failed, a tool that raised; not a question to the researcher or a lost lease) cancels the end, and the writer is shown what the command answered. On the tool's last retry the end goes through, and the next run's open-failures list still carries the write.
- **`edit-notes` names `probe notes append` and `probe notes edit` for adding or changing one paragraph.** Each is one command that reads the note on the server. Checkout and push stay for restructuring a note. This applies to the main agent, the daemon, Codex and pi.
- **The daemon's reader can skip a look that would find nothing.** Before a reader turn nobody asked for, a cheap model (the server's `gate` alias, Claude Haiku 5.5 by default, on its own lane, 20 seconds at most) reads the reader's own job description and the next window of unread events, the same window the reader would read, and says whether the reader should look. The server sets the mode on every answer (`x-probe-reader-gate`: `off`, `shadow` or `on`, overridable with `PROBE_DAEMON_READER_GATE`):
  - In `shadow` the reader looks anyway, and the verdict goes on the turn's trace.
  - In `on` a skip closes the wake as a `skipped` turn that costs only the gate's call. The reader's cursor does not move, so its next turn, or an ask, still reads the skipped events (up to one turn's window).
  - An ask never goes through the gate. A gate error, refusal or timeout counts as a look.
- **A conversation over the model route's ceiling starts fresh at once.** The route now refuses a daemon prompt it estimates over its ceiling (`prompt_too_large`, 260K tokens by default) before sending it, so the provider's double price above 272K is never paid. The writer ends its conversation and runs the same bite again at once, fresh from disk, with no failure counted and no ping. A fresh bite over it is cut short like any other. The reader starts fresh on the same events, without counting a failure. When a conversation ends because the route refused its history or its size, or its fingerprint or saved history no longer serves, a paused run waiting to carry on gets its events back on the queue (they were covered when it paused): the newest paused run's only, in the same transaction. The reader closes such a turn as `over the ceiling: fresh`, not `failed`, and a fresh writer retry does not wait for the writer's gap.
- **The writer can wait between runs.** The server sets the least gap between two writer runs (`x-probe-writer-min-gap-s`, overridable with `PROBE_DAEMON_WRITER_GAP_S`; 0, the default, keeps today's timing). Only a run whose reasons are the agent's turn end or the queue's age waits for it. A prompt, a full queue, the session ending or a paused run still starts at once. Each writer run's trace now says whether the gap could have held it back (`deferrable`).

## 0.245.2

- **`plan-research-review` logs every run to Probe.** A project already on W&B (or TensorBoard, MLflow) used to keep it, read as code to reuse; the plan and its implementation contract now replace it with Probe (`instrument-code`), without asking.

## 0.245.1

- **The status line names the project the daemon is writing to.** It used to name the last project of the session's work list, an order that ties for every project of one session and so falls to id order: it could show a project the daemon had stopped writing to, and never moved. Now each daemon write that lands and names a project or experiment (filing a run, a note, an experiment, a paper, an artifact, a project change) stores that project's slug in `~/.local/state/probe/sessions/<session>.scope`, and the segment (and the Codex on-change notice) shows it. An experiment shows its project. A write that names only a run, an artifact or a note by id, a failed or queued write, and a `name:` ref leave the label where it was; the daemon deleting the labelled project clears it. Only sessions with the status line or the notice installed pay the lookup (one or two small reads, 5 s at most per write). Writes the daemon does not make (inline mode, `--directed`) do not move it yet. A project name with control or bidi characters is no longer printed, from either source. Needs this CLI (the daemon) and this plugin (the status line); either alone keeps the old label.

## 0.245.0
- **Capy installs like every other coding agent.** It is in the installer's agent picker (listed when the Capy app is on this computer, or this computer already captures Capy), in `--agent capy`, and in "On this device" as a normal agent row. The separate **Cloud agents** menu entry (`--action cloud-agents`) is gone.
  - **Installing Capy** asks for a Capy API key and the projects to capture after the review screen, before anything is applied, so creating a key never spends the install's 300-second budget. It then connects capture (a sync every 10 minutes, and one right away when no system timer could be installed) and prints the steps for Capy's own settings (MCP server and skills), which no command can do. An empty key skips Capy capture and says how to connect later. Without a terminal it reads `$CAPY_API_KEY` and the new `--capy-project` (repeatable); a missing key or project is reported as unfinished, never a guess.
  - **The install verdict** never counts Capy's MCP as a missing plugin. A key Capy refuses, or a run without one, leaves the install unfinished without failing the other agents beside it.
  - **Update, uninstall, doctor and diagnose** have Capy branches: no plugin update ("its app updates itself"), uninstall disconnects and says to remove Probe in Capy's settings, and doctor and troubleshooting describe Capy instead of Claude Code. Capy has no instruction file, rules step or status line here.
  - `--agent` takes any installable agent's flag, id or alias from the registry; `both` and `all` still mean Claude Code + Codex.
  - Inside a Capy thread on your Mac, Capy's own environment variable now tells the CLI it runs inside Capy (before, only `PROBE_CAPY=1` did).
## 0.244.1

- **A daemon that lost its AI libraries gets them back, and its session gets its daemon back.** A bare `uv tool install --force probe-research` drops the `daemon` extra. Updates used to restate `[all]` alone after that, because they only asked whether the libraries were importable. Updates of a uv or pipx tool install now also keep `daemon` when the daemon records for any coding agent on the machine. A pip install gets them only from `probe daemon install`. The update that installs this release runs the previous release's code, so a stripped install heals on the update after it, or at once with `probe daemon install`. A worker that finds the libraries missing now tells capture plugin 0.9.19 to try again in 5 minutes. Older capture plugins stopped for good until the switch moved. The missing-libraries line reaches `daemon-errors.log` once an hour per session, and a half-installed extra (`pydantic_ai` without `pydantic_ai_harness`) takes that path instead of crashing later. A session already stranded on an older capture plugin still needs `/probe read` then `/probe on` (or a restart) to start its daemon again.
- **Probe stops rebuilding the tool's environment under running processes.** `uv tool install --force` deletes and rebuilds the tool's environment, and with no Python named it rebuilds it on the newest Python uv has (so does a plain install on uv before 0.10): `lib/pythonX.Y` disappeared under a live daemon worker, which crashed hours later reading its own files. `probe daemon install`, the update's fallback for a version-pinned install and the `npx probe-research` reinstall over an existing tool now run a plain `uv tool install`, which upgrades or adds packages in place; `--force` is left for a first install and the old probe-agent takeover. Every reinstall names the exact interpreter the environment runs on (from its `pyvenv.cfg`) when the receipt records none: `--python X.Y` let uv pick its own build of that version over the system one and rebuild just the same. `probe daemon install` checks the result in a fresh interpreter (the new environment's, after a probe-agent takeover), reinstalls only the daemon's packages when the install was a no-op over broken ones, and never reports success while they do not import. It refuses a receipt it cannot restate, as `probe update` does. Updates keep `daemon` because the daemon's own harness imports, no longer because `pydantic_ai` does, so a project environment with its own Pydantic AI is not handed the daemon's stack. The hints that told people to run `uv tool install --force 'probe-research[all]'` no longer force.
- **Capture plugin 0.9.19:** retries a daemon worker that exited for missing AI libraries every 5 minutes, instead of giving up until the switch moves.
- MCP: an experiment card shows `forked_from`, `fork_count` and, on a fork, where to read what it inherits; new `inherited` view (`view_options.runs`) on experiments. SDK models: experiment detail `inherits`.

## 0.244.0
- **Artifact kinds are a fixed list.** `probe artifact add --kind` (and `log_artifact(kind=...)`) takes `checkpoint`, `dataset`, `evaluation`, `code` or `other`. Any other word still works: Probe files it as `other` (a synonym such as `benchmark`, `model` or `script` as its kind) and keeps the word as the file's label, and `artifact add` says so in one line on stderr, e.g. `kind: filed as other (label: report)`. A file logged without a kind is `other`, an image included (it was `plot`); `.ckpt`, `.safetensors`, `.pt` and `.pth` files are still a `checkpoint`. Every word Probe files as code (`test` and `code_bundle` now too) is uploaded, never recorded as a pointer, as `--kind code` always was. Output capture no longer uploads a second copy of a file you already uploaded as code, and `probe run check` counts a note file filed as `other` (label `note`) as the run's notes. `track-work` now says `--kind code`.

## 0.243.2
- **The daemon stops paying again for an answer the model never gave.** When gpt-6.1-sol thinks until its token limit (16,384 by default) and answers nothing, or is cut off mid tool call, the writer used to treat it as a passing failure: it backed off, moved the bite to the back of the queue and sent the same request again. strand-ai's writer did that 41 times in 3.5 hours on 2026-10-12, at about $0.25 each. Now the writer starts fresh from disk with half the events and, if that fails too, skips the range with a notice (an "events skipped" ping, not "Daemon bug"). Each such bite in a row waits longer (30 s doubling, 30 min at most), and after 3 the agent records until a model round answers again. A continued run that answers nothing is dropped with a notice, not silently. The reader used to read the error as stray prose and keep its history, so the next wake thought to the limit again (one request was sent 14 times). Now the same events and question go once more on a fresh conversation, without counting as a reader failure; a second time they are passed over as a stopped turn, and newer events still get their own try.
- **A CLI reinstalled under a running daemon restarts it instead of crashing it.** `uv tool` replaces the CLI under running workers: a new Python moves its folder (`lib/python3.13` to `lib/python3.14`), and `probe update` rewrites its files in place. A worker started before that failed at its next read of its own files ("Daemon crashed", FileNotFoundError on `record_session.md`) or ran old code against new files. It now notices either at its next poll, between two model rounds, or when a run fails on it, and exits 0; capture starts the new install at once, with no crash backoff and no ping.

## 0.243.1
- **The reader's messages land where the agent got them, once.** A message the daemon's reader hands the main agent waits (10 s at most) until the chat line it came with is read, so one delivered with a new prompt lands after that prompt, in its turn, not at the end of the previous one. The transcript's own copy of the reader's messages (Claude Code's hook context and Stop-hook wake, Kimi's `<hook_result>`) is no longer read beside the whole message from the claim log; `[Probe]` text in a wording this CLI does not know still is.

## 0.243.0

- `probe experiment fork SOURCE NEW --question "..."` (SDK `fork_experiment`) makes a new experiment in SOURCE's project that copies its notes, sub-notes, page document, tags, chart settings and its own files (nothing re-uploaded), links it `forked_from` SOURCE, and reads SOURCE's runs and their files live until one changes on SOURCE's side, when the fork keeps its own copy. `probe experiment inherited NEW [--runs]` (SDK `experiment_inherited`) lists what a fork reads from its source. The daemon owns `experiment fork` and may retry it safely; `experiment inherited` is a read.
- `track-work` (main agent and daemon): a new experiment that starts from another's notes and files is made with `probe experiment fork SOURCE NEW --question "..."` instead of `experiment create` + `edge add`; the fork's own link comes only from that command.

## 0.242.0
- **The daemon's writer sees what the reader handed the main agent, whole.** It used to see only the transcript's copy of a `[Probe]` message: a 300-character harness preview on Claude Code and Kimi (every one measured on a devbox was longer; a `probe ask` answer averaged 4,267 characters), none of an answer the Stop hook woke the agent with, an output tag for a `probe ask --wait` answer, and nothing at all on Codex and pi. The worker now reads the mailbox's claim log (`claimed/<sid>/log.jsonl`, which every deliverer appends) as a `reader` stream: one event per message the daemon itself recorded (a message file nobody recorded is never shown as the reader's), as the agent read it, shown as `[Probe message to the main agent · <id>]` up to 20,000 characters, to the writer and in the reader's own view; its own messages never wake the reader. Claims wait until the chat log is read up to them, follow `.probe.config`, and a session already under way when the CLI updates starts from the log's end. Daemon stores gain a `source` column and the `events_sizes_source` index; earlier CLIs still open them.

## 0.241.0

- Capy has full support in the CLI, the wizard and the capture plugin.
  - **Wizard:** `probe wizard` has a **Cloud agents → Capy** entry. It shows the in-Capy setup steps, connects capture (the key is typed hidden and projects are picked from a list), syncs now and disconnects. A Capy line under "On this device" shows the last sync, or a refused key, with Capy's logo. `--action cloud-agents` prints the steps.
  - **Sign-out (in the wizard) and uninstall** now disconnect Capy: the timer, a sync already running, the key, the sync record and the capture credential. Before, Capy threads kept uploading after them. Capture is also pinned to the Probe server it was connected to: a shell pointing Probe elsewhere syncs nothing.
  - **Inside Capy** (`PROBE_CAPY=1`): `probe doctor` reports Capy's own checks instead of Claude Code's, and `probe session` / `probe ask` say why they cannot run and point to MCP search.
  - **Pairing messages** name Capy, not "coding agent".
  - **Capture plugin 0.9.18:** when a local agent starts a session, it starts a background `probe capy sync` if the last sync is more than 5 minutes old.
  - The MCP `entity` tool lists every captured agent for `session:<agent>/<id>`, Kimi Code included.

## 0.240.0

- **Daemon-mode agents search research papers themselves: `probe paper find`.** A new read command over the same delivery path as the Probe MCP's `find_papers` tool (same answer envelope and `--token-budget`): `search` ranks 40M+ abstracts by a sentence, `--mode read --paper-id arxiv:<id> --query ...` returns one paper's passages, `--mode similar` walks citers and references. It adds nothing to the team's records (the query reaches Probe's usage analytics, as the MCP tool's does) and spends one of the team's weekly web calls; `--cursor` pages within 30 minutes read the first answer instead of searching again. The daemon profile's guard admits it (the one read it leaves to the agent; `paper find` is classified a read in every state, pi included, and the daemon's team-note audit refuses it as it refuses `find_papers`), the daemon block gains a `### PAPERS:` section (pointer v42), and `plan-research-review` names it for related papers. A new plugin hook (`papers_hook.py`, `WebSearch` only, daemon profile only) holds a web search that looks like a paper search at most once per 15 minutes, and never after `probe paper find` ran in the last 15, naming the command; it never holds under `off` or beside a CLI without the command (it asks `probe paper find --help`, and keeps a definite answer for the session). Codex and pi have no hook point for their web search and get the block line only.

## 0.239.0

- **The Hugging Face and Lightning integrations can store checkpoints, and a run's best or latest one comes back with one command.** `ProbeCallback(checkpoints="upload")` (new; with `report_to="probe"`, set `PROBE_CHECKPOINTS=upload`) and `ProbeLogger(checkpoints="upload")` (now folders too: a sharded DeepSpeed/FSDP checkpoint was recorded as a location even in upload mode) upload each save as its own set, `<name>@step<N>`: every file of the checkpoint is a `file` row under it, and one `checkpoint` index row lists them in `meta.members`. Only the index is a `checkpoint`, so the failed-run alert and the disk finding still name and size the whole checkpoint, and only it is refreshed when `best`, `last` or `deleted` change (before, an uploaded Lightning row kept the `best` it was saved with). A file saved again in place (`last.ckpt`) starts a new set and marks the earlier one superseded, so a download never mixes two saves. A set is all of a checkpoint or none of it: one holding a link or an unreadable file, more than 1,000 files, or more than 2 GB that would be copied across disks on the training thread to stage it (set `PROBE_OUTBOX_DIR` on the checkpoint's disk) is recorded as a location only, with a warning; files a `.probe.config` excludes are neither uploaded nor named. Member uploads are never strict, so a strict callback never uploads gigabytes on the training thread. The default is unchanged: the location only, now with one warning when that location is the job's own throwaway disk. `probe artifact download --run <run> --checkpoint latest|best -o DIR` (or the index row's id) writes every stored file into `DIR` (a new or empty folder, a mounted volume included: the files land in a private folder inside it and move into place once all match their sha256, so a failed restore leaves the folder as it was and never mixes into another checkpoint; it says when files were excluded by `.probe.config` or stored with a credential masked), and refuses, naming the files, when any was not stored; the SDK has `client.checkpoint(run_id, "best")` and `client.download_checkpoint(row, dir)`. `latest` is the newest save whose files are all stored (a save still uploading, or whose upload was abandoned or lost with a preempted job, is passed over), `best` is the row the trainer marked, never a guess; two Lightning callbacks with a best each need `--callback`. `instrument-code` says how.

## 0.238.0
